1H.Cn-G.title: witness-scoped recoverability without validity inheritance
1H.Cn-G.boundary: preserved derivational paths can become searchable provenance-bearing knowledge objects; inverse retrieval can recover multiple paths around a concept; endpoint consensus is a scalable filter, not formal proof of every intermediate step or synthesized claim.

edges.title: PROVENANCE BECOMES PART OF VALIDITY UNDER ADAPTIVE REFERENCE CONSTRUCTION
edges.text:
w makes derivational/source provenance persist as an addressable object; x shows a concrete inferential case in which how the reference mechanism was learned changes the guarantee class. Together they derive that provenance is not merely explanatory metadata when the same history participates in both construction and judgment: the construction route itself can be part of the validity warrant.
Removal witness: remove w and there is no durable retrievable path/provenance object to carry; remove x and there is no demonstrated case in which same-history construction changes the admissible guarantee.

edges.title: RECOVERABILITY IS NOT VALIDITY
edges.text:
w separates preserved reasoning paths from certification of every intermediate claim; z separates exact representational recovery from semantic truth and from guarantee-free inversion under arbitrary interfaces. Together they derive a reusable distinction: successfully preserving or reconstructing an informational object proves availability/identity of that object under the stated interface, not the correctness or authority of the claims carried by it.
Removal witness: remove w and the result is only representational inversion; remove z and the result is only epistemic provenance filtering without a constructive recoverability distinction.

edges.title: RETRIEVABLE PROVENANCE SHOULD CARRY THE ASSUMPTION SLICE THAT MADE THE PATH LAWFUL
edges.text:
w makes derivational pathways and validation state directly retrievable; y shows that target law, encountered distribution, task relevance and scale can diverge while superficially sharing one symmetry label. Together they derive that reusable reasoning provenance should preserve the regime-specific assumptions under which its operations were meaningful, not only the endpoint or task name.
Removal witness: remove w and there is no retrievable path object on which to preserve assumption provenance; remove y and there is no earned separation among target, distribution, task and scale obligations.

edges.title: AN INVERSE DOES NOT RESTORE AN EXPIRED VALIDITY WITNESS
edges.text:
z supplies the strongest form of informational return available here—unique encoding plus constructive recovery under an exposed interface. x supplies the counter-pressure: even perfect access to the data/reference object does not reinstate an exact guarantee once its construction provenance has changed; a new calibration witness is required. Thus reconstruction of state and restoration of validity are different operations.
Removal witness: remove x and there is no guarantee-class transition requiring revalidation; remove z and there is no earned exact-recovery case against which to separate validity restoration.

edges.title: VALIDITY IS TYPED BY THE CURRENT DATA/REFERENCE REGIME
edges.text:
x binds inferential validity to reference-law provenance, two-nuisance interaction and asymptotic conditions; y binds symmetry-aware intervention to actual distribution, task relevance, scale and model regime. Together they derive a broader governance rule: reuse of a statistical/structural constraint must remain indexed to the current regime that licenses it rather than being carried forward by label alone.
Removal witness: remove x and the reference/calibration axis disappears; remove y and the target-versus-distribution/task/scale axis disappears.


zy — INFORMATION PRESERVATION AND DECISION ALIGNMENT ARE INDEPENDENT
z shows that a representation can remain injective and even exactly recoverable while becoming geometrically compressed; y shows that an exact invariance constraint can still suppress non-invariant information that is predictive under the encountered task/distribution. Together they derive that “the information is still there” and “the imposed decision constraint uses the right information” are separate questions.
Removal witness: remove z and no preserved-information counterexample remains; remove y and no task/distribution-dependent constraint-alignment problem remains.


4 FACES
wxy — ASSUMPTION-BEARING PROVENANCE FOR ADAPTIVE REUSE
Together, w + x + y derive that a retrievable reasoning object used again under an adaptive or shifted setting must carry more than its endpoint: it must retain the construction/reference provenance that determines guarantee class and the target/distribution/task assumptions that determine whether the same constraint is still appropriate.
Removal witnesses:
- remove w → there is no durable reasoning/path object on which the warrant can travel;
- remove x → adaptive same-history construction no longer has an earned validity consequence;
- remove y → target, distribution, task and scale collapse back into an undifferentiated assumption label.


wxz — RECONSTRUCTIBLE HISTORY IS NOT A SELF-AUTHENTICATING CERTIFICATE
Together, w + x + z derive that even exact reconstruction of a stored derivation or state cannot self-certify the validity of the process that produced or now reuses it. The path may be perfectly recoverable, while the reference-law warrant has changed and the reasoning chain itself remains only boundedly verified.
Removal witnesses:
- remove w → the reconstructible object loses its derivational/epistemic provenance;
- remove x → no changed validity warrant must be re-earned;
- remove z → no exact-reconstruction distinction remains.


wyz — EXACT RETURN MUST PRESERVE BOTH EPISTEMIC AND TASK/DISTRIBUTION SCOPE
Together, w + y + z derive that a losslessly recoverable representation or derivation becomes meaningfully reusable only when its provenance and assumption scope return with it. Exact byte/state/path identity cannot tell whether the current task/distribution/scale still supports the same inductive or epistemic interpretation.
Removal witnesses:
- remove w → no provenance-bearing derivation layer;
- remove y → no current task/distribution/scale obligation;
- remove z → no earned exact-return/recoverability pressure.


xyz — RECOVERED INFORMATION BECOMES OPERABLE ONLY THROUGH A CURRENT LOCAL REGIME WITNESS
Together, x + z + y derive a three-gate operational rule: the object must be recoverable through a specified interface/margin regime; the inferential/reference mechanism must satisfy its current calibration conditions; and any structural invariance must fit the actual target/distribution/task scale. Passing one gate does not imply the others.
Removal witnesses:
- remove x → current calibration/reference-law validity is ungoverned;
- remove z → there is no explicit recoverability/interface gate;
- remove y → current distribution/task/constraint scope is ungoverned.


1 VOLUME

1H.DUwl.title: revalidatable operational continuity
1H.DUwl.boundary:
This child is a cross-source relational synthesis, not evidence that the four source domains share one mechanism.
S.IIcl contributes a formal/constructive language claim about operation-preserving translation and executable tensor programs.
S.fGb4 contributes benchmark-bounded empirical evidence about compact video-history carriers, query coverage, downstream repurposing, anisotropic information loss, and modular memory extensions; its separately referenced supplement remains outside the chosen carrier.
S.fOgn contributes empirical held-out intracranial neural-encoding evidence from four clinical participants and preserves the explicit boundary that predictive coordinate alignment does not establish code, mechanism, architecture, or causal-pathway identity; separate supplementary material remains outside the chosen carrier.
S.CTLJ contributes a conceptual/literature-grounded design argument about autonomy, multiscale coordination, continuous rebuilding, embodiment, signaling, and cognitive-light-cone expansion; it does not experimentally establish necessity, sufficiency, AGI, or consciousness.
All claims below remain bounded by those source evidence classes.

edges.title: operation-bounded compression
edges.text:
Holding S.IIcl with S.fGb4 yields a criterion stronger than either alone: a compact carrier is useful for continuity when its reduction preserves or can re-expose the task-relevant operations that later computation actually needs, while its scarce capacity remains repurposable as the task changes. S.IIcl supplies the operation-preserving translation criterion; S.fGb4 supplies empirical finite-capacity compression, unpredictable-access training, downstream adaptation, and ablations showing selective loss.
Removal test: without S.IIcl, compression lacks an explicit cross-representation criterion for what operational structure must survive; without S.fGb4, the relation lacks a concrete bounded-memory regime demonstrating that broad access and later repurposing compete for selective capacity.

edges.title: correspondence without identity
edges.text:
Holding S.IIcl with S.fOgn yields an explicit distinction between useful representational correspondence and ontological identity. A mapping can preserve enough operations or predictive geometry to support cross-representation work even when the systems being related have different mechanisms, architectures, or internal codes. S.IIcl supplies constructive operation-preserving translation; S.fOgn supplies held-out empirical alignment plus an explicit alternative in which a learned map relates distinct biological and model codes.
Removal test: without S.IIcl there is no formal account of how translation can remain computationally substantive; without S.fOgn there is no empirical cross-system case forcing the non-identity boundary to remain live.

edges.title: reconstructible operational contract
edges.text:
Holding S.IIcl with S.CTLJ yields a carrier-independent continuity principle: if the operations and relations that define current competence are explicit enough to be re-instantiated, the implementation carrying them may be rebuilt without treating bytewise or architectural sameness as identity. S.IIcl supplies the addressable operational program/translation structure; S.CTLJ supplies continual reconstruction, self-maintained goals, and multiscale coordination as the system-level reason to permit implementation turnover.
Removal test: without S.IIcl the reconstruction criterion lacks an explicit operational interface; without S.CTLJ the relation lacks the system-level developmental claim that continuing competence may require rebuilding its own carrier.

edges.title: downstream-warranted latent sufficiency
edges.text:
Holding S.fGb4 with S.fOgn yields a shared empirical lesson across unrelated domains: a reduced or learned latent representation should be judged by held-out downstream usefulness under its stated task and evidence regime, not by exhaustive recovery of source detail or by assuming that predictive similarity identifies the generating mechanism. TinyHistory tests future-generation continuity under compression; the neural study tests held-out biological predictivity while retaining a code/mechanism gap.
Removal test: without S.fGb4 there is no finite-memory repurposing/compression stress surface; without S.fOgn there is no independent ecological predictive case that makes non-identity an explicit part of the warrant.

edges.title: goal-conditioned repurposing
edges.text:
Holding S.fGb4 with S.CTLJ yields a developmental relation: a memory/carrier may remain continuous by changing what it allocates capacity to, provided repurposing is governed by the goals and constraints that define current competent behavior rather than by preservation of every prior feature. TinyHistory supplies the freeze-versus-adapt evidence and selective bottleneck; S.CTLJ supplies the conceptual account of protected goals, reconstructive identity, and changing problem horizons.
Removal test: without S.fGb4 the relation lacks empirical evidence that a broadly useful pretrained carrier must be reshaped for downstream continuity; without S.CTLJ the reshaping lacks a system-level continuity criterion beyond the local training objective.

edges.title: action-usable coordinates with an ontology boundary
edges.text:
Holding S.fOgn with S.CTLJ yields a bounded account of internal models/coordinates: a coarse learned representation can be useful for prediction and potentially action without being a veridical copy or the same mechanism as the system it predicts. S.fOgn shows a concrete predictive coordinate relation that survives held-out natural data while leaving mechanism identity unsettled; S.CTLJ argues that action-guiding models need only be sufficiently informative for maintained goals and may remain coarse-grained.
Removal test: without S.fOgn the claim lacks a concrete cross-system predictive witness and explicit ontology fork; without S.CTLJ it lacks the goal-directed reason that a non-identical coordinate system can still be functionally sufficient.

faces.title: task-warranted operational representation
faces.text: S.IIcl + S.fGb4 + S.fOgn jointly earn a stronger notion of representational sufficiency: the relevant carrier must preserve executable/task-relevant relations across representation change, survive finite-capacity selection and downstream repurposing, and be validated against held-out behavior while its map is not promoted into mechanism identity. Remove S.IIcl and “sufficiency” loses the operation-preserving translation criterion; remove S.fGb4 and it loses the concrete compression/repurposing stress; remove S.fOgn and it loses independent held-out cross-system validation plus the explicit non-identity boundary.

faces.title: reconstructible operational memory
faces.text: S.IIcl + S.fGb4 + S.CTLJ jointly earn a memory/competence carrier that can change its implementation while remaining continuous: an explicit operational interface states what must remain executable, a compact carrier demonstrates that scarce representational capacity can be repurposed rather than frozen, and a reconstructive goal-directed system supplies the continuity criterion for when such reorganization is still the same competence. Remove S.IIcl and there is no explicit operational contract; remove S.fGb4 and there is no bounded empirical repurposing witness; remove S.CTLJ and there is no system-level reconstruction/goal continuity condition.

faces.title: non-identical coordinate governance
faces.text: S.IIcl + S.fOgn + S.CTLJ jointly earn a way to coordinate across heterogeneous representations without collapsing them ontologically: relations may be translated into an operation-preserving public interface, predictive coordinate maps may remain useful while internal mechanisms differ, and higher-level goals/constraints may govern which relations must remain available as implementation changes. Remove S.IIcl and the public relation lacks a constructive translation criterion; remove S.fOgn and the non-identity boundary loses its empirical cross-system witness; remove S.CTLJ and the relation loses the goal/constraint layer that governs reconstruction and multiscale use.

faces.title: revalidatable sufficiency under drift
faces.text: S.fGb4 + S.fOgn + S.CTLJ jointly earn a dynamic criterion for “enough representation”: the carrier may be compressed and repurposed, but sufficiency must be re-tested on held-out downstream behavior and reconsidered when the task, goal, or problem horizon changes; predictive usefulness never by itself proves mechanism identity. Remove S.fGb4 and the criterion loses finite-capacity repurposing and selective information-loss evidence; remove S.fOgn and it loses independent held-out ecological validation plus the ontology boundary; remove S.CTLJ and it loses the explicit system-level reason that the validation regime itself may have to change as competence expands.

volume.title: revalidatable operational continuity
volume.text:
All four parents together earn the following bounded closure:


A changing system can preserve task-relevant continuity without preserving a fixed implementation or exhaustive archive when it carries a compact, explicitly operational interface whose transformations preserve the relations needed for current computation; keeps that carrier repurposable under finite capacity as downstream demands change; revalidates adequacy against held-out behavior while preserving the distinction between useful correspondence and mechanism identity; and lets maintained goals, constraints, and an expanding problem horizon determine when the interface or its realization must be reconstructed again. Continuity is therefore warranted by re-executable relation plus renewed evidence, not by material sameness, total retention, or representational resemblance alone.


Full-rank removal tests:
- Remove S.IIcl: the volume loses the explicit operation-preserving translation/executability criterion and falls back to task-specific predictive usefulness.
- Remove S.fGb4: the volume loses direct evidence that finite-capacity carriers require selective access pressure, downstream repurposing, and trade-offs in what survives.
- Remove S.fOgn: the volume loses independent held-out cross-system validation and the explicit proof barrier between predictive correspondence and mechanism/code identity.
- Remove S.CTLJ: the volume loses the system-level goal, reconstruction, and expanding-horizon condition that explains when a once-sufficient carrier must be rebuilt or revalidated.


Bounded volume invariant:
Continuity through changing realization is earned when a compact operational relation can be regenerated for the current task, its adequacy is externally revalidated under the current evidence regime, and the conditions that trigger repurposing or reconstruction travel with the relation; neither implementation sameness nor representational correspondence alone is sufficient.

CREATE: establish a broadly usable carrier and the goal/competence obligations it must support.
COPY: retain the carrier's addressability while allowing its internal allocation to change.

CREATE: express the minimal operational interface and current evidence regime that define competent continuity.
COPY: regenerate that interface across representation or implementation changes.
CONTROL: re-test it on held-out behavior, maintain the correspondence≠identity boundary, and invalidate the warrant when conditions move outside its tested regime.
CULTIVATE: rebuild the carrier and its validation surface as goals, tasks, or problem horizons expand.

edges.title: Invariance is a lossy quotient whose erased distinctions must be justified
edges.text:
S.u1gk supplies the demonstrated consequence that a correct target symmetry can coexist with predictive distributional asymmetry that a hard symmetry-aware learner discards. S.exnj supplies the formal semantics that invariance/sameness is created by declaring a transformation quotient and that broader nuisance groups deliberately erase more distinctions. Together they earn a stricter relation: an invariance declaration is not neutral compression; it is a quotient that removes information, and its legitimacy depends on whether the removed degrees are actually nuisance for the stated obligation.
Removal test: without S.u1gk, quotienting lacks evidence that erased non-invariant structure can change downstream risk; without S.exnj, there is no explicit equivalence/quotient contract defining what is being erased.
Boundary: neither parent establishes one universally correct quotient or a universal preference for less invariance.

edges.title: Symmetry scope is locally conditional rather than one dataset-wide policy
edges.text:
S.u1gk shows that global distributional symmetry breaking does not determine whether equivariance helps and that task relevance/locality/regime matter. S.qogS supplies a constructive input-dependent symmetry field in which different examples can inhabit different transformation supports. Together they earn that the scope of a symmetry constraint may need to be conditioned on local/task context rather than inferred from one global statistic or one target-level group statement.
Removal test: without S.u1gk there is no downstream governance consequence of mismatched symmetry scope; without S.qogS there is no explicit local/input-conditioned symmetry object.
Boundary: the local estimator is assumption-bounded and is not itself an architecture-routing oracle.

edges.title: Preserve independently meaningful factors before deciding what may be quotiented away
edges.text:
S.u1gk shows that an apparently non-invariant degree can remain predictive under the encountered distribution and that hard invariance may remove it. S.6arU shows that two necessary factors can remain independently addressable until their deliberate conjunction, avoiding cross-talk without forbidding interaction. Together they earn a protective rule: before treating variation as nuisance, keep independently meaningful factors separately addressable long enough to test whether each affects the task; quotient only after the intended irrelevance has survived a discriminating intervention.
Removal test: without S.u1gk there is no evidence that discarded asymmetry may be task-useful; without S.6arU there is no constructive independent-addressability-before-conjunction discipline.
Boundary: independent addressability is a diagnostic/architectural strategy, not proof that all factors should remain permanently separate.

edges.title: More flexible equivalence requires more evidence about where equivalence actually holds
edges.text:
S.exnj shows that broader transformation quotients create a finite-sample estimation burden and can erase claim-relevant structure. S.qogS shows that the transformation support itself may vary locally and that local estimates pass through an approximation membrane whose quality depends on neighborhood density, representation and family assumptions. Together they earn an evidence-budget law: increasing invariance flexibility or making equivalence context-sensitive increases the burden of establishing which transformations are genuinely admissible at each relevant locus.
Removal test: without S.exnj there is no controlled quotient-flexibility/estimation-cost relation; without S.qogS there is no local identifiability/approximation burden.
Boundary: this is not a universal sample-complexity theorem.

edges.title: Quotient nuisance coordinates without quotienting away the task’s independent roles
edges.text:
S.exnj supplies architecture/claim-aware quotienting: admissible transformations must preserve the structure named by the comparison claim. S.6arU supplies a concrete case where content and position remain separate semantic roles until attention deliberately combines them. Together they earn that a valid invariance should erase coordinate realization while preserving the role axes the downstream operation must still query independently.
Removal test: without S.exnj there is no explicit nuisance-group/equivalence semantics; without S.6arU there is no independent-role witness showing how a shared operation can combine factors without collapsing their meanings.
Boundary: the correct preserved axes are obligation-specific and must be earned rather than named by analogy.

edges.title: Local transformation support can vary while coordinate roles remain stable
edges.text:
S.qogS supplies input-conditioned symmetry support that can change across examples or regimes. S.6arU supplies stable coordinate semantics whose meaning remains fixed while content and range change. Together they earn a compatibility condition for context-sensitive invariance: the set of transformations treated as locally admissible may vary, but the semantic roles used to state and query that variation must remain stable enough that changing support is not confused with changing meaning.
Removal test: without S.qogS there is no local variation in admissible symmetry support; without S.6arU there is no explicit stable-role/address semantics under changing regime.
Boundary: local support and coordinate roles are distinct objects; this does not imply one common mathematical mechanism across the two sources.

faces.title: Locally warranted equivalence requires task consequence, quotient semantics and local scope
faces.text:
S.u1gk contributes the downstream consequence of discarding task-relevant asymmetry; S.exnj contributes explicit quotient-relative sameness and the cost of broad invariance; S.qogS contributes a locally varying symmetry field and its identification boundary. Together they earn that a transformation may count as nuisance only under a locally warranted equivalence contract: the quotient must be declared, its erased distinctions must be irrelevant to the current task obligation, and the local support on which that claim is made must be sufficiently identified.
Removal tests: remove S.u1gk and irrelevance has no demonstrated task consequence; remove S.exnj and the equivalence relation itself is undefined; remove S.qogS and the scope collapses back toward one global regime.

faces.title: Loss-aware quotienting preserves task-relevant factors until irrelevance is tested
faces.text:
S.u1gk contributes evidence that hard symmetry can remove predictive information; S.exnj contributes the formal quotient that determines which distinctions disappear; S.6arU contributes independent addressability and deliberate conjunction. Together they earn a construction discipline: preserve candidate task factors as independently queryable degrees, test their relevance, and only then place truly nuisance variation inside the quotient. A convenient alignment or correct target symmetry is insufficient by itself.

faces.title: Constraint scope can vary locally without entangling the roles the task must still query
faces.text:
S.u1gk contributes task/regime-dependent consequences of symmetry constraints; S.qogS contributes input-local transformation support; S.6arU contributes stable independent role coordinates. Together they earn that an adaptive symmetry policy must vary the admissible transformation scope separately from the semantic roles used by the task. Local changes in invariance must not silently redefine the factors whose conjunction produces the answer.
Removal tests: remove S.u1gk and local scope lacks a task-risk governance reason; remove S.qogS and there is no input-conditioned support; remove S.6arU and local scope can become entangled with task-factor semantics.

faces.title: Context-conditioned quotient continuity has an explicit evidence membrane
faces.text:
S.exnj contributes quotient-relative sameness and estimation burden; S.qogS contributes a locally estimated symmetry support with approximation limits; S.6arU contributes stable address semantics under extrapolative change. Together they earn that a context-conditioned equivalence relation can remain interpretable across changing inputs only when the transformation family, its estimation/identification assumptions, and the semantic coordinate roles are carried together. Otherwise a changing quotient is indistinguishable from a changing definition of the object itself.
Removal tests: remove S.exnj and sameness lacks quotient semantics; remove S.qogS and the quotient has no local/context-varying support; remove S.6arU and no stable role/address semantics remain through the scope change.

volume.title: Locally warranted equivalence
volume.text:
Across all four parents, invariance becomes a governed, evidence-bearing operation rather than an intrinsic property that can be imposed globally without cost. S.u1gk separates target symmetry, encountered distribution symmetry and learner-imposed symmetry and demonstrates that erasing non-invariant structure can change risk. S.exnj makes representational sameness explicitly quotient-relative and shows that broader invariance both erases more structure and raises estimation burden. S.qogS makes the admissible symmetry regime itself local/input-dependent and preserves the approximation boundary on identifying that regime. S.6arU shows how task factors can remain independently addressable with stable semantics until an intentional conjunction, preventing a representational convenience from silently rewriting the roles a task needs.


The complete four-way closure is therefore: equivalence/invariance should be treated as a locally warranted, task-conditioned quotient rather than a global declaration of sameness. A transformation may be ignored only where current evidence supports that the distinction it erases is nuisance for the present obligation. Independently meaningful task factors should remain separately addressable until that irrelevance is tested and the intended conjunction occurs. Because admissible symmetry/equivalence scope can vary across inputs and regimes, and broader quotients create both information-loss and estimation debt, the quotient must carry its local validity/identifiability boundary and be re-evaluated when context changes.


Bounded volume invariant
A system can preserve useful equivalence across changing representations by quotienting only transformations that are locally warranted as nuisance for the current task, while keeping independently meaningful factors separately addressable until deliberate conjunction; the transformation scope and its evidence boundary must travel together because local symmetry can vary and broader invariance can erase predictive structure or exceed the evidence available to identify the equivalence.


Four-way necessity
- Remove S.u1gk: the closure loses the demonstrated distinction among target, data and imposed symmetry and the evidence that an incorrect hard quotient can delete predictive information.
- Remove S.exnj: the closure loses explicit quotient-relative sameness, metric/equivalence semantics and the evidence cost of widening nuisance freedom.
- Remove S.qogS: the closure loses the input-local symmetry field and the approximation/identifiability membrane that makes transformation scope context-dependent.
- Remove S.6arU: the closure loses the constructive rule that independently meaningful roles can remain separately addressable with stable semantics until deliberate conjunction.


DERIVED CROSS-ORGANISM INVARIANTS


INV-1H.F8cX-LOCAL-QUOTIENT — Treat invariance as a locally warranted equivalence contract
Minimal body: 1H.F8cX:wxy
Invariant: A transformation should count as nuisance only after an explicit quotient is declared, the erased distinction is shown to be irrelevant to the stated task obligation, and the local/contextual support on which that equivalence is asserted is sufficiently identified.
CREATE: state the task obligation, candidate nuisance transformation family, and local regime in which equivalence is proposed.
COPY: carry the same quotient definition together with its task/local validity conditions when reusing the comparison or constraint.
CONTROL: reject global or target-only symmetry claims as sufficient authorization for hard invariance when local/task evidence disagrees or remains unidentified.
CULTIVATE: re-estimate the admissible transformation support as data distribution, context, model regime or task changes.
Compression: equivalence is warranted locally; it is not free global sameness.


INV-1H.F8cX-PRESERVE-BEFORE-QUOTIENT — Preserve candidate task factors until nuisance status survives intervention
Minimal body: 1H.F8cX:wxz
Invariant: Before quotienting a variable or transformation away, keep the potentially independent factor addressable long enough to test whether its variation carries task-relevant information; only distinctions that survive that relevance test as nuisance should be erased.
CREATE: separate candidate semantic/task factors from candidate nuisance coordinates.
COPY: preserve those roles independently through representation and evaluation so changing one does not silently rewrite another.
CONTROL: independently vary the candidate factors and transformations; block quotienting when the supposedly nuisance degree changes the required outcome or evidential claim.
CULTIVATE: introduce deliberate conjunction only after role independence and nuisance irrelevance have been stress-tested across broader regimes.
Compression: test a distinction before making it disappear.


INV-1H.F8cX-EVIDENCE-BUDGET — Invariance flexibility cannot outrun equivalence identification
Minimal body: 1H.F8cX:xy
Invariant: More permissive or more context-sensitive equivalence increases the burden of identifying the admissible transformation set and estimating stable comparisons; invariance scope should expand only as evidence supports the additional nuisance freedom.
CREATE: pair every proposed quotient/symmetry-support family with an explicit estimation and identification regime.
COPY: preserve sample density, alignment/estimator family, neighborhood assumptions and validation protocol with the equivalence claim.
CONTROL: test convergence, neighborhood fidelity and counter-transformations that should remain visible; treat unstable local estimates or over-flexible alignment as open identification debt.
CULTIVATE: widen or localize the quotient incrementally as additional evidence closes the corresponding estimation burden.
Compression: every additional ignored degree of freedom must be paid for with evidence.


METABOLITE-COLLAPSE PASS
A candidate “use local symmetry instead of global symmetry” metabolite was rejected as too broad: S.qogS does not establish universal local identifiability and S.u1gk does not show that local constraints always dominate global ones. A candidate “disentanglement is always better” metabolite was rejected because S.6arU explicitly preserves deliberate conjunction and the other parents only require distinctions relevant to the present claim. A candidate “more invariance is worse” metabolite was rejected because S.u1gk contains regimes where symmetrization helps and S.exnj treats broader quotienting as a legitimate choice with an evidence cost rather than a universal error. Three metabolites survive collapse: locally warranted quotient scope, preserve-before-quotient intervention, and the evidence budget of invariance flexibility.

edges.title: Adaptive growth changes the assurance surface
edges.text: w makes competence and even its carrier expand through reconstruction; x makes assurance relative to a declared condition class and its finite-sample/complexity debt. Together they earn that growth of capability or operating horizon cannot by itself extend an existing guarantee. A new reachable regime may require a richer condition class, new assumptions, or a weaker/error-controlled assurance statement. Remove w and there is no endogenous expansion pressure; remove x and there is no explicit assurance boundary to be crossed.

edges.title: Reconstructive continuity needs an explicit quotient of ignorable change
edges.text: w permits identity/function to persist while material or representational realization changes; y shows one concrete way representation differences can be lawfully ignored only under a declared equivalence/canonicalization procedure. Together they earn that reconstruction requires a witness of which differences are immaterial to identity at that layer. Remove w and canonicalization has no adaptive turnover problem to solve; remove y and reconstructive persistence lacks a reproducible account of which representational differences may be quotiented away.

edges.title: Rebuilding across representations requires transformed obligations, not copied claims
edges.text: w makes changing carriers and multiscale organization normal; z shows that when source and target observations differ, assurance must cross through an explicit relation and may change strength or meaning. Together they earn relation-mediated reconstruction: a rebuilt carrier can count as continued function only after the obligations relevant to the new representation have been transported and checked. Remove w and there is no self-reconstructive carrier transition; remove z and the claim crossing that transition has no formal transport discipline.

edges.title: Canonical sameness and validity scope are independent contracts
edges.text: x indexes predictive assurance by a condition/shift family; y indexes representational sameness by a data-model/canonicalization quotient. Together they earn that eliminating syntactic variance does not strengthen statistical validity, and refining assurance resolution does not alter what counts as the canonical object. Remove x and there is no guarantee-scope axis; remove y and there is no representation-equivalence axis.

edges.title: Cross-representation assurance must carry both transport relation and guarantee class
edges.text: x shows that assurance strength depends on the declared condition family and error/complexity budget; z shows that properties crossing representation boundaries are transformed by a relation and typed by observation/property class. Together they earn a two-coordinate evidence boundary: what is transported and over which conditions it is guaranteed must travel together. Remove x and the condition-resolution debt disappears; remove z and representation/observation mismatch is silently normalized away.

edges.title: Quotient equivalence is not the same operation as relational translation
edges.text: y shows a within-model canonical quotient that removes incidental representation differences while preserving one canonical RDF dataset object; z shows cross-language translation where source and target observations may genuinely differ and properties must therefore be mapped rather than identified. Together they earn a sharp distinction: canonicalization may justify sameness inside one declared quotient, whereas translation across nonidentical observational domains requires a relation and can alter obligations. Remove y and there is no witnessed quotient-sameness case; remove z and there is no witnessed nonidentity transport case.

faces.title: Adaptive reconstruction separates identity continuity from assurance continuity
faces.text: w supplies continual rebuilding and horizon expansion, x supplies condition-indexed validity, and y supplies quotient-scoped canonical identity. Together they earn that a reconstructed system can remain the same object under an accepted representation quotient while its previous assurance becomes stale because the operating/conditioning frontier changed. Remove w and no evolving carrier pressures the two contracts; remove x and assurance cannot go stale independently; remove y and identity persistence has no explicit quotient witness.

faces.title: Expansion requires relation-mediated revalidation
faces.text: w supplies adaptive capability growth, x supplies bounded assurance resolution, and z supplies relation-mediated property transport. Together they earn that when an adaptive system enters a new representation or problem regime, inherited guarantees must be transported through the actual source-target relation and re-evaluated over the new condition/property class. Remove w and there is no boundary-crossing growth; remove x and revalidation has no scope index; remove z and the representation crossing has no transport law.

faces.title: Reconstructive continuity can use different witnesses within and between regimes
faces.text: w supplies continued function through changing realization, y supplies canonical sameness within a declared quotient, and z supplies relational correspondence when source and target representations are not identical. Together they earn a layered continuity witness: quotient/canonicalization can justify sameness inside a regime, while explicit relation transport is required between regimes whose observations differ. Remove w and there is no continuity claim to witness; remove y and within-regime representational equivalence is missing; remove z and cross-regime correspondence is missing.

faces.title: A portable claim has three separable coordinates
faces.text: x supplies assurance scope and error debt, y supplies identity/equivalence quotient, and z supplies source-target transport relation plus property/context typing. Together they earn that a portable claim is not one undifferentiated certificate: it must separately state what object is treated as equivalent, how the claim crosses representation boundaries, and the class/regime over which the resulting claim is warranted. Remove any parent and one coordinate becomes implicit.

volume.title: Scope-bearing adaptive transformation contract
volume.text:
A system that continually rebuilds or expands its own competence can preserve warranted continuity across representational change only by carrying three separable contracts with the transformation: (1) an identity/equivalence quotient specifying which representation differences may be ignored, (2) an explicit source-target relation specifying how obligations and guarantees are transported when observations differ, and (3) an assurance scope specifying the condition/property class, assumptions, approximation/error debt and contextual regime over which the transported claim is warranted. Adaptive growth supplies the pressure that makes these contracts dynamic rather than archival: when the reachable problem/representation frontier changes, an old identity witness may remain valid while its assurance scope or transport relation no longer does. Continuity of the organism therefore does not entail continuity of every warrant. Boundary-crossing transformations require the affected contracts to be revalidated or reissued rather than inherited silently.


Bounded volume invariant:
Reconstructive adaptation is lawfully portable when identity quotient, representation-transport relation, and assurance scope remain explicit and independently revalidated at the current boundary; persistence of one coordinate never automatically upgrades or preserves the others.


Evidence boundary:
This is a cross-source structural synthesis. It combines one conceptual biological design argument, one formal statistical framework, one normative RDF canonicalization standard, and one formal compiler/secure-compilation theory. Their recurrence earns an architectural distinction between identity, transport and assurance contracts under adaptive change; it does not prove that every adaptive system, statistical guarantee, graph canonicalization, or compiler instantiates one universal mechanism.


COLLAPSED METABOLITES — 2


INV-1H.FXzc-01 — SEPARATED TRANSFORMATION CONTRACT
Minimal earning body: xyz.
Bounded invariant: A claim carried through representation change has at least three logically separable coordinates when these source families are jointly respected: the equivalence/identity quotient, the source-target transport relation, and the assurance/property scope. Success of one coordinate does not certify the others.
CREATE: declare the three coordinates before treating a transformed artifact or claim as warranted continuation.
COPY: transport each coordinate explicitly rather than collapsing all three into a generic notion of “same”.
CONTROL: reject inferences that use canonical sameness as proof of stronger validity, or a lawful transport relation as proof that an unchanged guarantee class still applies.
CULTIVATE: refine the quotient, relation, or assurance class independently as new regimes expose different failure modes.
Compression: sameness, transport, and warrant are distinct parts of one transformation contract.


INV-1H.FXzc-02 — BOUNDARY-EXPANSION REVALIDATION
Minimal earning body: wxyz.
Bounded invariant: When reconstructive growth changes the reachable problem, representation, observation, or conditioning frontier, every affected part of the transformation contract must be retested at the new boundary; organism continuity does not authorize silent inheritance of stale assurance.
CREATE: mark a witnessed frontier crossing as a new validation event rather than as ordinary in-regime continuation.
COPY: preserve predecessor contracts as provenance while issuing the current boundary-specific witness.
CONTROL: classify whether the change affected identity quotient, transport relation, assurance scope, or more than one; require fresh evidence only where the boundary actually moved.
CULTIVATE: let repeated revalidation produce a lineage of explicit transformation contracts rather than accumulating hidden assumptions.
Compression: growth may preserve the organism while forcing its warrants to be earned again.

Two metabolites survive. INV-01 captures the triadic separation already earned by x+y+z. INV-02 requires the full four-parent volume because only w turns the static three-coordinate contract into a boundary-crossing adaptive lifecycle. edges.title: CERTIFIED STABILITY UNDER EXPLICIT VARIATION
edges.text:
S.P4wu makes stable decision performance meaningful only through an explicit minimax or saddle certificate and support scope; S.4USS makes universality meaningful only when a derived relation survives measured nuisance and carrier variation with failure coordinates retained. Together, invariance is not visual or rhetorical stability: it requires named variation coordinates plus a witness that the relation survives them.
necessity: w supplies the formal criterion and certificate; x supplies measured carrier/nuisance variation and relational stability.

edges.title: OPERATIONAL SUFFICIENCY DOES NOT SETTLE ONTOLOGY
edges.text:
S.P4wu earns a rule relative to a stated loss and risk problem; S.fOgn earns held-out prediction while leaving code and mechanism identity unresolved. Together, a criterion can certify operational adequacy without identifying the representation or mechanism realizing it.
necessity: w supplies a crisp certificate and sufficiency obligation; y supplies the demonstrated separation between predictive adequacy and identity.

edges.title: INVARIANT PRINCIPLE, MUTABLE IMPLEMENTATION OR LOCATION
edges.text:
S.P4wu preserves the same worst-risk principle across continuous and discrete support even when the boundary mechanism changes; S.s0XZ preserves exact digital object identity across origin or locator changes through an independent intrinsic verifier. Together, sameness belongs to the witnessed invariant or object, not to the current implementation or locator.
necessity: w supplies topology-sensitive implementation change under one criterion; z supplies object-bound identity separated from custody and location.

edges.title: ROBUST RECURRENCE EARNS RELATION, NOT MECHANISM IDENTITY
edges.text:
S.4USS establishes a derived response stable across device and regime variation; S.fOgn establishes predictive alignment across levels and held-out contexts while refusing to infer a shared code. Together, cross-context stability can warrant a relational invariant while leaving underlying mechanism identity open.
necessity: x supplies nuisance-resistant physical recurrence; y supplies explicit ontology restraint.

edges.title: STABLE OBJECT OR RELATION AND MUTABLE CONTEXT OCCUPY SEPARATE COORDINATES
edges.text:
S.4USS separates a stable derived response from disorder, device and crossover coordinates; S.s0XZ separates intrinsic object identity from origin, resolver and custody. Together, admissible variability must remain explicitly represented rather than folded into the identity or invariant itself.
necessity: x supplies physical nuisance-coordinate pressure; z supplies provenance/custody-coordinate pressure.

edges.title: CORRESPONDENCE AND RETRIEVAL COORDINATES ARE NOT IDENTITY COORDINATES
edges.text:
S.fOgn shows that a mapping can align model and biological coordinates without proving a common code; S.s0XZ shows that a locator or resolver can find and carry an object without defining exact object identity. Together, correspondence can be useful and reproducible while formally distinct from identity.
necessity: y supplies representational mapping without identity; z supplies retrieval/provenance without identity.


FOUR TRIPLE FACES
wxy — CERTIFIED GENERALIZATION WITHOUT ONTOLOGY COLLAPSE
A robust relation qualifies only after performance and stability are certified under stated variation, and even then mechanism identity remains open.
removal test: remove w and the explicit certificate criterion disappears; remove x and measured nuisance/carrier variation disappears; remove y and robustness can be overpromoted into mechanism identity.


wxz — TYPED-CHANGE INVARIANCE CONTRACT
An invariant can require a changed implementation when support topology changes, must be tested across device or nuisance variation, and can preserve exact object identity across origin or custody change only through an object-bound verifier. The admissible change class is therefore part of the continuity law; invariant, implementation and context remain separately auditable.
removal test: w is required for topology-typed adaptation; x for empirical nuisance testing; z for exact identity/provenance separation.


wyz — VERIFIED CONTINUITY WITHOUT REPRESENTATION OR LOCATOR IDENTITY
A decision criterion can independently certify adequacy while a predictive map remains non-identical to mechanism and a locator remains non-identical to object. Successful mapping or reacquisition may therefore carry a warranted relation while identity still requires a separate witness.
removal test: w removes the certificate; y removes the representation-nonidentity witness; z removes the object-identity versus location witness.


xyz — RECURRENCE MUST TYPE INVARIANT, VARIATION AND IDENTITY COORDINATES
A physical relational observable can remain stable under nuisance variation; a predictive mapping can remain stable without mechanism identification; and exact object identity can remain stable while provenance and custody move. Recurrence across contexts is interpretable only when what stayed stable, what varied, and what is merely a coordinate are separately typed.
removal test: x removes physical variation pressure; y removes ontology restraint; z removes the exact-object identity coordinate.


ALL-FOUR VOLUME — TYPED INVARIANCE WITHOUT IDENTITY COLLAPSE
The four bodies close on a single governance law: continuity and sameness are typed warrants, not free-floating labels. To claim that a relation, object, decision principle or correspondence persists, the organism must state the class of changes under which persistence was tested, carry an independent witness for the thing claimed invariant, and retain the boundary at which that warrant fails. Stable correspondence is allowed to remain correspondence. It does not inherit object or mechanism identity merely by recurring.


four-parent necessity:
- S.P4wu supplies certificate structure and the fact that one criterion may demand different implementation under changed support topology.
- S.4USS supplies empirically tested relational invariance together with explicit nuisance and failure coordinates.
- S.fOgn supplies strong predictive recurrence together with explicit refusal to identify mechanism or code.
- S.s0XZ supplies exact object identity separated from locator, origin and custody.
No proper triple carries all four obligations simultaneously: certification/adaptive implementation, empirical nuisance stability, ontology restraint, and intrinsic identity/provenance separation.

1. TYPED-INVARIANCE-WARRANT
Invariant validity names an admissible variation class, an independent witness or certificate, and a failure boundary. Context-free sameness is not earned.


2. CORRESPONDENCE-DOES-NOT-IDENTIFY
Predictive, retrieval or relational correspondence can be real and reproducible without proving identity of mechanism, object or implementation. Correspondence/context coordinates remain separate from identity.


3. BOUNDARY-REVALIDATION
When support, regime, carrier or context crosses outside the validated class, continuity must be adapted and re-certified or reissued. Authority is not silently inherited across an untested boundary.

edges.title: Locally regenerated control can be causally real without a persistent global state
edges.text:
S.MmWr establishes that just-in-time emotion-concept representations can causally regulate behavior even though a chronic speaker-specific state probe does not generalize convincingly. S.dgx1 establishes that a recognizable pattern can be maintained by continuously regenerated local dynamics rather than fixed coordinates. Together they earn a bounded recurrence: persistent functional effect can arise from repeated local reconstruction without a continuously stored global state.
Removal test: without S.MmWr, causal behavioral regulation by locally retrieved representations disappears; without S.dgx1, process identity through recurrent reconstruction is unearned.

edges.title: Selective retained structure can sustain policy continuity while deployment changes
edges.text:
S.MmWr shows that post-training can preserve broad representational geometry while changing which concepts are recruited and how they influence policy. S.Q41N preserves a small invariant anchor and rolling local context while ordinary history is discarded. Together they derive that continuity can reside in a bounded scaffold whose current deployment is repeatedly regenerated rather than in complete historical retention or a fixed activation profile.
Removal test: without S.MmWr, substrate-preserving policy reshaping disappears; without S.Q41N, explicit bounded retention through rolling execution disappears.

edges.title: Causal self/affect-relative regulation does not establish enduring or phenomenal selfhood
edges.text:
S.MmWr earns functionally real emotion-like causal variables while explicitly leaving subjective feeling and persistent hidden emotion open. S.dY9d earns framing-sensitive self-positioning while explicitly leaving enduring self-model and phenomenal awareness unestablished. Together they derive an epistemic recurrence: self- or affect-relative causal organization may be scientifically real at the functional level without licensing a stronger persistence or phenomenology claim.
Removal test: without S.MmWr, the affective causal intervention surface disappears; without S.dY9d, explicit self-similarity conditioning and its construct-validity boundary disappear.

edges.title: Open-ended process identity can be carried by bounded recurrent state
edges.text:
S.dgx1 shows stable identity as continuously maintained local process across changing visible states. S.Q41N shows long-running generation with fixed-size recurrent context using an anchor plus rolling state. Together they derive that an open-ended process need not preserve the whole past or one fixed snapshot when bounded local state is sufficient to reconstruct the relations required for continuation.
Removal test: without S.dgx1, process identity beyond snapshot equality is unearned; without S.Q41N, bounded-state open-ended execution is unearned.

edges.title: Identity claims must survive transformations orthogonal to the eliciting representation
edges.text:
S.dgx1 strengthens process claims by testing timing, orientation, damage, and grid changes while keeping interpretation bounded by failures. S.dY9d shows that a self-like behavioral effect remains tied to one task and an explicit “like you” cue until broader paraphrase/domain/mechanistic robustness is demonstrated. Together they derive a validity rule: an identity/process claim is stronger when the target relation survives perturbations that change its surface carrier or eliciting cue.
Removal test: without S.dgx1, there is no direct process-under-carrier-perturbation witness; without S.dY9d, the explicit construct-validity ladder for self-like claims disappears.

edges.title: Stabilizing context is also a policy bias
edges.text:
S.Q41N’s persistent attention sink prevents drift while resisting major scene changes; S.dY9d’s matched opponent framing changes the selected strategic policy. Together they derive that retained or supplied context is not neutral scaffolding: it can stabilize one policy family by restricting which alternatives remain reachable.
Removal test: without S.Q41N, the stability–adaptability cost of a persistent anchor disappears; without S.dY9d, controlled evidence that contextual identity framing changes policy disappears.

faces.title: Functional continuity can be regenerated from bounded local state
faces.text:
S.MmWr contributes causal just-in-time regulation without a validated persistent state, S.dgx1 contributes pattern identity through local reconstruction, and S.Q41N contributes a concrete bounded-memory recursive execution process. Together they earn a three-way recurrence: persistent function can be produced by repeated re-instantiation from bounded local state rather than by continuously storing the full state or full past.
Removal tests: remove S.MmWr and causally consequential local regulation disappears; remove S.dgx1 and identity-as-regeneration disappears; remove S.Q41N and bounded-state open-ended execution disappears.

faces.title: Operational self-like regulation must be defined by robust recurrence, not persistent-state assumptions
faces.text:
S.MmWr separates functional affect from persistent/phenomenal emotion, S.dgx1 separates process identity from snapshot identity, and S.dY9d separates behavioral self-positioning from enduring selfhood. Together they derive that a self/state label should track a recurrent functional relation that survives relevant perturbation, not merely the persistence of one activation or the strength of one eliciting label.
Removal tests: remove S.MmWr and the causal local-regulation boundary disappears; remove S.dgx1 and process-vs-snapshot identity disappears; remove S.dY9d and self-reference construct validity disappears.

faces.title: Scaffolds that preserve behavior can also constrain future policy
faces.text:
S.MmWr shows that inherited representational structure can be redeployed by post-training, S.Q41N shows that retained anchors stabilize while resisting radical change, and S.dY9d shows that identity framing changes strategic policy. Together they derive that preserved representational/contextual structure is simultaneously continuity carrier and intervention surface: what is retained to stabilize behavior can bias which future policies or interpretations remain accessible.
Removal tests: remove S.MmWr and developmental redeployment of a preserved substrate disappears; remove S.Q41N and the anchoring cost disappears; remove S.dY9d and the contextual policy-selection witness disappears.

faces.title: Recursive identity claims require self-produced-state exposure plus perturbational validity
faces.text:
S.dgx1 exposes recurrent local organization to timing/substrate/damage perturbations, S.Q41N explicitly trains the deployed recursive process on self-generated rollout state, and S.dY9d requires self-like claims to survive changes beyond one eliciting phrase/task. Together they derive a validation discipline for recursive systems: generality is earned by confronting the states the recurrence itself produces while also perturbing carriers/cues that could otherwise masquerade as stable identity.
Removal tests: remove S.dgx1 and distributed process-under-perturbation evidence disappears; remove S.Q41N and self-produced-state training disappears; remove S.dY9d and the construct-validity ladder disappears.

volume.title: Regenerative identity under bounded state
volume.text:
Across four heterogeneous source organisms, continuity and control repeatedly persist without one continuously active global state or complete retained history. Emotion-like control can be locally re-instantiated when context makes it relevant; a neural cellular automaton repeatedly rebuilds the relations that define its pattern; a streaming generator preserves only a small anchor plus rolling state while ordinary history disappears; and self-like strategic positioning remains only as strong as the intervention robustness that distinguishes a functional relation from an eliciting cue.


The four-way closure is therefore: functional identity can be carried by a recurrently regenerated control regime that preserves only enough state or scaffold to reconstruct task-relevant relations. But preservation mechanisms are not neutral. Anchors, role representations, objectives, and identity framings also constrain which future behaviors remain reachable. Continuity therefore requires two simultaneous disciplines: enough retained structure to regenerate the relevant relation, and enough perturbational freedom to detect when the stabilizing scaffold has become an obsolete bias rather than a faithful carrier.


Bounded volume invariant
A functional identity can persist through recurrent reconstruction from bounded local state rather than continuous storage of a complete state, provided the preserved scaffold is sufficient to regenerate the relevant relations and is revised when its own stabilizing bias blocks required change.


Four-way necessity
- Remove S.MmWr: the closure loses causal local regulation without a persistent state and collapses toward process continuity without a behaviorally active control variable.
- Remove S.dgx1: the closure loses the direct distinction between process identity and snapshot identity and collapses toward bounded memory/conditioning without demonstrated regenerative pattern identity.
- Remove S.Q41N: the closure loses the explicit bounded-state execution mechanism and the anchor stability–adaptability tradeoff.
- Remove S.dY9d: the closure loses the intervention-bounded validity criterion that prevents operational identity/self-conditioning from becoming an unearned enduring ontology.


DERIVED CROSS-ORGANISM INVARIANTS


INV-1H.L4ld-RECONSTRUCTION — Persistent function can be regenerated from bounded state
Minimal body: 1H.L4ld:wxy
Invariant: A recurrent system may preserve task-relevant identity/function without preserving its complete past or one continuously active global state when bounded local state repeatedly reconstructs the relations required for continuation.
CREATE: Define the relation that must remain recognizable and a bounded recurrent state sufficient to reconstruct it when needed.
COPY: Carry the relation by repeatedly re-instantiating it across changing local states rather than copying one complete snapshot or full history.
CONTROL: Remove or corrupt retained state, vary rollout length and perturb local carriers; require continuity to fail specifically when reconstruction-critical information is removed.
CULTIVATE: Learn which retained variables are actually reconstruction-critical, compress dispensable history, and expand state only when new obligations prove the reduced carrier insufficient.
Compression: Preserve what lets the relation be rebuilt, not necessarily everything that ever happened.


INV-1H.L4ld-ANCHOR-DEBT — Stabilization consumes reachable futures
Minimal body: 1H.L4ld:wyz
Invariant: A scaffold or anchor that suppresses drift also biases the process toward policies compatible with that retained context, so continuity mechanisms require explicit revision conditions.
CREATE: Introduce a stable anchor, inherited representation, or contextual frame that constrains recurrent behavior.
COPY: Preserve that scaffold across updates so the process remains inside a coherent operating region.
CONTROL: Stress with regime changes, alternative framings, scene replacement, post-training shifts, and other cases where old context should cease to dominate.
CULTIVATE: Replace, relax, or reweight the scaffold when evidence shows that its former stabilizing role now blocks required adaptation.
Compression: What prevents drift can become the thing that prevents change.


INV-1H.L4ld-VALIDITY — Identity is only as strong as the perturbations it survives
Minimal body: 1H.L4ld:wxz
Invariant: Operational self-, affect-, or process-identity claims should be promoted only to the level supported by robustness across interventions that change the eliciting cue, carrier, context, or snapshot while preserving the target functional relation.
CREATE: Formulate the narrow functional identity claim and the contrast or relation that would witness it.
COPY: Reproduce the relation across repeated contexts and independently varying carriers rather than relying on one wording, state, or visual realization.
CONTROL: Apply paraphrase, role, substrate, timing, damage, and mechanistic perturbations chosen to separate true relation-level recurrence from cue-specific persistence.
CULTIVATE: Promote the identity claim stepwise only as wider intervention families preserve it; retain weaker operational language when generalization fails.
Compression: A recurring label is not an identity; a relation that survives independent perturbation may become one.


METABOLITE-COLLAPSE PASS
A provisional “recursive systems should train on self-generated state” metabolite was not retained independently because S.Q41N already earns that claim at source level; its cross-organism contribution is absorbed into the VALIDITY and RECONSTRUCTION bodies, where self-produced state becomes one of several necessary stress surfaces. A provisional “local state is always sufficient” metabolite was rejected because every parent preserves explicit regime boundaries and failure modes. A provisional “persistent self does not exist” claim was rejected: the sources only show that persistent functional identity does not require one specific continuously active carrier and that stronger selfhood claims remain unearned in these studies. Three cross-organism metabolites survive collapse.

edges.title: Relational structure carries role-specific warrants, not one generic validity
edges.text: w makes correspondence/update structure operational only through compatibility, reflection and property-specific composition laws; x makes dependence topology evidential only through a genuine independence contract. Together they earn a role-separation rule: a relational structure is not self-certifying. The warrant that licenses coordinated propagation is distinct from the warrant that licenses stochastic concentration. Remove w and no propagation/repair contract remains; remove x and no probabilistic dependence contract remains.

edges.title: Compatible propagation must be scoped to the invariance regime actually present
edges.text: w permits update-informed restoration across changing representations but only under explicit compatibility; y shows that transformation symmetry can be heterogeneous and input-local rather than globally shared. Together they earn that equivalence-sensitive propagation cannot silently inherit one global invariance regime: the scope over which a transformation relation is treated as stable must be locally warranted. Remove w and there is no propagation obligation; remove y and there is no source-grounded pressure for locally varying invariance scope.

edges.title: Restoration can be directed by the downstream obligation without erasing change history
edges.text: w preserves the initiating update and prior consistent context as conditioning information for restoration; z makes the downstream query the explicit object whose uncertainty should guide experimental action. Together they earn a selective repair principle: when several distinctions remain unresolved, coordination may prioritize distinctions that affect the declared obligation while still preserving the causal/update history that made repair necessary. Remove w and target-directed action loses its continuity/history constraint; remove z and restoration has no source-grounded obligation selector.

edges.title: Local neighborhood structure is not a stochastic independence certificate
edges.text: x requires actual independent subfamilies/nonadjacency semantics before topology can support concentration; y reaches local symmetry through invariant-space neighborhood proxies whose quality is itself an assumption. Together they earn a strict boundary: similarity, neighborhood membership, symmetry class or visual separation cannot be converted into effective independent samples merely because they define a useful local geometry. Remove x and the statistical prohibition disappears; remove y and there is no concrete learned local-neighborhood structure whose evidential status must be separated.

edges.title: Informative intervention choice does not certify independent evidence
edges.text: x makes finite-sample stochastic strength depend on a witnessed dependence structure; z chooses interventions adaptively for expected information about a declared query. Together they earn that an experiment can be well targeted yet still produce dependent evidence. Query-specific information gain and effective independent evidence are different quantities and require different witnesses. Remove x and dependence no longer constrains evidential strength; remove z and there is no adaptive information-selection process to distinguish from that strength.

edges.title: Local or task-specific sufficiency can close before global structural closure
edges.text: y makes a local symmetry support/level a meaningful estimand even when one dataset-wide symmetry summary is inadequate; z shows formally that a query can become identified while the posterior over full causal models remains broad. Together they earn a non-maximal sufficiency principle: the variable required for a local task may close before the larger structural model does, provided the local estimand and its approximation/identifiability boundary remain explicit. Remove y and locality/heterogeneity is not represented; remove z and early stopping before global model identification is not formally warranted.

faces.title: Locally scoped relational operation requires separate propagation and evidence witnesses
faces.text: w supplies compatibility-gated synchronization, x supplies independence-gated concentration, and y supplies a locally varying symmetry/equivalence scope. Together they earn that a local relational regime needs at least two independent custody channels before it is both actionable and evidential: one witness says which transformations/updates may be propagated there, while another says what stochastic dependence assumptions support statistical strength there. Local geometry alone supplies neither. Remove w and coordinated change is ungated; remove x and stochastic evidence is ungated; remove y and the contract has no locally varying regime to govern.

faces.title: Query-directed coordination does not collapse its statistical evidence contract
faces.text: w supplies history-sensitive restoration across representations, x supplies the dependence witness required for finite-sample evidence, and z supplies the downstream query that decides which uncertainty matters for the next action. Together they earn a three-way separation between what should be changed, how consistency may be restored, and how strongly the resulting observations count as evidence. Remove w and there is no coordinated restoration; remove x and evidential strength becomes ungoverned; remove z and the action has no explicit downstream obligation.

faces.title: Obligation-scoped coordination can remain local under heterogeneous invariance
faces.text: w supplies lawful propagation under compatibility, y supplies input-dependent symmetry scope, and z supplies query-relative sufficiency/action. Together they earn an adaptive coordination rule: the system need not force a global representation or global symmetry decision before acting. It may coordinate only within the locally warranted invariance regime and only to the degree needed by the declared downstream obligation, while preserving unresolved structure outside that obligation. Remove w and no propagation law remains; remove y and scope cannot vary locally; remove z and selective stopping/action has no target.

faces.title: Local target sufficiency is not equivalent to global statistical certainty
faces.text: x supplies the distinction between descriptive topology and statistically warranted independence, y supplies an approximation-bounded local estimand, and z supplies the possibility that a declared query closes before the full model. Together they earn that local/task success can be legitimate without being promoted into a globally identified model or an independence claim. Remove x and statistical certainty can leak from structure; remove y and there is no local approximation membrane; remove z and early target closure is not an explicit objective state.

volume.title: Warrant-separated selective action
volume.text:
A changing multi-representation system can act selectively before globally resolving every structural uncertainty only when four distinct warrants remain explicit. A local scope warrant states where an invariance/equivalence assumption is currently meaningful; a downstream-obligation warrant states which unresolved distinctions still matter for the target quantity; a propagation warrant states which updates, amendments and compositions may lawfully carry change across representations; and an evidence warrant states what dependence assumptions justify statistical strength. These warrants interact but do not substitute for one another.


The four parents jointly make this closure operational. Input-local symmetry can delimit the regime in which a transformation assumption is plausible; query-scoped Bayesian design can delimit which uncertainty is worth reducing next; update-conditioned synchronization can carry and repair change through that regime under compatibility laws; and partial-dependence concentration blocks the resulting topology, recurrence or successful coordination from being mistaken for independent evidence without a separate stochastic witness. Selective action therefore does not mean selective rigor: local/query sufficiency may close while broader structure remains unresolved, but approximation debt, compatibility debt and dependence debt remain separately visible.


Rank necessity: remove S.REkw and the closure loses a law for preserving causal change-history through coordinated multi-representation repair; remove S.FLcQ and it loses the independent evidential gate separating topology from stochastic strength; remove S.qogS and it loses the source-grounded reason scope must be input/regime local; remove S.nmMo and it loses the downstream obligation that licenses non-maximal stopping and directs the next information-seeking action. No three-parent face therefore contains the full four-warrant selective-action contract.


Evidence boundary: this is a cross-source structural synthesis, not a universal theorem about adaptive systems. It combines distinct formal and empirical regimes and conserves their original assumptions. In particular, it does not assign effective sample sizes or confidence to /papers genealogy, does not make inferred symmetry an architecture-routing truth, does not turn synchronization compatibility into statistical independence, and does not generalize ABCI beyond its bounded Bayesian/model/approximation regime.


COLLAPSED METABOLITES — 3


INV-1H.NUgs-01 — FOUR-WARRANT SELECTIVE ACTION
Minimal earning body: wxyz.
Bounded invariant: Selective action under unresolved global structure is warranted only when local scope, downstream obligation, propagation compatibility and stochastic evidence are kept as separable contracts. Success of one contract does not silently upgrade the others.
CREATE: name the target quantity and current local regime before acting.
COPY: carry scope, update history, compatibility and dependence assumptions with the action rather than compressing them into one generic confidence label.
CONTROL: block substitutions such as local similarity → independence, successful synchronization → statistical validity, or query closure → full-model identification.
CULTIVATE: revalidate only the contract whose boundary changes while preserving the others as explicit provenance.
Compression: act on what is sufficient, but keep every warrant that made sufficiency lawful.


INV-1H.NUgs-02 — INFORMATIVE CHANGE IS NOT INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Minimal earning body: wxz.
Bounded invariant: A query-targeted or history-informed intervention/update may be highly informative and operationally lawful without constituting statistically independent evidence; evidential strength remains governed by its own dependence witness.
CREATE: distinguish intervention utility from evidence weight.
COPY: retain the sampling/dependence lineage alongside adaptive intervention history.
CONTROL: refuse to infer effective sample size or concentration strength from informativeness, novelty, topology or repeated successful repair alone.
CULTIVATE: design stochastic recurrence experiments explicitly when quantitative evidence strength is needed.
Compression: choosing a good next move does not tell you how many independent observations you have.


INV-1H.NUgs-03 — LOCAL SUFFICIENCY MAY PRECEDE GLOBAL CLOSURE
Minimal earning body: yz.
Bounded invariant: A locally defined or downstream-specific quantity may become sufficient for a declared task while broader structural uncertainty remains, but that sufficiency inherits the approximation and model assumptions that define the local/query object.
CREATE: state the smallest quantity whose closure would satisfy the current obligation.
COPY: preserve unresolved global alternatives rather than collapsing them into the local answer.
CONTROL: stop the current task when the target is sufficiently identified without claiming global model or symmetry identification.
CULTIVATE: reopen broader structure only when a new obligation makes previously irrelevant distinctions consequential.
Compression: the answer needed now can close before the world-model does.


COLLAPSE WITNESS
Three metabolites survive independently. INV-01 requires all four parents and carries the full separated-warrant architecture. INV-02 requires synchronization/action/evidence separation and cannot be reduced to any one parent's native invariant. INV-03 is the cross-source local/query sufficiency relation supplied jointly by S.qogS and S.nmMo. Narrower restatements of compatibility, fractional-cover penalties, symmetry estimators and ABCI utilities remain parent tissue rather than being duplicated as holon metabolites.
