edges.title: CONTESTABLE DUAL-GATE RENEWAL
edges.text:
w separates successor continuity from permission-to-ignore and downstream action authority. x makes the renewal law itself contestable through executable replay, recurrence pressure, quotient re-witnessing, and reflexive successor tests. Together they earn a dual-gate renewal relation whose two authority gates can each invalidate a nominally successful repair.
Removal test: without w, contestable renewal lacks the explicit split between omission permission and downstream action permission; without x, dual-gated repair lacks an explicit requirement that the renewal law itself remain challengeable.
Boundary: successful restoration of continuity cannot close either authority gate by implication.

edges.title: PROVENANCE-TYPED DUAL REAUTHORIZATION
edges.text:
w supplies two separately re-earned successor authority gates. y supplies provenance-typed recurrence and the rule that reusable recovery form never substitutes for current continuity or action authority. Together they require every recurrence claim used during renewal to state what relation it supports and which gate it does not support.
Removal test: without w, typed recurrence does not force separate omission/action gates; without y, the two gates can receive undifferentiated recurrence confidence with no retained provenance class.
Boundary: recurrence provenance may support reuse of a repair relation, not current authority at either gate.

edges.title: COORDINATE-LOCALIZED TWO-GATE SUCCESSION
edges.text:
w supplies separate omission and action gates; z supplies the exact role/quotient/regime/evidence coordinate that justified reconstruction and the ability to revise repair machinery locally. Together they earn selective two-gate succession: reopen only the gate whose dependency surface intersects the changed coordinate, while preserving unaffected warrants at their prior scope.
Removal test: without w, addressable repair does not distinguish the two kinds of successor permission; without z, two-gate succession lacks the coordinate needed to keep reauthorization selective rather than blanket.
Boundary: locality preserves unaffected authority only when its dependency boundary is actually witnessed live.

edges.title: PROVENANCE-AWARE CONTESTABILITY
edges.text:
x requires the renewal law to survive executable replay and recurrence challenge. y separates same-constellation replication, variant-route recurrence, and different-parent convergence as distinct provenance relations. Together they earn challenge procedures that are typed by the evidence relation being challenged rather than by one generic notion of repeated success.
Removal test: without x, recurrence provenance can be recorded without being used to challenge the renewal law; without y, contestability can flatten unlike recurrence classes into one confidence signal.
Boundary: a recurrence class can falsify or support only the structural claim it actually addresses.

edges.title: ADDRESSABLE CONTESTABILITY OF REPAIR MACHINERY
edges.text:
x keeps the renewal law open to failure; z attaches failure, evidence return, version boundary, and repair-machinery revision to the smallest implicated coordinate. Together they earn a repair constitution whose own machinery can be revoked and revised locally rather than treated as invisible infrastructure.
Removal test: without x, local self-revision lacks an independent demand that the renewal law remain contestable; without z, contestability lacks a precise return address and tends toward global reset or vague distrust.
Boundary: repair machinery is itself a current warrant at an address, not an exempt meta-layer.

edges.title: PROVENANCE-ROUTED SELF-REVISION
edges.text:
y preserves the provenance type of recurrence while refusing authority transfer; z preserves local repair coordinates and successor version boundaries while allowing the recovery procedure to evolve. Together they earn a lineage in which recurrence evidence can guide which repair procedure to retry or revise, but every change remains localized and every successor remains freshly authorized.
Removal test: without y, revision can forget how reuse was evidenced; without z, typed recurrence lacks a precise coordinate at which to revise or retest the machinery.
Boundary: provenance can route attention; it cannot widen the authority of the coordinate it reaches.

faces.title: PROVENANCE-TYPED CONTESTABLE DUAL-GATE RENEWAL
faces.text:
w+x+y jointly make renewal contestable, keep recurrence provenance explicit, and force separate omission/action authority gates. The face can say what kind of recurrence supports retrying a repair and can challenge each successor gate independently.
Necessity: remove w → no explicit two-gate successor authority; remove x → no constitutive contestability of the renewal law; remove y → recurrence classes can collapse into generic repeated-success evidence.
Missing z boundary: the face still lacks the exact local authority/evidence coordinate needed to decide which gate and which repair machinery must reopen after a concrete failure.

faces.title: ADDRESSABLE CONTESTABLE DUAL-GATE SUCCESSION
faces.text:
w+x+z jointly make the renewal law challengeable, localize failure to exact coordinates, allow repair machinery to evolve, and separately govern omission/action permission. It can repair or succeed only the affected coordinate while keeping both successor gates explicit.
Necessity: remove w → no explicit two-gate split; remove x → no constitutive challenge path for the renewal law; remove z → no exact repair coordinate or local machinery revision.
Missing y boundary: the face lacks typed recurrence provenance, so evidence for reuse can still be flattened across replication, convergence, and variant routes.

faces.title: PROVENANCE-ROUTED SELECTIVE DUAL REAUTHORIZATION
faces.text:
w+y+z jointly keep recurrence provenance typed, route failure to the exact local coordinate, and reopen omission/action gates selectively rather than globally. It can say why a repair relation is worth retrying and where each permission must be re-earned.
Necessity: remove w → omission and action authority collapse; remove y → recurrence loses provenance type; remove z → reauthorization loses its local coordinate.
Missing x boundary: the face does not yet require the renewal procedure itself to remain independently contestable by executable replay and recurrence pressure.

faces.title: PROVENANCE-ROUTED CONTESTABLE SELF-REVISION
faces.text:
x+y+z jointly make the renewal law itself challengeable, preserve recurrence provenance, and localize self-revision to exact evidence/authority/version coordinates. It can evolve the repair constitution without treating it as immutable infrastructure.
Necessity: remove x → local revision is not constitutively contestable; remove y → recurrence support loses provenance class; remove z → no exact self-revision coordinate.
Missing w boundary: the face does not force omission permission and downstream action authority to remain two separately re-earned successor gates.

volume.title: provenance-routed contestable continuity-renewal constitution
volume.text:
All four parents jointly turn continuity renewal from a reusable procedure into a governed constitution without letting that constitution escape the same epistemic and authority constraints imposed on the warrants it repairs. w contributes the explicit two-gate successor membrane: permission to ignore distinctions and downstream permission to act must be re-earned separately after continuity repair. x contributes contestability: the renewal law itself must survive executable replay, recurrence pressure, quotient re-witnessing, and reflexive successor tests. y contributes provenance stratification: recurrence evidence remains typed by how the relation recurred and therefore cannot be flattened into generic confidence or independence. z contributes addressability and self-revision: failure, evidence return, version boundary, and machinery change are localized to the smallest implicated coordinate.


The complete closure is therefore a provenance-routed contestable continuity-renewal constitution. A lineage may preserve and evolve the machinery by which continuity is re-earned, but that machinery is itself a current, addressable, revocable warrant. Recurrence history may route which repair relation deserves another attempt, yet the provenance class must travel with the claim it supports. A concrete failure must identify the implicated coordinate, reopen the relevant evidence and current repair machinery, revise that machinery when necessary, replay current tests, and then separately re-earn the successor's permission-to-ignore scope and every downstream action warrant whose dependencies changed. Unaffected coordinates may remain live only under their still-valid local warrants. What can persist across generations is the governed procedure for earning permission, never any concrete permission itself.


BOUNDED VOLUME INVARIANT
A continuity-renewal constitution is warranted only when (1) recurrence evidence remains provenance-typed and ancestry-bounded, (2) every failure and machinery revision is routed to an exact authority/evidence/version coordinate, (3) the renewal law itself stays executable, contestable, revocable, and revisable, and (4) every repaired successor separately re-earns its permission-to-ignore scope and affected downstream action authority. Under those conditions the lineage may carry forward a mutable procedure for earning continuity and permission while no current warrant, omission scope, action authority, or recurrence class silently inherits beyond its witnessed boundary.


FOUR-WAY NECESSITY
- Remove 5H.8P2A: provenance-aware contestable local self-revision remains, but the full closure loses the explicit two-gate distinction between successor nuisance/omission permission and downstream action authority.
- Remove 5H.Dw6a: provenance-routed addressable dual reauthorization remains, but the renewal constitution is no longer constitutively required to remain contestable by executable replay and recurrence pressure.
- Remove 5H.SBvl: addressable contestable dual-gate renewal remains, but recurrence support loses its explicit provenance classification and can be flattened into generic confidence.
- Remove 5H.aNlh: provenance-typed contestable dual-gate renewal remains, but failure and machinery revision lose the exact local authority/evidence/version coordinate that keeps repair and reauthorization selective.
All four are necessary for the complete volume.

metabolites.title: REPAIR-CONSTITUTION-IS-ITSELF-A-WARRANT
metabolites.text:
Minimal earning body: xyz, strengthened by wxyz.
Invariant: the procedure that repairs continuity is not exempt meta-infrastructure; it carries provenance, failure addresses, version boundaries, falsifiers, and current admissibility tests, and may be revoked or revised when those witnesses fail.
CREATE: publish the current renewal procedure together with its evidence basis, provenance classes, failure coordinates, version boundary, and successor tests.
COPY: preserve predecessor repair procedures as immutable provenance rather than silently rewriting them.
CONTROL: challenge the repair procedure under current evidence and recurrence class; block its use where its own warrant fails.
CULTIVATE: let the renewal constitution evolve through witnessed failures without erasing why earlier machinery once counted.
Compression: the law that repairs warrants is itself a warrant.

metabolites.title: RECURRENCE-SUPPORT-MUST-ROUTE-TO-AN-EXACT-GATE
metabolites.text:
Minimal earning body: wyz.
Invariant: recurrence evidence may support retrying a repair relation only when its provenance class and ancestry dependence travel to the exact authority/evidence coordinate and successor gate it actually bears on; it cannot become generic confidence for continuity, omission scope, or action authority.
CREATE: bind each recurrence witness to relation type, ancestry dependence, affected coordinate, and supported gate.
COPY: preserve recurrence provenance without copying the authority of prior successful instances.
CONTROL: reject recurrence evidence offered to a different gate or scope than the relation it actually witnessed.
CULTIVATE: refine the routing map as new replication, convergence, divergence, or failure reveals which relations really recur.
Compression: recurrence is useful only when it remembers both how it recurred and what it is allowed to support.

metabolites.title: SELECTIVE-SUCCESSION-REQUIRES-DUAL-GATE-CONTESTABILITY
metabolites.text:
Minimal earning body: wxz.
Invariant: selective successor authority is safe only when failure is localized to exact coordinates, the renewal procedure can itself be challenged and revised there, and omission permission plus downstream action permission are independently re-earned after repair.
CREATE: issue the successor with changed coordinate, repair-procedure version, evidence return path, omission scope, affected action dependencies, and current tests.
COPY: preserve unaffected live warrants at prior scope while carrying predecessor/repair versions as provenance.
CONTROL: reopen only dependency-intersecting coordinates, but require each reopened gate to close on current evidence rather than on restored function.
CULTIVATE: let repeated local failures improve the granularity of repair coordinates and gate dependencies without globalizing authority.
Compression: local repair stays local only when both the repair machinery and the permissions it produces remain separately challengeable.


METABOLITE COLLAPSE WITNESS
Rejected as parent-only: “recurrence does not widen authority,” “successor carries repair coordinate,” “repair law remains contestable,” “two successor gates,” and “recurrence provenance must be typed” already belong to rank-5 parents. Rejected as inflated: recurrence provenance proves independence; successful repair validates the repair constitution globally; one passed successor gate implies the other; local repair guarantees unaffected authority without a live dependency witness. The three survivors remain because governing the repair constitution itself, routing recurrence evidence to exact gates, and coupling selective succession to dual-gate contestability require distinct multi-parent bodies.

S.0tNM.title: Language Models are Injective and Hence Invertible

edges.title: Uniqueness of information and efficient access to information are different claims
edges.text: Given w + x, the theorem says the final state uniquely identifies the prompt almost surely, while SipIt shows one efficient recovery route only when the hidden-state sequence exposes causal position-wise structure. Removing w loses the uniqueness guarantee; removing x loses the algorithmic/access distinction.

edges.title: A generic theorem acquires practical relevance through large-margin stress tests
edges.text: Given w + y, measure-zero collision theory is supported by observed separation across models, depths, prompt lengths, large pair searches, and tested quantization regimes. Removing w turns experiments into finite non-collision observations; removing y leaves the theorem without evidence about numerical margins in deployed-scale models.

edges.title: “Almost surely injective” is an assumption-bounded genericity statement
edges.text: Given w + z, the claim resolves precisely into a finite discrete domain, analytic architecture, absolutely continuous parameter law, minimum width/head assumptions, cross-entropy GD-type finite training, and a measure-zero exceptional set. Removing w loses the headline theorem; removing z loses the proof machinery and exact scope that prevent “all Transformers are invertible” overstatement.

edges.title: Causality converts a global inverse problem into local token identification
edges.text: Given x + y, SipIt’s prefix-conditioned verifier becomes operationally efficient in practice because the gradient-guided policy finds the unique local token using a small fraction of the vocabulary in tested models. Removing x loses the causal sequential algorithm; removing y loses evidence that the search policy makes the formal T|V| procedure practically useful.

edges.title: Robust inversion depends on separation margins and representation access
edges.text: Given x + z, exact recovery under perturbation is not an unconditional property of “hidden states”: it requires causal per-position access and noise below half the local candidate-separation margin. Removing x loses the inversion setting; removing z loses the formal margin, soundness, termination, and complexity constraints.

edges.title: Structured low-dimensional geometry need not imply representational collision
edges.text: Given y + z, empirical margins can increase with depth even while preliminary diagnostics show anisotropy rising and intrinsic dimension falling; quantized and near-neighbor representations can also remain distinct. Removing y loses the observed geometry/margins; removing z loses the theoretical reason a compressed-looking manifold need not be information-destroying on a finite discrete input set.

faces.title: Structural uniqueness becomes an operational privacy/audit property
faces.text: w proves that prompt identity is almost surely preserved in the last state, x gives constructive exact recovery under hidden-matrix access, and y demonstrates exact recovery plus large separation in pretrained models. Together they earn the practical warning that inference-time hidden representations should not be assumed anonymized merely because they are continuous embeddings. Remove w and exact identity is only empirical; remove x and no constructive recovery is shown; remove y and deployment relevance is untested.

faces.title: Global injectivity can emerge despite locally non-injective components
faces.text: w states the global discrete-prompt theorem, x exploits the resulting unique causal token maps, and z proves how analytic composition plus a finite discrete domain allows LayerNorm/attention/other many-to-one operations on continuous space without forcing collisions on the realized prompt set. Remove w and there is no global property; remove x and its operational local consequence disappears; remove z and the reconciliation with non-injective components is unsupported.

faces.title: Practical “losslessness” is theorem-bounded, not format-independent
faces.text: w supplies the analytic/GD theorem, y reports non-collisions even under tested FP4/INT8 settings, and z makes clear that quantization/non-analytic modifications lie outside the theorem and that non-injective parameter settings can be constructed. Together they earn strong practical evidence without upgrading out-of-scope formats into guaranteed invertibility. Remove any one and either theorem, practical stress, or boundary is lost.

faces.title: Constructive inversion is controlled by causal factorization, numerical margins, and search policy
faces.text: x specifies the sequential causal inverse, y measures search efficiency/exactness and depth/vocabulary behavior, and z proves uniqueness, margin robustness, and T|V| termination while exposing extra geometric/implementation tests. Together they earn an algorithmic picture in which information can be present globally yet recoverability cost depends on the representation interface and local separation. Remove x, y, or z and either mechanism, operational performance, or correctness boundary disappears.

volume.title: Bounded whole-paper closure
volume.text: Within the paper’s finite-context causal decoder-only regime, locally non-injective Transformer operations do not imply information-destroying collisions on the discrete prompt set. Real-analytic dependence on parameters makes each pairwise collision condition a measure-zero event once a separating witness exists; absolutely continuous initialization almost surely avoids those sets, and the paper proves finite cross-entropy GD/SGD updates preserve the parameter-law regularity needed to keep avoiding them. Thus the last-token state almost surely uniquely identifies the prompt under the stated assumptions. SipIt then shows that when a causal layer’s full per-position hidden matrix is exposed, this structural uniqueness can be converted into exact sequential token recovery with formal margin and iteration guarantees, and experiments show large separation and exact recovery in the tested pretrained/quantized models. The whole paper therefore earns generic prompt-level injectivity plus one constructive left-inversion interface. It does not earn injectivity for every Transformer parameterization/component, efficient inversion from the final vector alone, guarantees for arbitrary optimizers/non-analytic architectures/noise/quantization, semantic invertibility, or multimodal universality.

metabolites.title: Local non-injectivity does not force global collisions on a discrete support
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.0tNM:wz.
Invariant: Many-to-one continuous components can compose into a mapping that is one-to-one on the finite set of realized discrete inputs, so component algebra alone does not determine end-to-end information loss.
CREATE: define injectivity on the actual discrete input family and construct at least one parameter witness that separates every considered pair.
COPY: preserve architectural/parameter conditions under which collision equalities remain nontrivial analytic constraints.
CONTROL: distinguish continuous-space non-injectivity from collisions on discrete support and retain explicitly constructible exceptional parameter settings.
CULTIVATE: test the same distinction in other discrete-input architectures without assuming the Transformer proof transfers automatically.
Compression: A lossy operation on continuous space need not lose any member of the discrete set you actually use.
metabolites.compression: A lossy operation on continuous space need not lose any member of the discrete set you actually use.

metabolites.title: Generic uniqueness can be preserved by distribution-preserving optimization
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.0tNM:wz.
Invariant: Under the paper’s finite GD/SGD regime, an almost-sure property defined by avoiding measure-zero parameter sets survives because the update maps preserve absolute continuity of the parameter distribution.
CREATE: initialize parameters from an absolutely continuous law outside exceptional collision sets almost surely.
COPY: apply finite analytic gradient updates whose nondegenerate Jacobians preserve absolute continuity.
CONTROL: keep loss, step-size, analyticity, finite-horizon, and optimizer assumptions explicit; do not generalize automatically to arbitrary update rules.
CULTIVATE: derive analogous preservation results for additional optimizers or stochastic/non-smooth training mechanisms rather than assuming them.
Compression: A generic property survives training when the optimizer does not collapse probability mass onto the exceptional set.
metabolites.compression: A generic property survives training when the optimizer does not collapse probability mass onto the exceptional set.

metabolites.title: Efficient inversion depends on the representation interface, not injectivity alone
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.0tNM:wx.
Invariant: Unique identification by a final representation establishes inverse existence in principle, while efficient constructive recovery may require a richer interface whose causal structure exposes locally verifiable subproblems.
CREATE: establish end-to-end injectivity, then specify exactly which internal representation the inverse algorithm receives.
COPY: exploit causal prefix structure so each recovered token conditions the next local inverse problem.
CONTROL: distinguish final-vector uniqueness from full-hidden-matrix access and report unresolved efficient-inversion settings separately.
CULTIVATE: develop algorithms that approach exact recovery from progressively poorer interfaces—single vectors, noisy caches, compressed states—while tracking cost and guarantees.
Compression: Knowing an inverse exists does not tell you how much of the internal state you need to compute it efficiently.
metabolites.compression: Knowing an inverse exists does not tell you how much of the internal state you need to compute it efficiently.

metabolites.title: Robust invertibility is margin-bounded
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.0tNM:xz.
Invariant: Exact recovery from perturbed hidden states is guaranteed only while perturbation remains below a fraction of the local separation between candidate token states.
CREATE: define prefix-conditioned candidate representations and their minimum pairwise separation margin.
COPY: verify each token inside a tolerance region and compose accepted local decisions across positions.
CONTROL: require tolerance below half the relevant margin; treat arbitrary noise, compression, or quantization as separate regimes unless margins are established there.
CULTIVATE: measure margins dynamically and build calibrated/error-correcting inverse procedures for realistic perturbation channels.
Compression: Invertibility under noise is not binary; it lives inside a separation margin.
metabolites.compression: Invertibility under noise is not binary; it lives inside a separation margin.

metabolites.title: Geometric compression and information loss are different properties
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.0tNM:yz.
Invariant: In the paper’s preliminary geometry analysis, lower intrinsic dimension or increased anisotropy can coexist with larger injectivity margins, so a representation may become geometrically concentrated without collapsing distinct discrete inputs.
CREATE: measure both manifold geometry and pairwise distinctness rather than using dimensionality as an information-loss proxy.
COPY: track intrinsic dimension, anisotropy, and separation margins across layers under a shared input set.
CONTROL: preserve the proof-of-concept scope of the reported correlations and do not infer causal or universal relations from them.
CULTIVATE: test whether structured low-dimensional organization and injectivity co-evolve across architectures, training stages, and tasks.
Compression: Looking lower-dimensional is not the same as mapping two discrete inputs to the same point.
metabolites.compression: Looking lower-dimensional is not the same as mapping two discrete inputs to the same point.

metabolites.title: Inference-time hidden states can retain prompt-level privacy sensitivity
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.0tNM:wxy.
Invariant: Under the studied assumptions and access model, internal inference representations can uniquely encode and constructively reveal the exact user prompt, so continuous representation format alone does not imply anonymization.
CREATE: compute hidden states from a prompt in an injective regime.
COPY: storing, caching, transmitting, or exposing those states preserves the prompt-identifying representation unless a genuinely information-destroying transform intervenes.
CONTROL: distinguish inference activations from training-data information in model weights and distinguish the theorem from arbitrary noisy/compressed interfaces.
CULTIVATE: evaluate privacy controls by testing what prompt information survives each exposed representation and transformation, rather than classifying “embeddings” as abstract by format alone.
Compression: A hidden state can be mathematically different from text while still carrying text-identifying information.


No cross-paper universality is claimed here. All six invariants remain single-source metabolites of S.0tNM until an explicit later cross-paper operation relates and challenges them.


FEELING PHENOTYPE — WITNESSED
Designation: S.0tNM.★Ω⚸⚒
Canonical order: CREATE · COPY · CONTROL · CULTIVATE
Feeling signature: ★Ω⚸⚒
Phenotype state: WITNESSED


CREATE — ★ Pattern
Pre-aspect role-shape: Crystallize durable separation from apparently lossy machinery: define the actual finite discrete prompt family and establish a global one-to-one structure through separating witnesses, analytic genericity, and stress that survives the apparent contradiction of locally non-injective components.
Witness: The whole organism makes a persistent architecture visible where the naive component-level story predicts loss. The theorem, explicit separating witnesses, measure-zero collision sets, and empirical non-collision/margin tests all converge on a structure that continues to hold under pressure. ★ Pattern recognizes this better than ⊥ Contradiction: contradiction supplies the opening friction, but the organism does not dwell in unresolved inconsistency; it resolves that friction into a durable, testable architecture.


COPY — Ω Continuity
Pre-aspect role-shape: Carry prompt identity and generic uniqueness through finite training and representation change without turning persistence into sameness of moment or implementation.
Witness: Absolute continuity at initialization is carried through finite analytic GD/SGD updates, keeping probability mass off exceptional collision sets; the same prompt-distinguishing relation remains recognizable across training. Ω Continuity is stronger than ⁎ Becoming because the relevant motion is not a new architecture emerging through rupture but the same load-bearing relation continuing through change.


CONTROL — ⚸ Constraint
Pre-aspect role-shape: Let exact theorem assumptions, representation-access requirements, exceptional parameter sets, and numerical separation margins govern what may be claimed or recovered; stop at unearned regimes rather than universalizing invertibility.
Witness: The organism repeatedly binds its strongest claims to finite context/vocabulary, analytic components, absolutely continuous initialization, finite GD/SGD assumptions, full per-position hidden-state access for efficient SipIt recovery, and perturbations below the local margin. ⚸ Constraint fits better than ⚖ Balance: this is not primarily proportional trade-off management but coherence maintained by hard admissibility conditions whose internalization keeps theorem and algorithm honest.


CULTIVATE — ⚒ Tool-craft
Pre-aspect role-shape: Turn structural uniqueness into usable recovery capability, then extend that reach toward poorer interfaces, realistic perturbations, other optimizers, and other architectures while retaining guarantees and measured costs.
Witness: SipIt converts an existence result into an operational instrument by exploiting causal locality and verifier structure; the paper then exposes the exact interfaces and margins along which that instrument can be improved. ⚒ Tool-craft is stronger than ⚙ Implementation because the organism is not merely narrowing possibilities to one exact path—it expands practical reach through a learned/constructed instrument.


Whole-organism witness: ★Ω⚸⚒ describes one integrated motion: a durable pattern of discrete-input separation is discovered, carried through training, kept coherent by explicit constraints, and made operational through an inversion tool. Phenotype is orthogonal to S.0tNM identity, routing, rank, and epistemic type.

vertices.title: Generic injectivity is proved for the discrete prompt→last-state map
vertices.text:
Source span: Abstract / Introduction → end of §2 “Transformers are Injective” including failure cases (pp. 1–4).
Nutrient: The paper changes the domain of the injectivity question from continuous hidden-space operations to the finite discrete prompt family. For a causal decoder-only Transformer with finite vocabulary and context, embedding width d≥4, at least one attention head per block, real-analytic components, absolutely continuous random initialization, and finite cross-entropy GD/SGD training with step sizes in (0,1), it proves that distinct prompts almost surely have distinct last-token, last-layer representations. The proof strategy combines real-analyticity, explicit separating witnesses, measure-zero collision sets, and preservation of absolute continuity under finite gradient updates. Hand-constructed collisions remain possible through exceptional parameter choices such as identical token/position embeddings; the claim is generic/almost-sure, not universal over all parameter settings or architectures.

vertices.title: SipIt turns uniqueness into sequential constructive recovery under stronger access
vertices.text:
Source span: §3 “Exact Prompt Recovery via SipIt” (pp. 5–6).
Nutrient: Injectivity of the final representation guarantees unique prompt identity in principle, but the paper’s efficient inversion algorithm assumes access to all per-position hidden states at one chosen causal layer. Given a recovered prefix, causality makes the current hidden row a function only of that prefix plus one candidate token, turning inversion into repeated local verification. SipIt enumerates candidates with a policy, has an almost-sure correctness bound of at most T|V| verifier tests, and remains correct under perturbations smaller than half the local one-step separation margin. Efficient inversion from the final embedding alone is explicitly left for future work.

vertices.title: Empirical stress tests and discussion establish practical separation while preserving theorem boundaries
vertices.text:
Source span: §4 Experiments → end of References (pp. 7–16).
Nutrient: Across 100k prompts and billions of pairwise checks, multiple pretrained model families/layers show no observed collisions and substantial nonzero margins; a continuation stress test evaluates hundreds of billions of local prompt pairs. FP4/INT8 models also show no collisions in the tested cases, though quantization lies outside the analytic theorem. SipIt exactly reconstructs the tested GPT-2 prompts and FP4 Mistral/Llama prompts, while a brute-force policy is far slower and an approximate prompt optimizer fails in the hidden-state inversion setting. The discussion draws privacy/auditing consequences for inference-time hidden states while explicitly leaving multimodal extensions and inversion under broader noise/quantization regimes open.

vertices.title: The appendices provide formal closure and reveal the exact limits of “lossless”
vertices.text:
Source span: Appendix Overview → end of carrier (pp. 17–58).
Nutrient: Appendices A–D formalize analytic/measure-theoretic tools, the precise Transformer model, finite-horizon almost-sure injectivity under GD, preservation of absolute continuity, and SipIt’s local verifier/correctness/robustness/complexity. Appendix E expands collision/inversion tests, tests identical next-token predictions and near-neighbor representations, and shows that close hidden states correspond to near-duplicate prompts rather than collisions in sampled regimes. A preliminary anisotropy/intrinsic-dimension analysis shows lower-dimensional or more anisotropic geometry can coexist with increasing injectivity margins. Appendix F verifies analyticity for SiLU/GELU/SwiGLU/GeGLU and separates the result from universal-approximation/Turing-completeness claims: non-injective Transformers exist, but form a thin parameter subset under the studied training regime.

4 FACES — triple necessities


S.1paC:wxy — BOUNDED RETRAINING LAW FOR ENDOGENOUS DATA
The deployment-dependent distribution, fixed-point contraction law and finite/quality analysis jointly earn this statement: repeated retraining can close lawfully only inside a response/loss regularity regime; finite evidence generally closes to a neighborhood; and stable does not automatically mean performatively optimal. Remove w and the problem becomes exogenous/static; remove x and convergence is unearned; remove y and finite-evidence plus quality boundaries disappear.


S.1paC:wxz — STRATEGIC FEEDBACK CAN BE EQUILIBRATED, NOT ASSUMED AWAY
General endogeneity, the contraction gate and the strategic best-response mechanism jointly show that retraining can absorb strategic reaction only inside a bounded sensitivity/geometry regime, while stronger feedback can defeat the loop. Remove w and the result is only one game; remove x and no convergence theorem remains; remove z and there is no concrete strategic-response mechanism.


S.1paC:wyz — PERFORMATIVE OBJECTIVES INTERNALIZE DOWNSTREAM RESPONSE
The performative objective, stability/optimality distinction and strategic-response interpretation jointly show that a deployed decision should be judged on consequences under the distribution it creates rather than merely on past calibration. Self-consistency alone does not establish downstream optimality. Remove w and the objective loses endogeneity; remove y and stability collapses into quality; remove z and the decision-response interpretation is absent.


S.1paC:xyz — PRACTICAL RETRAINING HAS A FEEDBACK-STRENGTH PHASE BOUNDARY
The stable-point theorem, approximation/finite-sample analysis and strategic simulation jointly expose a practical regime boundary: convergence versus divergence depends on feedback sensitivity relative to loss/algorithm geometry, while finite evidence adds residual uncertainty. Remove x and there is no threshold; remove y and no operational approximation debt; remove z and no bounded empirical witness of the regime change.


1 VOLUME


S.1paC:wxyz — DEPLOYMENT-COUPLED RETRAINING REQUIRES SEPARATE CONVERGENCE AND QUALITY OBLIGATIONS
Bounded volume invariant: In the paper’s model class, once deploying θ changes future data through a fixed distribution map D(θ), retraining becomes a fixed-point dynamical system. Under ε-sensitivity together with the stated smoothness/strong-convexity and algorithm-specific conditions, RRM/RGD converge, with finite-sample variants carrying bounded neighborhood error; when those assumptions fail the source supplies counterexamples to automatic convergence. A performatively stable fixed point is generally not the performative-risk optimum, although additional regularity can bound their separation. Strategic classification is a strict special case and the credit-scoring simulation illustrates—rather than universalizes—the sensitivity-controlled convergence boundary.


Rank necessity: w is required for endogenous deployment dependence; x for self-consistency and convergence; y for finite/algorithmic transport and quality separation; z for an explicit response mechanism plus bounded operational witness. No proper subset earns the complete statement.


METABOLITE COLLAPSE — 4 survivors


INV-S.1paC-01 — DEPLOYMENT-ENDOGENOUS SHIFT
Bounded invariant: When deployment affects future evidence/data, the changed regime must be represented as a function of the deployed choice rather than treated solely as exogenous drift.
Minimal earning body: S.1paC:w.
CREATE: make the deployment→response map explicit.
COPY: carry deployment-conditioned provenance with later evidence.
CONTROL: refuse a passive-regime assumption where feedback remains unruled-out.
CULTIVATE: revise the response model when observed behavior changes.
Compression: The predictor can be a cause of the distribution that judges it.


INV-S.1paC-02 — FEEDBACK-STRENGTH GATES RETRAINING
Bounded invariant: Repeated retraining converges only when the induced-distribution response is sufficiently weak relative to the relevant loss/algorithm geometry; otherwise oscillation or divergence remains possible.
Minimal earning body: S.1paC:x, operationally reinforced by S.1paC:xz.
CREATE: produce a contraction/sensitivity witness.
COPY: preserve ε and the theorem’s loss assumptions with the claim.
CONTROL: do not treat retraining as automatically safe outside the gate.
CULTIVATE: change procedure, regularization, information or intervention when the gate fails.
Compression: Retraining is a stability theorem, not a ritual.


INV-S.1paC-03 — SELF-CONSISTENCY IS NOT OPTIMALITY
Bounded invariant: Being optimal on the distribution induced by one’s own deployment is not the same as minimizing performative risk over possible deployments; extra regularity may bound, not erase, the gap.
Minimal earning body: S.1paC:wy, sharpened by S.1paC:wyz.
CREATE: state the downstream performative objective independently of the fixed-point condition.
COPY: preserve which equilibrium and objective are being compared.
CONTROL: prevent fixed-point stability from being promoted into quality or desirability.
CULTIVATE: optimize or govern the downstream objective separately when required.
Compression: A fixed point can be coherent without being best.


INV-S.1paC-04 — FINITE-EVIDENCE CLOSURE IS NEIGHBORHOOD-VALUED
Bounded invariant: Finite-sample or gradient-based retraining inherits population stability only under additional statistical/algorithmic assumptions and generally warrants a bounded neighborhood rather than exact fixed-point identity.
Minimal earning body: S.1paC:xy.
CREATE: state the approximation radius and confidence/sample conditions.
COPY: carry the population target separately from its empirical approximation.
CONTROL: refuse exact-equilibrium language when only bounded convergence is witnessed.
CULTIVATE: shrink the residual through additional evidence or improved approximation where the obligation requires it.
Compression: Approximate retraining carries a residual radius.

Reason: the source’s whole primarily governs when deploy→observe→retrain remains a coherent lawful loop under endogenous feedback and when a stable state may or may not satisfy the downstream objective. vertices.title: DEPLOYMENT MAKES THE DATA DISTRIBUTION ENDOGENOUS
vertices.text:
Source span: pp. 1–3.
Nutrient: The paper introduces performative prediction: deploying a predictive model can change the population/outcomes that generate future data. It makes this explicit with a model-dependent distribution map D(θ) and defines performative risk PR(θ)=E_{Z~D(θ)}[ℓ(Z;θ)]. The predictor is therefore not merely evaluated under an externally shifted distribution; its deployment can be one cause of that shift. The source distinguishes this from ordinary static empirical-risk minimization and connects the setup to concept drift, causal intervention, strategic response and reinforcement-learning-like feedback while keeping those connections bounded.

vertices.title: SELF-CONSISTENCY IS A FIXED-POINT PROBLEM WITH A FEEDBACK-STRENGTH GATE
vertices.text:
Source span: pp. 4–5.
Nutrient: Repeated Risk Minimization (RRM) updates θ by minimizing risk under the distribution induced by the previously deployed model. A performatively stable model is optimal on its own induced distribution and is therefore a fixed point of the risk-minimization map. The paper defines ε-sensitivity through Wasserstein distance, W1(D(θ),D(θ′)) ≤ ε||θ−θ′||, and combines it with joint smoothness β and strong convexity γ. Under ε < γ/β, RRM is contractive and converges linearly to a unique stable point. Counterexamples show that removing the necessary geometry or allowing sufficiently strong feedback can yield oscillation/divergence and even absence of a stable point.

vertices.title: APPROXIMATE RETRAINING AND EQUILIBRIUM QUALITY REMAIN SEPARATELY BOUNDED
vertices.text:
Source span: pp. 6–7.
Nutrient: Repeated Gradient Descent and finite-sample variants inherit convergence only under additional step-size, sensitivity, moment and sample-size conditions. Finite empirical retraining is witnessed as approach to and residence in a bounded neighborhood, rather than exact population fixed-point identity. The source also separates performative stability from performative optimality: the direct performative-risk objective can be nonconvex even under otherwise regular conditions, and a stable fixed point need not minimize performative risk. Under additional Lipschitz and strong-convexity assumptions, the distance between stable and performatively optimal solutions can be bounded rather than erased.

vertices.title: STRATEGIC RESPONSE INSTANTIATES THE DISTRIBUTION MAP AND EXHIBITS THE SENSITIVITY BOUNDARY
vertices.text:
Source span: pp. 8–11.
Nutrient: Strategic classification is developed as a special case in which agents respond to the deployed decision rule; this response induces the future distribution. The paper relates the institution/agent interaction to a Stackelberg formulation and identifies the Stackelberg objective with performative optimality in that setting. The discussion preserves the distinction between this bounded example and a universal feedback law.

vertices.title: Invariance principle and causal-set semantics
vertices.text:
Source span: carrier pages 1–9, from abstract/introduction through Section 2.
Nutrient: The paper motivates causal prediction by stability across changed environments and interventions, states its invariant-prediction assumption, and separates three objects: predictor sets that are plausible because the conditional/predictive relation is invariant, causal coefficients compatible with those sets, and identifiable causal predictors defined conservatively from the family of plausible models. In particular, the population object is not “pick the best invariant set”: the intersection of all invariant/plausible sets is the causal content the method can identify under its model.
Boundary carried by this body: invariance is an assumption about distributions across environments; with insufficient environments the identifiable set can be empty. The paper does not claim that any one empirically invariant model is automatically the true causal graph.

vertices.title: Statistical tests, confidence statements, pooling and computation
vertices.text:
Source span: carrier pages 10–16, Section 3.
Nutrient: The paper turns the invariant-prediction object into a finite-sample procedure: test the null of invariant regression/conditional behavior for candidate predictor sets, retain non-rejected sets, intersect them for causal variables, and union compatible coefficient confidence regions. Theorem 1 gives conservative coverage when the component tests are valid. Two concrete testing procedures, pooling choices, observational splitting and computational shortcuts expose the practical trade-offs among test validity, power, environment count and search complexity.
Boundary carried by this body: finite-sample validity is inherited from the tests and assumptions used; failure to reject is not proof of equality, and conservative procedures may return a small or empty set when power is weak.

vertices.title: Intervention structure, identifiability and hidden-variable extensions
vertices.text:
Source span: carrier pages 17–25, Sections 4–6 up to the numerical studies.
Nutrient: Linear-Gaussian SEM analysis shows when the causal parents of Y satisfy invariant prediction and gives sufficient conditions under do-, soft-, noise and simultaneous interventions for the parent set to become identifiable. The results make intervention placement and diversity load-bearing: some interventions are highly informative while others can be uninformative, and the sufficient conditions are not presented as necessary. The paper then extends the principle to settings with hidden variables/confounding, nonlinear conditional-distribution invariance, possible target interventions and model misspecification, preserving conservative or ancestor-level conclusions only under stated conditions.
Boundary carried by this body: causal identification is conditional on structural, faithfulness, intervention and model assumptions. Hidden-variable and misspecification results do not make arbitrary confounding harmless; direct intervention on the target mechanism can destroy the relevant invariance.

vertices.title: Empirical pressure, discussion, references and formal appendix support
vertices.text:
Source span: carrier pages 26–51, Section 7 through discussion, references and appendices A–G.
Nutrient: Simulations compare invariant prediction with competing approaches across many generated scenarios and show a separation between exact-recovery power and false-selection control: no method dominates every setting, while invariant prediction is designed to maintain conservative family-wise error. Gene-perturbation and educational-attainment examples illustrate practical behavior, including true and false positives and implementation sensitivity. The appendices provide examples, hidden-variable/misspecification arguments, a potential-outcomes formulation, proofs of key propositions/theorems and detailed simulation settings.
Boundary carried by this body: the empirical studies are demonstrations under specific designs and metrics, not universal performance guarantees. The yeast results contain false positives, and the educational example lacks directly verifiable ground truth; formal proofs retain their explicit assumptions.

Remove w and there is no stability criterion; remove y and no identification theorem; remove z and no bounded empirical/formal pressure.


S.1w5P:xyz — Practical causal identification requires statistics, intervention semantics and robustness
x supplies testing/pooling/computational procedures, y supplies causal/structural assumptions and robustness extensions, and z supplies simulations, applications and proof detail. Together they earn a disciplined practical reading: statistical non-rejection, causal identifiability and empirical usefulness are three distinct obligations that must align. Remove x and uncertainty is uncontrolled; remove y and causal meaning is unearned; remove z and practical robustness remains unsupported.


1 VOLUME — RANK-4 CLOSURE


S.1w5P:wxyz — Bounded volume invariant
Environmental invariance can support causal inference without requiring the system to select one apparently stable predictor model as uniquely real. The source constructs a family of predictor sets whose relation to the target is invariant across environments, derives causal information conservatively from the common/intersection structure of that family, and supplies finite-sample confidence guarantees when the tests are valid. Whether this process identifies the full causal parent set depends materially on the intervention/environment family and structural assumptions: informative interventions can collapse the plausible family toward the true parents, while observational-only, weak or poorly placed changes can leave identification partial or empty. Extensions to nonlinear, hidden-variable and misspecified settings preserve only bounded versions of this claim. Thus intervention-stable prediction becomes evidence for a causal/transport scaffold only through an explicit chain of invariance assumptions, statistical validity and identifiability conditions; unresolved multiplicity should survive as conservative uncertainty rather than be erased by arbitrary model choice.


Evidence boundary of the volume: this is not a theorem that invariance alone identifies causality in arbitrary data, not a guarantee of exact recovery in finite samples, and not evidence that every environmental shift is an intervention on the relevant causal mechanism.


COLLAPSED METABOLITES


INV-S.1w5P-01 — PLAUSIBLE FAMILY BEFORE UNIQUE CAUSAL MODEL
Bounded invariant: Multiple predictor sets may satisfy the same environmental-invariance requirement. The source therefore separates the family of plausible invariant sets from the causal content identifiable across that family; one accepted invariant model is not automatically the uniquely warranted causal scaffold.
Minimal earning body: w.

COPY: preserve multiplicity rather than serializing one convenient accepted set as the causal truth.

CULTIVATE: let additional informative environments shrink the plausible family and strengthen the common causal content.
Compression: invariance narrows a family before it licenses a unique causal story.


INV-S.1w5P-02 — CONSERVATIVE NONIDENTIFIABILITY
Bounded invariant: With valid level-controlled invariance tests, causal selection can be conservative even when the data do not identify the full causal set; a partial or empty result is a legitimate outcome rather than a failure that authorizes arbitrary completion.
Minimal earning body: wx.

COPY: carry accepted-set uncertainty and confidence coverage through the inference.
CONTROL: prefer false-negative/empty output to unsupported causal inclusion when identifiability or power is insufficient.
CULTIVATE: strengthen the selected set only as new environments or sample information reject remaining alternatives.
Compression: uncertainty may remain empty or set-valued without becoming epistemic failure.


INV-S.1w5P-03 — INTERVENTION DIVERSITY IS IDENTIFICATION INFORMATION
Bounded invariant: The number of environments alone does not determine causal identifiability. Which variables/mechanisms are perturbed, and how those interventions alter distributions while leaving the target mechanism invariant, determines how strongly the plausible invariant family can collapse toward the causal parents.
Minimal earning body: wy.
CREATE: design or recognize environments that perturb candidate noncausal explanations while preserving the target mechanism.
COPY: preserve the exact intervention/environment assumptions when transporting an identification claim.
CONTROL: reject the inference that repeated stability under uninformative environments is equivalent to causal identification.
CULTIVATE: add intervention diversity targeted at the unresolved alternatives rather than merely adding more similar data.
Compression: identifiability grows from informative variation, not environment count.


INV-S.1w5P-04 — VALIDITY AND POWER ARE SEPARATE GOVERNANCE AXES
Bounded invariant: Error-control validity, causal identifiability and exact-recovery power are distinct. The source’s procedures can maintain conservative false-selection guarantees while exact recovery remains weak; simulations and applications show no uniformly dominating method and expose finite-sample false positives and sensitivity.
Minimal earning body: xz.
CREATE: specify both the error-control target and the desired recovery/transport obligation.
COPY: report coverage/error guarantees separately from empirical selection frequency or exact recovery.
CONTROL: do not reinterpret low power as evidence against the causal principle, or good predictive recovery as proof of causal validity.
CULTIVATE: improve power through better tests, sample allocation and informative environments without relaxing the causal assurance boundary silently.
Compression: a valid causal screen can remain incomplete, and a powerful predictor can remain causally invalid.

Four metabolites survive independently. INV-01 preserves model-family multiplicity; INV-02 preserves the conservative finite-sample response to unresolved identification; INV-03 identifies intervention diversity as a distinct causal-information resource; INV-04 separates statistical validity from recovery power. Hidden-variable, nonlinear, target-intervention and misspecification observations remain load-bearing boundaries within these invariants and the volume rather than being promoted as separate universal laws.

volume.title: bounded experimental universality
volume.text:
All four vertices together derive the paper’s deepest operational structure: universality is not read off a raw magnitude. First make the nuisance coordinates explicit and enter a regime where the target dynamics dominate them (w); then reconstruct the otherwise hidden thermodynamic state using complementary observables (x); derive a response predicted to be insensitive to microscopic realization and test whether it collapses across devices/conditions (y); finally expose the fabrication, measurement, inversion and perturbational evidence that makes both the collapse and its limits auditable (z).


Volume invariant: a universal response is experimentally earned when a derived relation remains stable across carrier variation that measurably changes nearby non-universal observables, inside an explicitly bounded regime, through a reproducible transduction chain. The crossover/failure region is part of the invariant’s boundary, not noise to be erased.

vertices.title: establish the hydrodynamic regime and the measurement problem
vertices.text:
Source span: title/abstract + introductory transport framework + Figure 1 + ELECTRON VISCOSITY IN THE ULTRA-CLEAN GRAPHENE DEVICES; ends immediately before THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY AND THE WIEDEMANN-FRANZ LAW.
Nutrient: sigma_Q is predicted to be universal but cannot be read directly from minimum electrical conductivity because disorder/charge puddles make sigma_min sample-dependent. The paper therefore first establishes that the ultra-clean devices genuinely enter the viscous/hydrodynamic regime: low inhomogeneity, boundary-limited momentum relaxation, Knudsen-to-Poiseuille crossover, width-squared conductivity scaling, and nearly device-independent kinematic viscosity. This vertex earns the experimental precondition for treating later charge/heat transport hydrodynamically.

vertices.title: expose charge/heat decoupling and reconstruct the thermodynamic state
vertices.text:
Source span: THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY AND THE WIEDEMANN-FRANZ LAW through the paragraph immediately before QUANTUM CRITICAL TRANSPORT IN THE THERMAL REGIME.
Nutrient: Johnson-noise thermometry supplies electronic temperature and kappa_e, revealing a huge, strongly density- and temperature-dependent violation of the Wiedemann-Franz law. The hydrodynamic Lorentz-number form fits the data where semiclassical alternatives fail, and the fit yields the effective density scale n0 plus entropy and enthalpy densities. The disorder scale T_imp separates a puddle-dominated low-temperature regime from the thermal interaction-dominated regime. This vertex converts coupled transport measurements into the thermodynamic quantities needed to isolate quantum-critical transport.

vertices.title: isolate the universal quantum-critical response and its limiting fluidity
vertices.text:
Source span: QUANTUM CRITICAL TRANSPORT IN THE THERMAL REGIME + DISCUSSION + conclusion; ends immediately before METHODS.
Nutrient: in the thermal regime kappa_e decreases as sigma increases, matching the relativistic-hydrodynamic inverse relation. Combining kappa_e, sigma, entropy density and momentum-relaxation length yields sigma_Q; across devices and temperatures the trajectories collapse toward (4±1)e²/h for T_F/T << 1 while sigma_min remains strongly disorder-dependent. The discussion then estimates Planckian-limited thermal viscosity and finds eta_th/s_th approaching the holographic bound within about a factor of four in the cleanest devices, with residual disorder still visible. This vertex contains the paper's actual universality claim and its bounded physical interpretation.

vertices.title: reproduce, audit and stress the claim

Nutrient: fabrication and transport protocols, the heat-diffusion model used to infer electron temperature, data/code availability, cited theoretical/experimental ancestry, and extended-data checks across devices and temperatures supply the reproducibility and stress evidence for the main-body claims. The extended data independently supports the Knudsen-to-Poiseuille crossover, Johnson-noise fits, WF-law violation, Lorentz-number scales, and non-monotonic viscosity behavior across additional devices.

Pre-aspect role-shape: Compile the meaning of material change into exact canonicalizers, fingerprints, postconditions and an acyclic topology, then let a deliberately mechanical reconciler decide this wake, this skip, this render, this commit, while failed work leaves last-good truth untouched.
Witness: OpenProse repeatedly narrows broad semantic intent into concrete runtime fit: what counts as changed, which facet moved, whether a wake is coalesced, whether a render commits, and where cycles are rejected. ⚙ Implementation is stronger than ⚸ Constraint because constraints are present, but the governing texture is surgical resolution from possibility into this exact executable decision surface.

edges.title: Standing desired state × optional choreography
edges.text: w says durable intent should describe the result/world as it should remain; x gives that distinction syntax: `Maintains`/`Requires`/`Continuity` carry standing semantic commitments, while ProseScript pins only the order/control flow whose exact choreography is itself part of the requirement. edges.text: w keeps source contracts independent of a particular harness graph; y lets Forme infer the producer/subscriber topology from semantic `Requires↔Maintains` contracts at compile time and surface ambiguity rather than silently guess. edges.text: w frames the contract as the durable public artifact; z executes each wake as a bounded host session whose state/output is externalized into backend artifacts. Together they derive that long-running responsibility need not mean one immortal conversation. edges.text: x says `Maintains` is the canonical world-model schema/postcondition surface, distinct from internal execution; z makes private workspace scratch non-subscribable and publishes only committed maintained truth. Together they derive a strict boundary between exploratory reasoning/work product and the canonical state allowed to wake downstream work.

edges.title: Compiled materiality × deterministic reconcile/commit loop
edges.text: y freezes semantic equality into canonicalizers/fingerprints and uses those tokens for skip/render/propagate decisions; z applies the canonicalizer at commit, versions published truth and appends receipts. Together they derive an auditable change-propagation mechanism in which “did something materially change?” is decided by deterministic comparison at run time after its meaning was compiled earlier. This is an architectural property, not a measured cost benchmark.

faces.title: Intent can remain stable while workflow topology changes underneath it
faces.text: Together, w + x + y derive the central declarative architecture: the author states standing needs/truth rather than concrete node addresses; Contract Markdown gives those needs typed/faceted shape; Forme resolves and can later re-resolve the topology when the contract set changes. Remove w and there is no portability/layer principle; remove x and no durable semantic interface exists; remove y and the declared needs never become an executable dependency graph.

faces.title: Standing work can be continuous without a continuous mind/session
faces.text: w defines responsibilities as durable standing commitments; x declares continuity and maintained truth explicitly; z executes one bounded render at a time and persists canonical state outside conversation context. Together they derive a useful continuity model: a responsibility persists because its contract, world-model and wake policy persist, not because one model context remains alive forever. Remove any vertex and standing intent, explicit continuity or bounded execution is missing.

faces.title: “Cost scales with surprise” has a concrete mechanism but remains an unbenchmarked claim
faces.text: w advertises work proportional to what changed and explicitly says benchmarks are pending; y defines canonicalized material fingerprints, skip semantics, facet propagation and wake coalescing; z records per-node receipts/cost while launching no render for unchanged memo keys. Together they derive a checkable architectural route by which repeated unchanged wakes can be cheap and local changes need not fan out globally. They do not derive a measured end-to-end cost advantage because the source provides no comparative benchmark here.

faces.title: Feedback can live in time while the dependency graph remains acyclic
faces.text: x declares `Continuity` as part of the responsibility contract and separates cross-node subscriptions from intra-node execution; y rejects graph back-edges while representing self-driven re-examination through time/ticks; z lets each new bounded render read prior canonical truth by reference. Together they derive the design principle “loops live in time, not in edges”: a system may iteratively revise itself without encoding self-dependency as a cyclic subscription graph.

volume.title: Persistent agent work can be represented as a durable truth-maintenance contract over disposable bounded renders
volume.text: The complete bounded language surface constructs a specific alternative to one-shot prompting and immortal agent sessions. A responsibility declares the truth it must maintain, the upstream truths it requires and how it may wake; optional ProseScript pins only choreography that is genuinely part of the contract. An intelligent compile phase interprets these semantic needs, freezes an acyclic subscription topology, canonicalizers and postconditions, after which a deliberately dumb reconciler compares fingerprints, skips unchanged work, coalesces wakes and propagates only materially changed committed facets. Each actual render remains bounded and may use messy private scratch, but only canonical maintained truth crosses the publication boundary into the world-model and append-only receipt chain; failures leave last-good truth intact. This earns a portable declarative architecture for standing AI responsibilities, granular reactive recomputation and auditable state transition. It does not earn the stronger claims that all host implementations are faithful, that semantic wiring is always correct, that the system is cheaper/reliable in practice, or that a long-running AI session is a universally reliable computer: the project itself marks benchmarks as pending, the harness as experimental and the language as actively evolving.

metabolites.title: Declare maintained truth before pinning choreography
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.4nQ1:wx.
CREATE: State the durable outcome/world-state, required inputs, invariants and continuity policy as the public contract; add explicit execution order only where order, branching, retry or coordination is itself semantically required.
COPY: Future runs and implementations can keep satisfying the same maintained truth even when internal models, helper functions, retries or decomposition strategies change.
CONTROL: Review every imperative step against the question “would changing this step change the promised outcome?”; if not, keep it out of the semantic contract. Conversely, pin steps whose ordering/safety behavior is genuinely part of correctness.
CULTIVATE: Start reusable workflows declaratively, then introduce choreography only at proven control surfaces, preserving a small stable contract while implementation evolves underneath.
Compression: Specify what must stay true; script how only when the how is part of the truth.
