Tetrahedral metabolism — 4 faces


S.DZqA:wxz — Trustworthy selective refinement needs visible pressure, hidden-debt accounting, and capable repair
The estimator/error contract, independent oscillation channel, and contraction machinery jointly show a three-part certificate. A system can refine only selected regions while proving global progress when it tracks both currently visible approximation error and representation-hidden source debt, and when refinement changes the local approximation space enough for the proof's state relation to convert those signals into error reduction.


S.DZqA:wxy — Permanent nonuniformity can be lawful when omission debt remains explicitly measurable
The problem contract, dual marking mechanism and numerical behavior jointly distinguish nonuniformity from neglect. Large regions may stay coarse and a global preadaptation pass may be unnecessary, but only while the model's independent oscillation accounting says the coarse representation is not hiding too much unresolved source information.


S.DZqA:wzy — Selectivity and efficiency share a mechanism but require different evidence
The source-wide setup, contraction proof and experiments jointly show why successful local adaptation should not be summarized as “sparse therefore optimal.” The paper rigorously certifies convergence; it only empirically exhibits quasi-optimal meshes/performance in its examples. The two claims must remain separately warranted.


S.DZqA:xzy — Small blind-spot terms may be proof-critical without demanding universal catch-up
The oscillation channel, contraction proof and implementation results jointly show a subtler alternative to periodic full refinement. Hidden-debt correction can be targeted and infrequent; when the debt is zero it does no work, when nonzero it activates locally, and its very existence closes the proof obligation that a visible-error-only scheduler cannot generally discharge.

S.DZqA:wxyz — Selective local adaptation can converge globally without periodic global refinement when missed information has its own certificate
Within the paper's bounded AFEM regime, global convergence does not require periodically making the mesh uniformly fine. A residual estimator directs work toward visible discretization error, a distinct data-oscillation quantity tracks source information lost by the current coarse representation, and nested local refinement supplies enough new finite-element freedom for these witnesses to force fixed-factor energy-error reduction. The transferable bounded distinction is therefore not “local refinement is safe” but “local refinement can be safe without global catch-up when omission debt is independently represented and contracted under a repair operation whose comparison law is explicit.” If that debt is exactly zero, no synthetic catch-up is required; if it is unresolved, low priority alone is not permission to omit.

INV-S.DZqA-01 — Selective prioritization needs an independent blind-spot certificate
Minimal earning body: S.DZqA:wxz.

COPY: carry both debts across adaptive steps rather than treating the scheduler's ranking as evidence of harmless omission.

CULTIVATE: search for the smallest independently grounded blind-spot witness that can close the progress proof in the local domain.

INV-S.DZqA-02 — Zero hidden debt is evidence-dependent, not a reason for mandatory catch-up
Minimal earning body: S.DZqA:xy.
CREATE: expose the hidden-debt channel even when a particular state may make it vanish.
COPY: preserve witnessed zero/small debt as a state fact, not as a permanent deletion of the channel.
CONTROL: do not schedule global repair solely because omission is possible, and do not suppress repair solely because omission was absent before.
CULTIVATE: let local debt evidence activate additional work only where and when the bounded model says it is needed.

INV-S.DZqA-03 — A certificate must couple to a repair action capable of changing the relevant state
Minimal earning body: S.DZqA:wz.
CREATE: pair diagnostics with an update/refinement operation that adds the local representational freedom required by the proof.
COPY: preserve the before/after comparison relation—here nested spaces and Galerkin structure—across repairs.

CULTIVATE: design selective repair so local expansion is sufficient for global task-error reduction while avoiding unnecessary whole-system work.

INV-S.DZqA-04 — Convergence and allocation optimality are distinct warrants
Minimal earning body: S.DZqA:zy.
CREATE: state separately the progress theorem and any resource/complexity claim.
COPY: preserve whether each claim is theorem-level, empirical, heuristic, or companion-dependent.
CONTROL: do not promote observed quasi-optimal slopes or competitive runtime into a universal optimal-complexity theorem.
CULTIVATE: acquire a distinct comparison-class/cardinality theorem when resource optimality becomes the actual obligation.
Compression: Proved contraction is not proved minimum work.

volume.title: Selective local adaptation can converge globally without periodic global refinement when missed information has its own certificate
volume.text: Within the paper's bounded AFEM regime, global convergence does not require periodically making the mesh uniformly fine. A residual estimator directs work toward visible discretization error, a distinct data-oscillation quantity tracks source information lost by the current coarse representation, and nested local refinement supplies enough new finite-element freedom for these witnesses to force fixed-factor energy-error reduction. The transferable bounded distinction is therefore not “local refinement is safe” but “local refinement can be safe without global catch-up when omission debt is independently represented and contracted under a repair operation whose comparison law is explicit.” If that debt is exactly zero, no synthetic catch-up is required; if it is unresolved, low priority alone is not permission to omit.

S.FLcQ:wxz — Partial-dependence concentration is a three-stage certified pipeline
The independence contract, proof engine and model-specific construction jointly yield an operational route: construct genuinely independent subfamilies, quantify the resulting cover/graph complexity, then apply the concentration theorem. Remove w and there is no admissible dependence certificate; remove x and no concentration guarantee follows; remove z and the abstract theorem has no justified application-specific graph.


S.FLcQ:wxy — Topology earns conservative evidence only under a witnessed missing-edge contract
The formal dependence representation, proof and limitation surfaces jointly show that nonadjacency must mean the source-defined independence, not merely “different parent,” “no visible overlap,” or “far apart.” Once that witness exists, topology can support conservative probability; without it, the graph remains descriptive provenance.


S.FLcQ:wzy — Structural transfer does not imply mechanistic equivalence
The general cover vocabulary, applications and limitations jointly show that dependency topology can recur across very different stochastic models without asserting a shared hidden mechanism. The transferable object is the certificate form; the model-specific independence relation and resulting sharpness must be re-earned each time.


S.FLcQ:xzy — Tractability trades against faithfulness in dependence representation
Proof machinery, applications and limitations jointly expose a governed compression of dependence. Chromatic or degree surrogates can make the theorem usable, but the simplification may discard information and weaken the exponent. Computational convenience and stochastic faithfulness are therefore separate evaluation surfaces.

S.FLcQ:wxyz — Topology can certify concentration only through admissible independence
Within the source’s bounded stochastic regime, topology supports finite-sample concentration only by organizing an independently witnessed decomposition of the random variables. Fractional-cover/chromatic complexity is an explicit dependence penalty against the independent-case rate, not an evidence generator. This creates a middle regime between naive independence and a full generative dependence model: a thinner local-independence contract can be enough for rigorous concentration, but only when that contract is genuinely true. For /papers, genealogical topology can receive probabilistic meaning only inside a deliberately stochastic recurrence protocol that separately witnesses the required local independence; present structural recurrence alone remains nonprobabilistic.


Bounded volume invariant
A dependence graph can support finite-sample evidence without a full covariance or ancestry model only when its independent subsets/nonadjacencies are themselves warranted; the graph’s cover complexity then penalizes, rather than creates, concentration strength.

INV-S.FLcQ-01 — Topology needs an independence witness before it is evidence
Minimal earning body: S.FLcQ:wxy.
CREATE: define which subsets of the stochastic observations are genuinely independent before assigning inferential meaning to a topology.
COPY: carry that independence contract with every use of the graph or cover rather than copying edges/nonedges as naked structure.

CULTIVATE: design future recurrence experiments so their randomization and shared conditions make the required local-independence claims auditable.
Compression: Topology can organize evidence; it cannot manufacture the independence that gives the evidence force.


INV-S.FLcQ-02 — Fractional-cover complexity is an explicit dependence penalty
Minimal earning body: S.FLcQ:wx.
CREATE: cover the observation index set by certified independent subfamilies and measure the cheapest fractional cover.
COPY: preserve χ*=1 as the fully independent baseline and treat larger cover/chromatic quantities as lost concentration strength.
CONTROL: distinguish χ* from easier χ or Δ+1 surrogates and keep the resulting conservatism visible.
CULTIVATE: prefer the sharpest legally supported dependence representation when the quality of the bound matters.
Compression: Partial dependence enters the theorem as an explicit penalty on the independent-case concentration rate.


INV-S.FLcQ-03 — Valid concentration can deliberately discard dependence strength
Minimal earning body: S.FLcQ:xy.
CREATE: choose a dependence abstraction sufficient for the guarantee being sought.
COPY: preserve the distinction between proof-valid structure and a complete description of the joint law.
CONTROL: do not infer tightness, weak correlation or mechanistic independence from a valid independent-cover bound.
CULTIVATE: enrich the dependence model only when the added structure earns materially sharper or more relevant evidence.
Compression: A theorem may be correct precisely because it forgets information, and that same forgetting can make it loose.


INV-S.FLcQ-04 — Dependency construction is model-specific
Minimal earning body: S.FLcQ:wz.
CREATE: derive graph edges/nonedges from the actual stochastic construction rather than from a generic overlap heuristic.
COPY: keep the source-domain witness attached when transporting the same graph vocabulary to another system.
CONTROL: audit naive overlap graphs for unnecessary edges and audit sparse graphs for unjustified missing edges.
CULTIVATE: treat dependence modeling as part of experimental design, not merely a post hoc visualization step.
Compression: The topology that controls a bound must be earned from the model, and its granularity materially changes the result.

vertices.title: Cover-based dependence certificate
vertices.text:
Source span: carrier beginning through the end of §2, including title/abstract/introduction, definitions of independent sets, proper covers and fractional covers, dependency graphs, and the principal concentration statements before the proofs section.
Nutrient: fixes the admissible partial-independence contract. Independent index subsets and fractional covers define what information the method is allowed to use; χ* measures the cheapest fractional independent cover; dependency graphs provide a sufficient encoding only when their nonadjacency semantics correspond to real independence. This body establishes the dependence quantity that will later enter the deviation bounds.

vertices.title: Proof engine for independent decomposition
vertices.text:
Source span: §3, “Proofs,” through Remark 3.5, immediately before §4.
Nutrient: turns the cover certificate into a concentration theorem. Exact fractional-cover decompositions, Jensen-type arguments and moment-generating-function factorization over independent blocks yield Hoeffding- and variance-sensitive bounds; Cauchy–Schwarz and equitable graph coloring provide usable chromatic/maximum-degree surrogates. The proof makes explicit that the gain comes from lawful independent decomposition, not from topology alone.

vertices.title: Model-specific dependence constructions
vertices.text:
Source span: §4, Examples 4.1–4.4, from the beginning of the applications section through its end immediately before §5.
Nutrient: instantiates the abstract contract in U-statistics, random-string pattern counts, and random graph/hypergraph substructure counts. Each application must construct a dependence relation appropriate to the model, and the examples show that a careful graph can be substantially sparser than a naive overlap graph. The chosen representation of dependence materially changes the resulting exponent.

vertices.title: Explicit limits of the abstraction
vertices.text:
Source span: §5, “Further remarks,” through the complete references and author/contact matter at the end of the carrier.
Nutrient: states what the machinery leaves out. The method intentionally exploits only independence of suitable subfamilies and can therefore be conservative when additional weak-dependence information exists; alternate decompositions may be inferior, graph formulations are convenient rather than ontologically complete, and actual independent-set covers may sharpen graph-based surrogates.

S.Flfg.title: SAFFRON: an Adaptive Algorithm for Online Control of the False Discovery Rate

edges.title: Regulation: the online error target becomes executable through an adaptive spending rule whose thresholds are past-measurable and whose candidate accounting estimates null-directed spend.
Growth: empirical gains come from retaining more alpha wealth for likely alternatives, while lambda/tuning changes efficiency and creates no universal best setting.
Responsibility: formal control requires the conditional-superuniform p-value contract; full FDR additionally requires the source’s independence and monotonicity conditions.
Adaptation: candidate filtering and alpha-investing/Storey relations show how observed history may lawfully alter future test levels without spending unknown future evidence.
Integrity: the FDP/wealth invariant is only a valid certificate when theorem assumptions keep the expectation and reverse-superuniformity steps lawful.
Learning: simulation evidence diagnoses power and tuning; it cannot replace proof assumptions or extend the guarantee class.
edges.text:
4 FACES
wxy — Regenerative online allocation: problem → adaptive accounting → empirical pressure yields a rule that recycles stream history into future levels rather than resetting at every test.
wxz — Proof-bounded governance: setup + construction + proof show family-level control is a coupled accounting certificate, not an aggregation of individually valid local tests.
wyz — Evidence boundary: motivation + experiments + proof separate observed power from guarantee scope.
xyz — Adaptive calibration: algorithm + empirical tuning + proof imply tuning/candidate adaptation is lawful only inside the declared filtration and p-value contract.


1 VOLUME — Metabolism
A potentially unbounded adaptive testing lineage can keep stream-level false-discovery debt bounded only by carrying an explicit online accounting certificate over the sequence. SAFFRON’s candidate-based estimator can spend less on p-values that look like alternatives and improve power in tested regimes, while full FDR—not merely mFDR—remains conditional on additional independence and monotonicity assumptions.


SURVIVING INVARIANTS
1. Local validity ≠ lineage validity.
Bounded invariant: Individually fresh/valid tests do not imply open-ended family-level FDR control; the stream needs its own sequential error-accounting certificate.
Earning body: w+x+z.
CCCC: CREATE — distinguish the family-level obligation from local witnesses; COPY — preserve the declared p-value contract; CONTROL — carry the wealth/FDP certificate across the stream; CULTIVATE — update future levels only through lawful history.
Compression: local stopping robustness is not lineage error control.


2. Past-dependent adaptation is lawful when billed into the certificate.
Bounded invariant: Test levels and candidate rules may depend on prior outcomes under the paper’s filtration/conditional-superuniform contract, but current evidence cannot be used in undeclared ways.
Earning body: w+x+z.
CCCC: CREATE — propose the next level from prior state; COPY — retain the filtration boundary; CONTROL — charge adaptation to the accounting rule; CULTIVATE — let accumulated history reshape future allocation.
Compression: adapt from the past, not around the proof.


3. Adaptive null-spend estimation can buy power, not assumption freedom.
Bounded invariant: Candidate/Storey-style estimation reallocates alpha toward likely alternatives; lambda is an efficiency/tuning parameter, not a universal optimum and not a repair for invalid p-values.
Earning body: x+y+z.
CCCC: CREATE — estimate null-directed spend; COPY — preserve the source’s threshold/candidate semantics; CONTROL — constrain reallocation by wealth; CULTIVATE — tune against observed regime without widening the theorem.
Compression: adaptation reallocates budget; it does not manufacture validity.


4. Guarantee tier must stay typed.
Bounded invariant: Conditional superuniformity plus the paper’s FDP accounting gives mFDR control; the full FDR theorem additionally relies on stated independence and monotonicity conditions.
Earning body: w+x+z.
CCCC: CREATE — name the exact target guarantee; COPY — carry its assumptions intact; CONTROL — refuse silent strengthening; CULTIVATE — upgrade only when additional conditions are witnessed.

edges.title: EMPIRICAL SUCCESS REMAINS IMPLEMENTATION- AND SCOPE-BOUNDED

S.G9sN:wxy — CONDITIONAL EQUALITY ACROSS COVARIATE REGIMES REQUIRES ESTIMAND SEPARATION, CALIBRATED INFERENCE, AND EMPIRICAL WITNESS
w separates conditional-law comparison from covariate-marginal equality; x makes that separation statistically executable; y shows the procedure behaving across the source’s tested conditional-shift regimes. Removing w collapses the target into an ambiguous two-sample problem, removing x loses inferential calibration, and removing y loses the source’s finite encounter with the construction.

w provides cross-generation and the overlap-bounded population equality criterion; x supplies the feasible test and coupled approximation-rate law; z proves the asymptotics and exhibits failure without overlap or interaction. Removing any one turns the claimed conditional-equality test into either an unimplemented characterization, an unbounded algorithmic promise, or an assumption-blind comparison.


S.G9sN:wyz — SUPPORT LOSS NARROWS THE CLAIMABLE DOMAIN; IT DOES NOT BECOME EVIDENCE OF DRIFT

S.G9sN:wxyz — OVERLAP-BOUNDED CONDITIONAL CONTINUITY UNDER COVARIATE SHIFT

S.GIWv.title: Reshaping reservoirs with unsupervised Hebbian adaptation

edges.title: Structural adaptation becomes evidence only when task-shaped wiring survives comparative load
edges.text: Given w + x, the paper moves from an architectural proposal to a bounded empirical result. w says that the recurrent carrier itself can be grown from data rather than frozen randomly; x shows that this actually improves classification performance against static and locally plastic reservoir baselines in several regimes while failing to dominate large-data gradient-trained recurrence or forecasting. Remove w and the benchmark gains are detached from the structural intervention; remove x and structural self-organization remains only a plausible design idea.

edges.title: Task-specific wiring changes representation quality, not merely connection count
edges.text: Given w + y, the intended structural adaptation is connected to measured changes in reservoir geometry: lower redundancy, broader effective subspace than excitatory static reservoirs, and substantially improved class clustering/separability. Crucially, y also shows that more raw dimensionality is not monotonically better. Remove w and the geometry has no specific growth mechanism; remove y and “task-shaped” remains an architectural description without evidence for what the task shaping does to the representation.

edges.title: HAG is homeostasis-gated correlation growth, not generic Hebbian reinforcement
edges.text: Given w + z, the biological slogan is narrowed into the source’s actual law. Correlation chooses a growth partner only for neurons first identified as under-active relative to a homeostatic target; over-active neurons are pruned by a different, partly random rule, and multi-timescale windows plus saturation controls regulate the process. Remove w and the algorithm loses the problem/contribution it is meant to solve; remove z and “fire together, wire together” overstates the mechanism and hides its engineered gates, asymmetry, stochasticity, and hyperparameters.

edges.title: The task contrast localizes what the reshaped geometry is good for
edges.text: Given x + y, classification gains coincide with lower redundancy and stronger class compactness/separation, while forecasting gains are marginal and the paper warns that representational expansion can disrupt temporally stable structure needed for prediction. Remove x and the geometric analysis has no task-performance contrast; remove y and the classification/forecasting difference lacks a representational mechanism. Together they earn a regime-specific statement: reshaping geometry toward separability is useful when separability is the task bottleneck, not automatically when temporal continuity is.

edges.title: Useful structural adaptation does not require a uniquely converged final topology
edges.text: Given x + z, HAG delivers repeatable benchmark improvements across seeded trials even though the method has no formal convergence guarantee and stochastic pruning/tie-breaking can produce different final connectivity on the same series. Remove x and non-uniqueness is only an implementation fact; remove z and performance could be misread as evidence for a uniquely learned architecture. Together they show that functional benefit in this system is compatible with a family of task-shaped carrier realizations.

edges.title: Homeostatic structural growth selects a useful subspace rather than maximizing dynamical richness
edges.text: Given y + z, HAG’s measured outcome—moderate effective dimensionality with low within-class spread and reduced redundancy—can be related to a growth law that adds correlated connections only when local activity is below a target and prunes when above it. The network is therefore not driven simply toward maximal edge density or maximal CEVD. Remove y and there is no evidence for the resulting representation geometry; remove z and the observed minimal-sufficient region has no source-grounded control mechanism.

faces.title: Carrier-level learning can create a task-relevant representation before the simple readout is trained
faces.text: w defines the departure from a static random reservoir, x shows classification gains over conventional reservoir baselines, and y shows that the grown carrier has lower redundancy and stronger class organization rather than merely more activity or more dimensions. Together these bodies earn a carrier-learning distinction: unsupervised structural adaptation can preprocess the computational substrate into a representation that makes a later linear readout’s job easier. Remove w and there is no carrier intervention; remove x and no task benefit; remove y and no evidence for how the carrier became useful.

faces.title: A lightweight learner can move adaptation into structure while preserving a cheap downstream readout
faces.text: w establishes the motivation to retain reservoir computing’s cheap linear-readout regime, x shows where HAG remains competitive under that constraint, and z shows that the structural pass itself is unsupervised and gradient-free at the reservoir level. Together they earn a bounded middle path between frozen random reservoirs and fully end-to-end recurrent training: spend adaptation on the internal wiring, then retain simple supervised readout training. Remove any constituent and the tradeoff between method, performance, and training regime is lost.

faces.title: Local regulation can produce global representational differentiation without selecting a unique final architecture
faces.text: w proposes task-shaped structural self-organization, y observes decorrelation and discriminatively organized representation geometry, and z shows the local/stochastic homeostatic rules plus non-unique final connectivity. Together they earn a non-uniqueness distinction: global representational improvement can arise from locally regulated structural changes even when no single canonical wiring is selected. This is an empirical property of HAG, not evidence that all local plasticity laws behave this way.

faces.title: Optimizing separability can trade against temporal continuity
faces.text: x establishes the strong classification versus weak/mixed forecasting contrast, y links classification gains to decorrelation and class-separable geometry, and z specifies the structural process that actively rewires the recurrent dynamics. Together they earn a task-bound control principle: changing the recurrent carrier to make states more discriminatively separable can improve classification while being neutral or harmful where stable temporal dependencies are the key resource. Remove x and the task tradeoff disappears; remove y and the geometry is unknown; remove z and the intervention producing it is unspecified.

volume.title: Bounded whole-paper closure
volume.text: The paper demonstrates that a reservoir need not remain a frozen random projection to preserve the lightweight reservoir-computing regime. HAG begins with nearly empty excitatory recurrent connectivity and uses homeostatic need to gate structural change: under-active neurons preferentially strengthen connections from highly correlated partners across sampled temporal windows, while over-active neurons prune existing inputs and variance-HAG adds a saturation safeguard. Across the tested benchmarks, this stochastic unsupervised restructuring most clearly benefits classification, especially in smaller and medium-data regimes, while forecasting improvements are marginal and large-data gradient-trained recurrent networks can remain superior. Representation analysis explains the classification effect more precisely than “higher dimensionality”: HAG reduces redundant activation, expands an overly collapsed excitatory reservoir, and organizes states into compact, separable class structure, but the best-performing reservoirs occupy a minimal-sufficient region rather than maximizing effective dimensionality. The full carrier therefore earns a bounded mechanism: activity-regulated structural plasticity can reshape the computational carrier into a task-relevant representational subspace before a simple readout is trained. It does not earn universal Hebbian optimality, monotonic benefit from dimensional expansion, superiority across task regimes, formal convergence, or a unique final wiring law.

metabolites.title: Homeostatic need gates structural learning
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.GIWv:z.
Invariant: In HAG, correlation is not sufficient to create structure: a neuron must first fall outside a homeostatic activity band, after which correlation selects growth for under-active neurons while over-activity invokes pruning.
CREATE: detect a local deficit/excess relative to an explicit operating band before permitting structural mutation.
COPY: reproduce the same need-gated growth/pruning relation across windows, seeds, datasets, and both mean- and variance-regulated variants rather than copying any one final adjacency matrix.
CONTROL: keep homeostatic targets, saturation safeguards, pruning behavior, and adaptation-window scale explicit; ablate correlation-only growth versus need-gated growth to distinguish the gate from the partner-selection heuristic.
CULTIVATE: derive better local removal criteria, adaptive homeostatic bands, or alternative partner-selection measures while preserving the distinction that structure changes in response to regulated need rather than correlation alone.
Compression: Relation proposes a partner; local need decides whether wiring is allowed to change.
metabolites.compression: Relation proposes a partner; local need decides whether wiring is allowed to change.

metabolites.title: Useful dimensionality is minimal-sufficient, not maximal
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.GIWv:y.
Invariant: Across the studied classification reservoirs, HAG’s strongest representations combine improved class compactness/separability with only moderate effective dimensionality; pushing CEVD higher does not monotonically improve accuracy and can add noise beyond a dataset-dependent tipping point.
CREATE: expand a representation only until additional dimensions improve the task-relevant organization rather than treating expansion itself as the target.
COPY: reproduce the criterion with both expressivity metrics and task-structure metrics so “more dimensions” cannot stand in for usefulness.
CONTROL: track CEVD, activation dependence, within-class spread, between-class separation, and downstream accuracy together; stop expansion when added dimensions cease to improve the task geometry.
CULTIVATE: learn task- or data-dependent sufficiency thresholds and selectively allocate representational degrees where they improve separability or another explicitly measured objective.
Compression: The useful space is large enough to separate what matters, not as large as possible.
metabolites.compression: The useful space is large enough to separate what matters, not as large as possible.

metabolites.title: Representation-shaping gains are objective-dependent
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.GIWv:xy.
Invariant: The same structural reshaping associated with decorrelated, class-separable states yields clear gains for classification but only marginal or mixed gains for forecasting, where preserving stable temporal dependencies can matter more than expanding/separating the feature space.
CREATE: identify the representational bottleneck of the target objective before choosing an adaptation pressure.
COPY: test the same structural intervention across objectives that reward different geometries—separation, temporal memory, smooth prediction—rather than generalizing from one task family.
CONTROL: require cross-task negative controls and measure both the property being amplified and the property that may be disrupted.
CULTIVATE: condition plasticity on task regime or combine separability-promoting growth with mechanisms that explicitly preserve temporal dependencies when forecasting requires them.
Compression: An adaptation is useful relative to the structure the task needs preserved.
metabolites.compression: An adaptation is useful relative to the structure the task needs preserved.

metabolites.title: Functional closure need not select a unique carrier
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.GIWv:xz.
Invariant: In the studied HAG procedure, seeded runs can yield useful performance even though formal convergence is not guaranteed and stochastic pruning/tie-breaking can produce different final reservoir connectivities on the same data.
CREATE: allow a stochastic structural process to search a family of task-compatible carriers rather than requiring one predetermined final topology.
COPY: reproduce function and representational properties across independent runs while treating exact edge identity as contingent unless the data show otherwise.
CONTROL: separate functional reproducibility from structural identity; report seed variance, convergence failures, connectivity variability, and performance jointly.
CULTIVATE: characterize equivalence classes of successful reservoirs and derive which structural/statistical properties are actually conserved across them before promoting any specific wiring pattern as necessary.
Compression: Stable function can be carried by a family of structures even when no single final structure is selected.

vertices.title: Motivate structural adaptation and define HAG’s departure from static or locally tuned reservoirs
vertices.text:
Source span: Abstract → Introduction → “Static reservoir computing: strengths and limitations” → “Previous work” → “Contributions,” ending immediately before Results.
Nutrient: The paper starts from the reservoir-computing bargain: keep a recurrent feature-generating reservoir mostly fixed, then train only a cheap linear readout. This yields low-data and low-compute advantages but leaves performance hostage to a random, task-agnostic recurrent architecture. Prior plasticity work mainly modifies activity or existing synapses locally. HAG instead begins with nearly empty recurrent connectivity and grows task-shaped structure from longer-window co-activation statistics while maintaining homeostatic targets. The authors explicitly target multivariate time-series and distinguish their contribution by structural growth from scratch, correlation measured over extended windows, task-specific use of cross-channel structure, and evaluation on classification as well as forecasting. This body establishes the intervention hypothesis: adaptation can act on the computational carrier itself rather than only on a readout or a dense pre-existing reservoir.

vertices.title: Establish where HAG helps, where it only matches, and where gradient-trained recurrence wins
vertices.text:
Source span: Results opening → Tables 1–2 and surrounding analysis → paragraph ending that forecasting gains are marginal and classification forms the main core of the paper’s theory/improvement.
Nutrient: Across five classification datasets, mean-HAG and variance-HAG obtain the best cumulative ranks among the compared models and frequently outperform static ESNs plus Intrinsic Plasticity, Anti-Oja, and their combination. HAG leads on the smaller Japanese Vowels and CatsDogs datasets and remains competitive on medium-sized FSDD and Spoken Arabic Digits, while large Speech Commands is dominated by gradient-trained GRU/LSTM. Forecasting is different: HAG is competitive on Mackey-Glass and improves over many reservoir baselines, but GRU/LSTM are substantially better on Lorenz and Sunspot; the authors characterize HAG’s forecasting improvement as marginal. They explicitly interpret this task contrast: decorrelation and expanded features aid linear separability in classification, whereas forecasting must preserve temporal dependencies that aggressive representational reshaping may disturb. The paper therefore does not earn “adaptive structural growth is generally superior”; it earns a regime-dependent advantage concentrated in classification and low-/moderate-data reservoir settings.

vertices.title: Resolve the performance effect into reservoir geometry and identify minimal-sufficient expansion
vertices.text:
Source span: Remaining Results, beginning with the representational-capacity analysis after the forecasting/classification boundary → all dimensionality/dependency and class-separability analyses → Discussion, ending immediately before Methods.
Nutrient: The paper distinguishes task-agnostic expressivity from task-relevant representation quality and measures reservoir behavior with spectral radius, average activation correlation, PCA-derived cumulative explained-variance dimension (CEVD), distance correlation, and several clustering/separability metrics. Relative to excitatory-only static ESNs, HAG commonly increases spectral radius, sharply reduces redundant activation correlations, and expands effective dimensionality, especially on higher-dimensional inputs. Yet fully signed ESNs can reach still lower correlation or higher expressivity without becoming the most accurate classifier. On class-structure metrics, one HAG variant is best in most dataset×metric comparisons; the strongest HAG reservoirs occupy a region of near-optimal within-class consistency with only moderate CEVD. The authors therefore refine their own dimensionality claim: beyond a dataset-dependent tipping point, extra components mainly inject noise and erode class structure. HAG’s advantage is a minimal-sufficient, discriminatively organized expansion rather than indiscriminate dimensional growth. Discussion retains the negative side: classification gains are clearer than forecasting gains, and larger/more complex tasks remain future work.

vertices.title: Expose the actual plasticity law, stochastic/nonunique closure, evaluation controls, and carrier limits
vertices.text:
Source span: Methods → end of carrier, including HAG algorithm, datasets, baseline/training protocol, hyperparameter search/evaluation, data/code/author/competing-interest/additional-information statements, references, and the article’s explicit pointer to supplementary material.
Nutrient: HAG is an engineered homeostatic structural-growth procedure over excitatory recurrent weights. Two variants regulate either mean activity or activity variance; the authors explicitly state there is no formal proof that either target is universally preferable. At adaptation steps, neurons outside a target homeostatic band are selected: under-active neurons increase an incoming weight from the most highly correlated eligible partner, whereas over-active neurons prune a randomly chosen existing connection because the authors lack a reliable local removal criterion that increases global dimensionality. Correlation windows are sampled over multiple timescales; variance-HAG adds synaptic scaling when activity approaches saturation. Correlation-driven additions tend to become reciprocal, while random pruning can introduce asymmetry. Formal convergence is not guaranteed, tie-breaking and stochastic pruning make final connectivity non-unique, and repeated runs may close on different architectures. Experiments use a single unsupervised pretraining stream where required, cross-validated hyperparameters, multiple static/plastic reservoir baselines and one-layer GRU/LSTM comparators, and eight seeded trials for reported test metrics. The article links code/data and supplementary material; that companion material is not treated as verified tissue in this pass.

edges.title: Latent-score certification.
edges.text: w supplies the target statistic and sufficient-condition score interface; x supplies the coupling, independent-sum limit theorem and vanishing-discrepancy proof. Together they turn a representational condition into a certified asymptotic-normality result. Without w the proof has no defined rank-statistic family to certify; without x the conditions remain unsupported assertions.

edges.title: Conditions become usable constructions.
edges.text: w gives the abstract admissibility conditions; y supplies concrete latent populations, scores and coefficient schemes for familiar rank statistics. Without w the examples lack one common certification law; without y the theorem has no demonstrated operational reach.

edges.title: Alternative sufficient route gains independent reach.
edges.text: w supplies Dwass’s criterion; z exhibits a statistic for which an earlier sufficient condition fails while the new theorem still applies. Without w there is no alternate certificate; without z there is no demonstrated separation from the older sufficient family.

edges.title: Transfer mechanism explains application breadth.
edges.text: x supplies the iid coupling and approximation mechanism; y shows several differently named statistics realized through that mechanism. Without x the examples are a list rather than one transfer principle; without y the proof’s reusable range is unwitnessed.

edges.title: Proof mechanism does not depend on the older certificate.
edges.text: x proves normality by latent-sum approximation; z supplies a case rejected by a prior sufficient criterion but accepted by this route. Without x failure of the old condition would establish no positive result; without z the new proof’s logical independence from that criterion remains untested.

edges.title: Recovery and extension are both visible.
edges.text:
y shows continuity with known asymptotically normal rank statistics; z shows at least one case outside an earlier sufficient-condition theorem. Together they distinguish an alternate theorem from both mere repackaging and unsupported novelty. Without y there is no continuity witness; without z there is no strict-extension witness.


4 FACES


wxy — Operational sufficient-condition calculus.
The theorem interface, proof mechanism and worked applications together give a constructive procedure: choose a latent score representation, verify the stated conditions, transfer the normal limit, and instantiate the rank statistic. Remove w and there is no criterion; remove x and no proof; remove y and no realized use.


wxz — Logically independent certification route.
The theorem, its proof, and the explicit older-condition failure together show a sufficient route whose mechanism certifies normality beyond one earlier sufficient family. Remove w and no alternate criterion remains; remove x and the new certificate is unproved; remove z and its independent reach is not witnessed.


wyz — Bounded coverage map of sufficient conditions.
The abstract theorem, familiar applications and the boundary counterexample jointly show both recovery and added reach while preserving the distinction between sufficiency and necessity. Remove w and there is no unifying law; remove y and recovery disappears; remove z and strict added reach disappears.


xyz — Representation transfer, not named-test inheritance.
The coupling proof, varied applications and prior-condition counterexample show that the transferable object is the latent score/approximation structure rather than membership in one named earlier theorem. Remove x and there is no transfer mechanism; remove y and no breadth; remove z and no evidence that older theorem membership is nonessential.


1 VOLUME — S.Hqok:wxyz
Bounded volume invariant: In Dwass’s stated rank-permutation setting, asymptotic normality can be certified by representing rank scores through expected powers of order statistics from a continuous latent population, coupling the rank statistic to a normalized independent weighted sum with the same finite-N distributional skeleton, and proving the score/order-statistic discrepancy vanishes. This sufficient-condition route recovers familiar rank tests and covers at least one constructed statistic outside a prior Hoeffding sufficient condition. It is not a necessary condition and not a universal central-limit theorem for arbitrary rank statistics.


COLLAPSE — 3 SURVIVING METABOLITES


INV-S.Hqok-01 — LATENT REPRESENTATION TRANSFERS LIMIT LAWS
Bounded invariant: When a target statistic has a source-witnessed latent representation with the same finite distributional obligation and its discrepancy from a simpler independently analyzable quantity vanishes in the required mode, a proved limiting law can transfer without identifying the two carriers pointwise.
Minimal earning body: wx.
CREATE: construct a latent score representation.
COPY: preserve the target distribution/limit through the coupling.
CONTROL: keep the discrepancy bound and theorem assumptions explicit.
CULTIVATE: reuse the proof route for further admissible rank statistics.
Compression: transfer the limit through a witnessed approximation, not by analogy.


INV-S.Hqok-02 — SUFFICIENT-CONDITION FAILURE IS NOT PHENOMENON FAILURE
Bounded invariant: Failure of one existing sufficient asymptotic-normality criterion does not imply failure of asymptotic normality when a genuinely different proof mechanism closes under its own stated assumptions.
Minimal earning body: xz.
CREATE: formulate an alternate certificate family.
COPY: preserve the same asymptotic target property.
CONTROL: exhibit the old-condition failure and the independent positive proof together.
CULTIVATE: extend the admissible problem class without promoting sufficiency to necessity.
Compression: a failed certificate is not a failed property.


INV-S.Hqok-03 — SCORE DESIGN MAKES ABSTRACT ASYMPTOTICS OPERATIONAL
Bounded invariant: An abstract limit theorem becomes reusable when its representation conditions can be instantiated by explicit latent distributions, order-statistic scores and coefficient schemes that are checkable for concrete statistics.
Minimal earning body: wy.
CREATE: choose a latent distribution/score map and coefficient scheme.
COPY: carry the rank statistic into the theorem’s representation.
CONTROL: verify continuity, moments and the stated normal-or-diffuse coefficient conditions.
CULTIVATE: reuse the construction to test further rank statistics.
Compression: make the theorem usable by designing the representation it can certify.


BOUNDARY
Single-source claims only. All conclusions remain inside Dwass’s permutation-rank-statistic theorem and its stated continuity, moment, score-representation and coefficient conditions. The applications are mathematical instantiations, not empirical validation. The counterexample shows failure of one earlier sufficient condition while Dwass’s theorem applies; it does not show Hoeffding’s theorem false, prove Dwass’s conditions necessary, or establish a universal CLT for arbitrary rank statistics. No later /papers source, holon conclusion, Tetrix ontology, or project metaphor has been imported.

vertices.title: Sufficient-condition interface
vertices.text:
Source span: §1 and theorem statement in §2, printed pp. 303–304.
Nutrient: Dwass starts from a uniformly random permutation of ranks and a weighted rank statistic S_N. He gives a sufficient-condition theorem built from a continuous latent random variable X whose order-statistic moments generate the rank scores, together with moment and normality/diffuse-coefficient conditions. The source presents this as a different sufficient route from Wald–Wolfowitz/Hoeffding-type criteria, not as a necessary characterization.

vertices.title: Latent-iid coupling proof
vertices.text:
Source span: theorem proof in §2, printed pp. 304–305.
Nutrient: Dwass associates iid latent variables with their random ranks, constructs a random variable g_N(X) having the same finite-N distribution as the rank statistic, and decomposes the problem into a normalized independent weighted sum plus a rank/order-statistic discrepancy. Lyapunov supplies the normal limit for the independent sum under the stated coefficient/moment conditions; a Hoeffding order-statistic result drives the mean-square discrepancy to zero, transferring the same limiting distribution to the rank statistic.

vertices.title: Applications and recovery of familiar rank statistics
vertices.text:
Source span: §3, Examples 1–4, printed p. 305.
Nutrient: The theorem is instantiated for the Hotelling–Pabst rank-correlation statistic, order-statistic score statistics, two-sample coefficient structures, and a statistic linearly related to Wilcoxon/Mann–Whitney. These examples show how the abstract score representation becomes a checkable route to asymptotic normality and how known cases sit inside the new criterion.

vertices.title: Strict boundary witness beyond an earlier criterion
vertices.text:
Source span: §3, Example 5 and references, printed p. 306.
Nutrient: Dwass treats a Terry variance-alternative statistic and then constructs a case with fixed m for which condition (13) of an earlier Hoeffding theorem fails for even powers while Dwass’s theorem still yields asymptotic normality. vertices.title: Gaussian-target reduction
vertices.text:
Source span: §§1–3, printed pp. 288–289.
Nutrient: Fraser states the moving-target hit problem, generalizes it to a k-dimensional Gaussian prediction model, and proves the lemma that convolving Gaussian dispersion around a prediction with a Gaussian diffuse target leaves the success function Gaussian in the prediction coordinates. This makes aiming uncertainty, dispersion uncertainty, and target spread composable inside one closed Gaussian form.

vertices.title: Exact finite-n hit distribution
vertices.text:
Source span: §4, printed pp. 290–291.
Nutrient: The at-least-one-hit probability is expressed by inclusion–exclusion P = nE1 − E2 + … with each joint-hit term Es determined from the covariance/correlation structure, target radius, dispersion and aiming error. The Cunningham–Hynd two-dimensional case is specialized explicitly, and two limiting forms are stated under distinct scaling assumptions.

vertices.title: Small-burst numerical realization
vertices.text:
Source span: §5, printed pp. 291–292.
Nutrient: For a one-second burst of five rounds, empirical correlation values are inserted into the exact expressions and P is evaluated across aiming- and dispersion-error combinations. The formal probability law becomes an operational surface whose sensitivity to error sources can be inspected numerically rather than only symbolically.

vertices.title: Large-n approximation and correction stability
vertices.text:
Source span: §§6–7, printed pp. 292–294.
Nutrient: Direct inclusion–exclusion becomes excessive for large n. Fraser factors correlated terms against an uncorrelated baseline, introduces correction factors c_r and the approximation k_r, derives nonnegativity/stability properties, and reports that k_r approaches a limit with n and is approximately insensitive to r and a in the stated large-a regime. This supplies a tractable approximation path while preserving its regime conditions.

S.IIcl.title: Tensor Logic: The Language of AI

edges.title: one statement type carries both deduction and adaptation
edges.text: w defines tensor equations as a common representation for logical and numeric structure; x gives those equations chaining semantics and automatic differentiation. Derived relation: reasoning and learning are not external modules glued together after representation; they are alternate operations over the same program substrate. The same addressed equation can participate in inference and gradient propagation.

edges.title: unification is operational when translations preserve computation
edges.text: w supplies explicit relation↔tensor and rule↔einsum correspondences; y re-expresses neural, symbolic, kernel and probabilistic systems with those operations. Derived relation: the paper’s unification is stronger than common syntax because the translations preserve joins, projections, products, marginalization, message passing and attention as executable algebraic operations.

edges.title: sparse symbolic identity and dense distributed identity are alternate carriers in one algebra
edges.text: w treats relations as sparse Boolean tensors while retaining tensor factorization and numeric types; z embeds objects, relations and rules into dense tensors and recovers answers by tensor contraction. Derived relation: symbolic tuples and distributed embeddings can be represented as different carrier regimes of the same index/join/projection algebra, with exactness or approximation determined by representation choice rather than by changing languages.

edges.title: derivational structure can itself be the learning path
edges.text: x defines forward/backward chaining and backpropagation through the derivation actually used by an example; y shows programs whose structures encode neural layers, symbolic rules, graph neighborhoods and probabilistic factorization. Derived relation: once heterogeneous computations are expressed as one derivational graph, the path used for inference can also determine where learning updates flow.

edges.title: deduction and analogy become parametrically coupled modes
edges.text: x supplies chaining and learnable tensor programs; z replaces exact one-hot/sparse identities with embeddings whose similarities allow neighboring objects to borrow inferences, while thresholding/temperature can push the system back toward discrete behavior. Derived relation: in the proposed formalism, analogical generalization is not a separate reasoning engine but a controlled relaxation of the same chaining process. This is a formal construction, not an empirical guarantee for arbitrary learned embeddings.

edges.title: a common language becomes generative when paradigms can be composed
edges.text: y demonstrates that neural, symbolic, kernel and probabilistic computations already inhabit the same equation language; z then combines symbolic rules with learned embeddings and tensor decompositions to propose new reasoning systems. Derived relation: the value of the common substrate is not only that existing paradigms can be rewritten in it, but that operations from previously separate paradigms can be composed without crossing a representation-language boundary.

faces.title: executable differentiable unification
faces.text: w defines an operation-preserving common carrier; x supplies inference and learning semantics; y shows multiple AI paradigms encoded within it. Three-way derivation: a unifying language becomes computationally substantive when the same primitive statement can represent heterogeneous systems, execute their inference, and expose learnable parameters to differentiation. Remove w and there is no shared algebra; remove x and the language is descriptive only; remove y and breadth remains untested.

faces.title: discrete core with continuous relaxation
faces.text: w anchors exact logical structure in Boolean tensors/rules; x makes the equations executable and learnable; z moves the same structures into approximate or learned embedding carriers with explicit threshold/temperature controls. Three-way derivation: the formalism supports a proposed continuum between discrete deduction and continuous similarity-based inference while preserving a route back to the discrete regime. The soundness of the relaxed region is conditional on the stated embedding/threshold assumptions.

faces.title: operation-preserving translation enables hybrid construction
faces.text: w establishes the primitive correspondences; y demonstrates that major paradigms can be expressed through them; z uses the shared operations to build embedding-space rule systems not native to any one of the original paradigms. Three-way derivation: genuine formal unification is evidenced not only by translation of existing systems but by the ability to construct hybrids whose components remain legible in the same operation vocabulary.

faces.title: one derivational substrate can mix inference, learning, probability and analogy
faces.text: x gives the program execution/learning machinery; y supplies neural, symbolic, kernel and graphical-model forms; z adds embedding-space reasoning and scaling strategies. Three-way derivation: once these computations share a derivational substrate, a single program can in principle mix exact rules, learned weights, probabilistic factors and similarity-based generalization while retaining explicit tensor equations as the addressable program structure. This is an expressivity/formalism claim, not a demonstrated end-to-end production benchmark.

volume.title: operation-preserving computational unification
volume.text:
All four vertices together derive the paper’s deepest structure: heterogeneous AI paradigms can share a language when their representations and procedures are mapped onto a small common algebra without discarding the operations that make them distinct. Relations/rules become sparse Boolean tensors and joins/projections (w); the resulting equations acquire both chaining and differentiation semantics (x); neural, symbolic, kernel and probabilistic systems are constructively expressed in that substrate (y); and the common carrier then supports proposed hybrids such as embedding-space rule reasoning plus dense/sparse scaling strategies (z).


Volume invariant: unification becomes computationally useful when translation preserves operational structure closely enough that inference, learning and cross-paradigm composition can occur without leaving the shared substrate. The paper earns a formal/constructive unification claim; it does not by itself establish that the proposed embedding-space reasoning is empirically superior, universally sound under arbitrary learned representations, or already scalable as a production language.

metabolites.text:
Source body: S.IIcl:wxyz
CREATE — identify a shared primitive algebra by mapping relations to sparse tensors and logical join/projection to tensor join/projection/einsum rather than merely renaming concepts.
COPY — re-express heterogeneous systems in that algebra while preserving their operative transformations: attention, message passing, Datalog inference, kernel evaluation, marginalization and factor combination.
CONTROL — retain types, index structure, nonlinearities, thresholds, sparsity and inference direction so the common language does not erase the distinctions that determine behavior.
CULTIVATE — compose previously separate operations inside the same program to generate new hybrids, then extend implementations/libraries without changing the primitive statement form.
Compression: unification is strongest when translation preserves operations, not merely vocabulary.

Source body: S.IIcl:wxyz
CREATE — express knowledge/model structure as tensor equations whose LHS/RHS dependencies form the executable program.
COPY — reuse the same equations under forward chaining, backward chaining and derivative propagation; the addressed program structure remains shared across inference and learning.
CONTROL — mark supplied versus learnable tensors, choose inference direction, retain Boolean thresholds where exact logic is required, and restrict updates to the derivational structure actually used.
CULTIVATE — learn parameters and latent decompositions through backpropagation through structure while preserving explicit equations as the program’s inspectable scaffold.

metabolites.title: controlled deductive–analogical relaxation
metabolites.text:
Source body: S.IIcl:wxyz
CREATE — embed objects, relations and rules into distributed tensors so the existing chaining operations can act in embedding space.
COPY — propagate inferences through the same forward/backward rule structure, with similarity allowing related objects to borrow conclusions.
CONTROL — use embedding dimension, threshold/extract/re-embed steps and the proposed temperature parameter to regulate approximation error and move between near-discrete deduction and broader analogy.
CULTIVATE — learn embeddings and potentially rule-specific temperatures so similarity structure becomes task-adapted while keeping the deductive limit explicitly addressable.
Compression: analogy can be formulated as a controlled relaxation of deduction when both inhabit the same operational substrate; its reliability remains conditional on the representation and control assumptions.


FEELING PHENOTYPE — WITNESSED
Designation: S.IIcl.⛨Α⚖⚒
Canonical order: CREATE · COPY · CONTROL · CULTIVATE
Feeling signature: ⛨Α⚖⚒
Phenotype state: WITNESSED


CREATE — ⛨ Bridge
Pre-aspect role-shape: Construct one algebraic carrier that can hold symbolic relations and numeric/tensor computation simultaneously, so systems that previously required different languages can meet without losing their operative structure.
Witness: Tensor Logic explicitly spans Datalog relations/rules and tensor algebra by mapping relations to sparse Boolean tensors and joins/projections to tensor joins/projections/einsums, then gives the shared carrier executable inference and learning semantics. ⛨ Bridge is stronger than ☯ Harmony because the compatibility is not merely discovered as already effortless; the paper constructs load-bearing architecture that lets distinct computational shores be crossed while preserving what holds on each side.


COPY — Α Archetype
Pre-aspect role-shape: Re-express heterogeneous AI systems while preserving the operative transformations that make each system itself, so the same deep computational template can be recognized across neural, symbolic, kernel, and probabilistic forms.
Witness: Attention, message passing, Datalog inference, kernel evaluation, factor combination, and marginalization all become legible through the same index/join/projection/equation grammar without being reduced to common vocabulary alone. Α Archetype is stronger than Ω Continuity because the central recurrence is not one organismal thread surviving a break; it is the same underlying operational geometry appearing independently across domains that previously looked unlike one another.


CONTROL — ⚖ Balance
Pre-aspect role-shape: Preserve types, indices, nonlinearities, thresholds, sparsity, inference direction, approximation error, and temperature so a common language can hold exact deduction and continuous analogy, sparse and dense carriers, learning and inference without collapsing one regime into another.
Witness: Boolean thresholds recover discrete logic, temperature moves embedding-space reasoning from near-deductive toward increasingly analogical behavior, and sparse/dense/Tucker choices expose scaling and approximation trade-offs. ⚖ Balance is stronger than ⚸ Constraint because the controlling motion is truthful proportional placement among multiple legitimate computational regimes rather than primarily the internalization of a prohibitive boundary.


CULTIVATE — ⚒ Tool-craft
Pre-aspect role-shape: Compose previously separate operations into new hybrid programs, learn parameters and latent decompositions through the same explicit equations, and extend implementation/scaling machinery while retaining the primitive statement form as a transparent instrument.
Witness: The shared substrate is generative precisely because it can be wielded to build embedding-space rule reasoning, mixed neural-symbolic programs, backpropagation-through-structure, and future libraries without crossing language boundaries. ⚒ Tool-craft is stronger than ⁂ Evolution because growth here occurs through increasing fluency and reach of a designed computational instrument, not through an architecture recursively discovering its own form.


Whole-organism witness: ⛨Α⚖⚒ describes one integrated motion: a bridge-language spans previously separate computational paradigms, exposes their common operative archetype, keeps distinct exact/approximate regimes honestly balanced, and becomes a practical instrument for composing and learning new hybrids. Phenotype remains orthogonal to organism identity and does not strengthen the paper’s formal proposal into a claim of production-scale validation or universal soundness for arbitrary learned embeddings.

vertices.title: establish the common algebraic substrate
vertices.text:
Source span: ABSTRACT + INTRODUCTION + BACKGROUND + TENSOR LOGIC 3.1 REPRESENTATION; ends immediately before 3.2 INFERENCE.
Nutrient: the paper identifies a concrete correspondence rather than a surface analogy: sparse Boolean tensors compactly encode relations; tensor join/projection reduce to database join/projection in the Boolean case; and Datalog rules correspond to Boolean tensor equations/einsums with thresholding. Tensor logic then takes the tensor equation as its sole statement form, with sparse facts and Datalog syntax retained as alternate notations. This vertex constructs the common carrier on which symbolic and numeric computation can coexist.

vertices.title: make the common substrate executable and learnable
vertices.text:
Source span: TENSOR LOGIC 3.2 INFERENCE + 3.3 LEARNING; ends immediately before IMPLEMENTING AI PARADIGMS.
Nutrient: tensor equations are given generalized forward- and backward-chaining semantics, so the same program can be executed data-first or query-first. Because there is only one statement type, automatic differentiation yields another tensor-logic program; learning can update parameters along the actual derivational structure used by each example via backpropagation through structure. Numeric relaxation and tensor decomposition extend the same substrate toward learned latent structure, while Boolean thresholding can recover discrete predicates in the proposed construction.

vertices.title: demonstrate cross-paradigm expressibility
vertices.text:
Source span: IMPLEMENTING AI PARADIGMS 4.1–4.4; ends immediately before REASONING IN EMBEDDING SPACE.
Nutrient: the paper writes CNNs, GNNs, attention and a full transformer, Datalog symbolic reasoning, kernel machines and probabilistic graphical models in the same tensor-equation language. The mappings are operational: graph-neighbor aggregation is a relation/tensor join; attention is a sequence of tensor equations; Datalog is already valid tensor logic; graphical-model marginalization and pointwise product map to projection and join. This vertex tests whether the proposed primitive vocabulary actually spans heterogeneous AI computation styles.

vertices.title: use the shared substrate to construct hybrid reasoning and expose its scaling boundary
vertices.text:
Source span: REASONING IN EMBEDDING SPACE + SCALING UP + DISCUSSION + ACKNOWLEDGMENTS/REFERENCES to end.
Nutrient: objects, relations and rules are embedded into tensor representations so forward/backward chaining can operate in embedding space. Random embeddings give approximate retrieval with error decreasing as dimension grows; learned embeddings introduce similarity-weighted inference, and the paper proposes temperature as a control from near-deductive to increasingly analogical reasoning. Scaling is proposed through sparse/dense separation or Tucker compression, with approximation error traded against embedding dimension and denoising. The discussion presents this as a research/programming-language proposal and future implementation path, not as an already validated production system.

edges.title: An observed representational asymmetry becomes actionable only when supervision is made asymmetric
edges.text: Given w + x, the paper turns a spectral correlation into a design intervention. w supplies evidence that semantic alignment is concentrated toward coarse/low-frequency structure while pixel encoders retain relatively more higher-frequency detail; x uses that asymmetry to constrain only the low-frequency semantic base and leave residual bands available for reconstruction detail. Remove w and the selective split becomes an architectural choice without the paper’s empirical motivation; remove x and the spectral regularity remains descriptive rather than operational.

edges.title: A spectral hypothesis gains engineering credibility when the representation built around it survives competing objectives
edges.text: Given w + y, the same low-versus-higher-frequency organization that motivates the hypothesis is associated with a latent space that supports semantic probing, high-fidelity reconstruction, competitive generation, faster convergence, and compact-token efficiency. Remove w and the results show a successful tokenizer without explaining why its organization matters; remove y and the hypothesis has no evidence that organizing around the relation helps under real objective conflict.

edges.title: The Prism relation is strengthened as a control heuristic without becoming a universal law
edges.text: Given w + z, the initial spectral evidence is tested indirectly through ablations and transfer: removing low-band semantic regularization weakens semantic accuracy, excessive semantic constraint harms reconstruction, and the unified recipe remains useful in a pixel-space model. Remove w and the ablations lack the spectral hypothesis they are probing; remove z and the original observation has less evidence that its proposed division corresponds to a manipulable design surface. Neither body proves that low frequency is semantics by definition.

edges.title: Frequency organization can serve simultaneously as representation structure and generation schedule
edges.text: Given x + y, UAE’s ordered frequency bands are not merely a storage format. The generator can begin from compact low-frequency content and progressively admit higher bands, while the reported experiments show competitive generation and substantial efficiency gains for reduced low-frequency token budgets. Remove x and there is no ordered latent mechanism; remove y and there is no evidence that exploiting the ordering improves practical generative computation.

edges.title: Selective constraint, not maximal constraint, preserves coexistence of abstraction and fidelity
edges.text: Given x + z, the architecture’s asymmetric loss is justified by its ablation surface: zero low-band semantic alignment sacrifices semantic accuracy, but extending semantic constraints too far into the representation progressively damages reconstruction. High-frequency masking provides a second control that can improve generation by preventing deterministic dependence on detail coefficients. Remove x and the ablations have no designed mechanism to interpret; remove z and the architecture could be mistaken for an arbitrary fixed decomposition rather than a tunable tradeoff.

edges.title: The useful spectral subspace couples compression, generation, and transfer across implementation regimes
edges.text: Given y + z, strong performance in the latent model combines with evidence that compact low-frequency token sets can accelerate generation and retain more semantic signal, while the unified-training idea also improves a pixel-space JIT model under matched settings. Remove y and there is no full performance/efficiency load; remove z and there is no ablation or pixel-space evidence that the relation survives changes in token budget or implementation regime.

faces.title: Empirical spectral structure can be converted into a working bridge between formerly competing representational objectives
faces.text: w establishes the low-band semantic / higher-band detail regularity, x turns it into an asymmetric unified encoder, and y shows that the resulting representation can retain semantic quality while recovering fine visual detail and supporting generation. Together these bodies earn the central engineering result: a measured representational asymmetry can organize a single latent space that serves both abstraction and fidelity. Remove w and the bridge loses its source-backed organizing relation; remove x and there is no bridge; remove y and there is no demonstrated coexistence under load.

faces.title: The operative principle is preservation of a privileged base plus freedom in residual degrees, not a fixed semantic-frequency identity
faces.text: w motivates a privileged low-frequency semantic base, x implements selective low-band anchoring with residual detail bands, and z shows through ablations that both under-constraint and over-constraint have distinct failure signatures. Together they earn an asymmetric control principle: preserve the subspace carrying the desired organization while allowing the remaining degrees of freedom to specialize. Remove any one constituent and the claim loses empirical motivation, mechanism, or stress evidence.

faces.title: The Prism Hypothesis is experimentally productive even though its strongest ontological wording remains unearned
faces.text: w states the hypothesis and its preliminary evidence, y demonstrates useful performance and efficiency in the resulting representational family, and z adds ablation and pixel-space transfer evidence. Together these bodies justify treating the spectral relation as an experimentally productive hypothesis. They do not show that all modalities are literally projections of one universal spectrum, that a unique frequency basis exists, or that semantic meaning is intrinsically low-frequency. Remove w and there is no hypothesis to evaluate; remove y or z and the usefulness claim loses either full task load or stress/transfer support.

faces.title: A unified representation becomes generation-friendly by exposing which information must be preserved and which can be progressively reconstructed
faces.text: x separates a semantically anchored base from detail-bearing residual bands and exposes their ordering; y shows that the representation supports strong reconstruction/generation and compact-token efficiency; z shows that selective semantic anchoring and high-frequency masking materially change semantic fidelity, reconstruction, and convergence. Together they earn a practical mechanism: generation becomes easier when the representation makes a compact structural base available first and treats finer information as progressively refinable rather than requiring all information to be equally fixed at once.

volume.title: Bounded whole-paper closure
volume.text: Across the studied visual encoders and benchmarks, the paper finds that retrieval-relevant semantic structure is disproportionately associated with coarse/low-frequency content while pixel-oriented representations retain relatively more mid/high-frequency detail. UAE turns that empirical asymmetry into an explicitly ordered latent representation: a low-frequency region is selectively aligned to a pretrained semantic encoder, higher-frequency capacity remains freer to encode reconstruction detail, and masked high-frequency prediction plus frequency ordering make the same representation usable for progressive generation. Reconstruction, semantic probing, generation, convergence, efficiency, ablation, and pixel-space-transfer results collectively support this organization as a useful engineering control surface. The full carrier therefore earns a bounded principle: abstraction and fidelity need not be implemented as incompatible encoder families when a measured representational asymmetry can be preserved in one base-plus-residual representation and exposed to training and generation. It does not earn semantics = low frequency as an identity, a universal shared spectrum across all modalities, a unique optimal frequency basis/cutoff, or UAE as the uniquely necessary architecture.

metabolites.title: Preserve the privileged subspace; free the residual bandwidth
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.IJnH:xz.
Invariant: In the studied UAE setup, semantic organization is best retained by selectively constraining a low-frequency base while leaving higher-frequency bands freer to acquire pixel detail; constraining none of the base weakens semantics, while constraining progressively more of the representation harms reconstruction.
CREATE: identify a subspace with an empirically supported role, anchor only that subspace to the desired prior, and leave complementary degrees available for specialization.
COPY: reproduce the division across multiple semantic encoders and test whether the same role separation survives changes in backbone and training configuration.
CONTROL: ablate both directions—remove the privileged constraint and expand it into residual bands—and measure the distinct semantic-versus-fidelity failure signatures rather than assuming more regularization is better.
CULTIVATE: learn or adapt the boundary dynamically, test alternative bases/orderings, and preserve the principle only where the role separation continues to survive intervention.
Compression: Preserve what must stay invariant; do not freeze the degrees that need to differentiate.

metabolites.title: Representation order can become computation order
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.IJnH:xy.
Invariant: When a latent representation is ordered from coarse/shared structure toward finer residual detail, generation can exploit that same order by modeling a compact structural subset first and progressively admitting additional detail.
CREATE: expose an information ordering in the representation rather than presenting all latent components as exchangeable.
COPY: reuse the ordering in spatial or frequency-domain generators while preserving the same coarse-to-fine dependency.
CONTROL: compare token budgets, convergence, generation quality, and reconstruction as progressively larger parts of the ordered representation are admitted.
CULTIVATE: allocate computation adaptively so examples or regions that already close at coarse rank need not pay the full cost of fine-detail modeling.
Compression: An information hierarchy can double as a compute schedule.

metabolites.title: Compression and generation can share a privileged structural base
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.IJnH:yz.
Invariant: In the studied visual models, compact low-frequency subsets can retain comparatively strong semantic utility while also improving early generative convergence and reducing computation, linking what is worth preserving under compression to what is useful to generate first.
CREATE: compress by retaining the empirically privileged structural subset rather than uniformly discarding information.
COPY: test whether the retained subset continues to support both representation quality and downstream generation across matched latent and pixel-space settings.
CONTROL: vary retained token count and measure semantic probing, generative convergence, reconstruction, FID/IS, and compute jointly so a gain on one axis cannot masquerade as general compression quality.
CULTIVATE: learn content-dependent token budgets and progressive refinement policies that preserve the shared structural base while spending additional bandwidth only where detail matters.
Compression: What survives compression best can also be what generation should establish first.

metabolites.title: A productive hypothesis need not be promoted into ontology
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.IJnH:wxyz.
Invariant: The Prism relation earns value because an observed spectral regularity motivates a concrete architecture whose behavior survives performance tests, ablations, and an implementation transfer; those successes still do not prove that frequency is the uniquely correct or universal coordinate of semantic versus detail information.
CREATE: convert an empirical regularity into a falsifiable design intervention instead of declaring the regularity fundamental at observation time.
COPY: reproduce the intervention across backbones, objectives, datasets, and implementation regimes while preserving the same bounded claim.
CONTROL: search for alternative decompositions, counterexamples, regimes where the spectral relation weakens, and architectures that achieve the same result through inequivalent coordinates.
CULTIVATE: retain the hypothesis as long as it continues to compress prediction and design choices; strengthen it only when alternatives are actually ruled out.
Compression: Engineering success can validate a handle without proving that the handle is the world’s unique axis.
