S.VjyQ.title: Testing One Simple Hypothesis Against Another

metabolites.title: LOCAL REARRANGEMENT CANONICALIZES WITHOUT PERFORMANCE LOSS
metabolites.text:
Bounded invariant: Under the source assumptions, likelihood-ratio-ordered acceptance/continuation regions can be earned by local probability-mass rearrangement while preserving or improving the relevant operating characteristics.
Minimal earning body: S.VjyQ:x
CREATE: construct a canonical local decision region from an arbitrary admissible one.
COPY: preserve the operating quantities that the replacement is obliged to carry.
CONTROL: constrain admissible rearrangement by likelihood-ratio order and probability balance.
CULTIVATE: compose the local replacement backward through additional stages.
Compression: canonical form can be derived locally rather than assumed globally.
metabolites.compression: canonical form can be derived locally rather than assumed globally.

metabolites.title: UNIFORM PROCEDURE DOMINANCE EXCEEDS EXPECTATION-ONLY OPTIMALITY
metabolites.text:
Bounded invariant: Comparing complete decision-time CDFs together with error behavior yields a stronger obligation than merely comparing expected sample size.
Minimal earning body: S.VjyQ:wz
CREATE: define a richer procedure comparison than a scalar expected-cost objective.
COPY: carry the full decision-time distribution and hypothesis-specific acceptance performance.
CONTROL: refuse replacements that improve one scalar while degrading another part of the distribution/error contract.
CULTIVATE: lift the stronger order into broader downstream decision/loss analyses.
Compression: a whole distribution can be the conserved performance object.
metabolites.compression: a whole distribution can be the conserved performance object.

metabolites.title: STAGE-DEPENDENT THRESHOLDS ARE A CANONICAL SEQUENTIAL FORM
metabolites.text:
Bounded invariant: Fixed Wald thresholds are not required for the paper's general domination result; predetermined stage-specific likelihood-ratio bounds provide a canonical class broad enough to dominate arbitrary eventually-decisive tests under the stated framework.
Minimal earning body: S.VjyQ:wxy
CREATE: admit time-varying decision boundaries.
COPY: preserve stage-indexed continuation/decision behavior under transformation.
CONTROL: keep each stage governed by likelihood-ratio threshold order.
CULTIVATE: extend canonicalization across the horizon instead of freezing one boundary pair.
Compression: canonical sequential control may require a trajectory of bounds, not one constant bound.
metabolites.compression: canonical sequential control may require a trajectory of bounds, not one constant bound.

metabolites.title: PROCEDURE ORDER LIFTS TO MONOTONE LOSS ORDER
metabolites.text:
Bounded invariant: If wrong decisions are no cheaper than correct ones and loss is nondecreasing in observation count as specified by the source, the uniformly better GSPRT stochastically improves the resulting loss distribution.
Minimal earning body: S.VjyQ:wz
CREATE: translate procedural dominance into a decision-theoretic consequence.
COPY: preserve the ordering through the loss map.
CONTROL: restrict the lift to the explicitly stated loss monotonicity/error-penalty assumptions.
CULTIVATE: reuse the procedural order for downstream choices without re-deriving a bespoke scalar criterion.
Compression: a lawful procedure order can survive a monotone decision-cost transformation.
metabolites.compression: a lawful procedure order can survive a monotone decision-cost transformation.

S.WW3e.title: The Shape of Word Embeddings
S.WW3e.boundary: All four diamonds are metabolites of exact arXiv v1 S.WW3e only. No claim from the later v2, another embedding family, another language family, Tetrix, or cross-paper recurrence is imported here. Cross-paper coalescence requires a separate later derivation.

edges.title: Label erasure × topology pipeline makes global shape independently measurable
edges.text: w removes token identity/correspondence as the information channel; x supplies a complete route from point-cloud topology to pairwise language distance and tree comparison. Together they derive an identifiable experimental object: representation-wide geometry can be tested for historical structure without relying on translation pairs or matching individual lexical items. Neither vertex alone earns that independence.

edges.title: Unlabeled-shape hypothesis × significant phylogenetic recovery
edges.text: w asks whether shape carries information beyond token semantics; y shows broad statistically significant agreement with Indo-European reference structure across many configurations after labels/cognates have already been discarded. Together they earn the bounded positive claim that unlabeled embedding geometry contains recoverable signal correlated with language history in the tested corpus.

edges.title: Shape hypothesis × fixed-topology control
edges.text: w attributes potential information to the point-cloud shape; z removes a major nuisance explanation by fixing the Ethnologue tree topology and varying only language-label assignment against the TDA distance matrices. The above-chance results persist, supporting the conclusion that the signal is not merely an accidental consequence of UPGMA/NJ producing a convenient tree shape.

edges.title: Analysis family × broad parameter-sweep recurrence
edges.text: x defines a combinatorial family of embedding metrics, homology dimensions, diagram representations/distances, language subsets, tree algorithms, and comparison metrics; y shows that significant results occupy a substantial portion of that family rather than one isolated winning configuration. Together they derive robustness to many analysis choices while preserving real method sensitivity.

edges.title: Pipeline construction × method-family diagnostics
edges.text: x makes every analytic transformation explicit; z then aggregates performance by those choices and shows systematic differences—e.g. dimension 1 generally stronger, sliced Wasserstein/bars statistics stronger than bottleneck/persistence-image variants in this setup, UPGMA often stronger than NJ at stringent thresholds. Together they derive that “TDA signal” is not one method but a family whose operators contribute materially to recoverability.

edges.title: Statistical recoverability × unresolved semantic mechanism
edges.text: y establishes reproducible phylogenetic correlation and also lists representation/reference limitations; z adds robustness tests plus the surprising informativeness of some low-persistence features. Together they derive a sharp boundary: a representation can contain statistically recoverable structure before the field knows which internal geometric/topological features correspond to which linguistic mechanisms or historical causes.

faces.title: Population geometry can carry information after element identities are erased
faces.text: Together, w + x + y derive the paper’s strongest empirical body: token identities and cross-language correspondences are removed; a topology-based point-cloud pipeline is applied; and resulting language distances recover phylogenetic structure far beyond permutation backgrounds across many parameter settings. Remove w and the identity-erasure distinction disappears; remove x and there is no measurement channel; remove y and there is no empirical recovery.

faces.title: Nuisance-preserving randomization can isolate the relational signal under test
faces.text: w specifies that the target information is global unlabeled shape rather than token identity; x constructs trees whose topology can itself bias tree-distance scores; z preserves each algorithmic topology while permuting labels, and separately fixes the Ethnologue topology while optimizing label assignments. Together they derive a methodological control principle: preserve nuisance structure while randomizing the hypothesized information channel so significance reflects the relation of interest rather than gross structural mismatch.

faces.title: Strong signal can coexist with weak interpretation
faces.text: w proposes an information-bearing geometric object; y reports broad/significant phylogenetic recovery but explicitly cannot explain which linguistic phenomena generate loops/voids/non-isometry; z shows that even topological features near an intuitive noise boundary can participate in useful aggregate discrimination. Together they derive that statistical information content and semantic interpretability are different epistemic achievements. Remove any one and the tension between signal, robustness, and mechanism is lost.

faces.title: Robust evidence lives in an analysis neighborhood, not a canonical winning recipe
faces.text: x defines many legitimate analytic choices; y shows a broad but nonuniform field of significant results; z diagnoses which families work better and shows alternate-topology controls agree directionally. Together they support a neighborhood-level conclusion: the phylogenetic signal is not reducible to one cherry-picked configuration, yet no unique TDA metric/tree construction is established as necessary or optimal.

volume.title: Representation-wide geometry can carry relational history beyond element-level correspondence
volume.text: The complete v1 carrier supports this bounded closure: monolingual FastText vocabularies, treated only as unlabeled high-dimensional point clouds, possess multiscale geometric/topological structure from which pairwise language distances can be derived. Across a large TDA/tree-comparison parameter sweep, those distances recover Indo-European phylogenetic organization substantially better than topology-preserving random labelings, and a supplementary fixed-reference-topology analysis preserves the above-chance relation. This demonstrates that cross-language embedding non-isometry can contain structured language-history signal that is not localized in token identities or explicit cognate/translation correspondences. However, the effect is conditioned on the tested FastText embeddings, Indo-European language sets, Ethnologue reference, preprocessing/metric/TDA/tree choices, and shallow accessible homology dimensions; the paper does not show that historical relatedness uniquely causes the geometry, identify what linguistic property individual topological features represent, or outperform dedicated cognate-based phylogenetics.

metabolites.title: Structure can survive removal of element identities
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.WW3e:wxy.
CREATE: Represent each population as an unlabeled relational/geometric object and deliberately remove element-to-element identity correspondences before measuring population structure.
COPY: Compare invariant or multiscale properties of the resulting populations so relational signal can recur even when no individual element has been matched across populations.
CONTROL: Verify the result against label-preserving/null permutations and against alternative population sizes/metrics; do not infer that the recovered relation is independent of how the representation itself was trained or sampled.
CULTIVATE: Use identity-erasure experiments whenever a representation may contain global organization beyond explicit symbols, testing what population-level information remains after the obvious correspondence channel is destroyed.
Compression: A system may remember relations in its global shape after the names of its parts are removed.
metabolites.compression: A system may remember relations in its global shape after the names of its parts are removed.

metabolites.title: Preserve nuisance structure while randomizing the information channel under test
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.WW3e:wxz.
CREATE: Identify a nuisance property that strongly affects the evaluation metric—here tree topology—and construct null samples that hold that nuisance property fixed while randomizing only the labels/assignment whose informativeness is being tested.
COPY: Repeated constrained randomizations generate a background distribution that retains the same structural difficulty as the observed object.
CONTROL: Compare the observed labeled relation to that constrained background; supplement with an alternate control that fixes the reference topology when feasible, and avoid nulls that change both topology and labels at once.
CULTIVATE: Design randomization tests around the causal/relational question rather than convenience: freeze every structural degree of freedom not presently under test, then randomize the suspected information-bearing degree.
Compression: A good null destroys the signal while preserving the nuisance structure that could fake it.
metabolites.compression: A good null destroys the signal while preserving the nuisance structure that could fake it.

metabolites.title: Robust evidence should occupy a neighborhood of analysis choices
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.WW3e:xyz.
CREATE: Define a principled family of plausible preprocessing, representation, metric, model, and evaluation choices before interpreting the best-performing configuration.
COPY: Track the sign/strength of the result across the family and report the population of successful configurations, not only the maximum statistic.
CONTROL: Use permutation/background tests for each configuration, inspect parameter-family asymmetries, and keep multiple-comparison/selection effects visible; recurrence across many choices supports robustness without making all choices equivalent.
CULTIVATE: Treat sensitivity maps as part of the scientific object: learn which transformations preserve the signal, which amplify it, and which destroy it, then use those boundaries to design stronger follow-up experiments.
Compression: Evidence is harder to dismiss as tuning luck when the signal occupies a region, not a single point, of the analysis space.
metabolites.compression: Evidence is harder to dismiss as tuning luck when the signal occupies a region, not a single point, of the analysis space.

metabolites.title: Statistical information can precede semantic interpretation
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.WW3e:wyz.
CREATE: Demonstrate that a representation supports reliable discrimination/prediction/correlation against a meaningful external structure even when the internal features carrying that information are not yet semantically decoded.
COPY: Reproduce the information signal across controls, parameter families, or related populations while keeping the unknown mechanism explicitly marked as unresolved.
CONTROL: Separate “contains recoverable information” from “we know what feature means,” “we know why it arose,” and “the external structure caused it”; use perturbations/alternate representations to close those stronger claims later.
CULTIVATE: Let robust predictive/statistical structure guide the next mechanistic experiments rather than either dismissing uninterpreted signal as meaningless or prematurely naming its internal semantics.
Compression: You can know that a representation carries information before you know what inside it carries the information.
metabolites.compression: You can know that a representation carries information before you know what inside it carries the information.

vertices.title: Unlabeled representation shape as an information-bearing object
vertices.text:
Source span: Abstract, Introduction, and Section 2 “Topological Data Analysis,” from the opening question through the persistent-homology construction and persistence-diagram representations, ending before the language-phylogeny/data section.
Nutrient: the conceptual and mathematical substrate: discard token identities and correspondence maps, treat each monolingual embedding vocabulary as a point cloud, and characterize its multiscale shape through persistent homology so population-level geometry can be compared without aligning individual words.

vertices.title: Topology-to-phylogeny measurement pipeline
vertices.text:
Source span: Sections 3–4, covering Indo-European reference trees/language subsets, FastText vocabulary construction, Euclidean/cosine metrics, persistence dimensions 0/1/2, persistence-diagram distances/representations, pairwise language-distance matrices, UPGMA/NJ reconstruction, six tree-comparison metrics, 100,000 label permutations, and the full parameter sweep, ending before Experiments/Results.
Nutrient: the operational transformation from unlabeled point cloud to testable historical structure: many explicitly varied TDA choices produce language-distance matrices, trees, and topology-preserving permutation backgrounds against which label-specific phylogenetic agreement can be measured.

vertices.title: Main empirical signal and explicit limits
vertices.text:
Source span: Section 5 Experiments/Results through Limitations and main References, ending before Supplemental Material.
Nutrient: the principal evidence and its boundaries: 144 reconstructed TDA trees × six tree metrics yield 864 evaluations; 484 are significant at empirical p≤0.05, 255 at ≤0.01, 57 at ≤0.001, ten at ≤0.0001, with a strongest reported 6.87σ result; signal varies by language set/method and is strongest in many 50-language cases. The source simultaneously limits interpretation by embedding family, reference-tree quality, metric/normalization/outlier choices, accessible homology dimension, and the unresolved question of what linguistic phenomena the topological features actually encode.

vertices.title: Supplementary controls and method-stress body
vertices.text:
Source span: Supplemental Material A.1–A.5 through the end of the carrier, including fixed-Ethnologue-topology label optimization, six tree-metric details, label-permutation significance procedure, aggregate significance tables, parameter-family comparisons, reference trees, significance plots, and persistence diagrams.
Nutrient: robustness/control tissue that tests alternate explanations and exposes method dependence: fixing the Ethnologue topology while optimizing only leaf labels still produces above-chance agreement for almost all TDA configurations; empirical-rank and z-score significance agree closely; dimension 1 generally performs best but low-persistence Euclidean dimension-2 features can still yield strong aggregate phylogenetic signal; sliced Wasserstein/bars statistics outperform some alternatives; and tree/metric choices remain consequential.

S.Wohx.title: The Hardness of Conditional Independence Testing and the Generalised Covariance Measure

metabolites.text:
Bounded invariant: No broadly assumption-light CI certificate exists in the paper’s stated absolutely-continuous continuous-conditioning class: uniform type-I control over the entire null forces power to remain at level against every alternative.
Minimal earning body: S.Wohx:x
CREATE: specify the admissible distribution class before creating a CI claim.
COPY: carry the exact null/alternative and conditioning-domain scope with every reuse.
CONTROL: reject universal nonedge conclusions that omit that scope.
CULTIVATE: seek explicit restricted classes or designed experiments that restore testability.
Compression: No restriction, no nontrivial universal CI certificate.
metabolites.compression: No restriction, no nontrivial universal CI certificate.

metabolites.text:
Bounded invariant: Testability and global distributional separation are distinct; CI can be untestable under uniform validity even when relevant null and alternative distributions are bounded apart in TV/KL, because the null class can still mimic finite-sample rejection behavior.
Minimal earning body: S.Wohx:xz
CREATE: distinguish rejection-event mimicry from global metric closeness.
COPY: preserve both the no-free-lunch theorem and the separation witness.
CONTROL: block “hard only because distributions are nearly identical” as an unsupported explanation.
CULTIVATE: inspect the geometry/richness of the null and the sample-level testing protocol.
Compression: Separation does not imply uniform testability.
metabolites.compression: Separation does not imply uniform testability.

metabolites.text:
Bounded invariant: Useful CI evidence is assumption-bounded evidence: a positive test inherits the model/design/estimation conditions that make its calibration possible, so those conditions belong in the certificate.
Minimal earning body: S.Wohx:xy
CREATE: build the witness together with its restriction contract.
COPY: propagate assumptions and guarantee class with the resulting edge/nonedge statement.
CONTROL: prevent a restricted or asymptotic guarantee from being promoted to universal observational independence.
CULTIVATE: improve or experimentally ground the assumptions instead of hiding them.
Compression: The assumptions are part of the witness.
metabolites.compression: The assumptions are part of the witness.

metabolites.text:
Bounded invariant: For the GCM route, regression quality enters through a decomposable approximation budget: the product of nuisance prediction errors controls the leading bias, weighted errors control stochastic remainders, and high-dimensional/RKHS variants add explicit moment, covariance-approximation and spectral/tuning requirements.
Minimal earning body: S.Wohx:yz

S.YFs0.title: Nash Identity Safe
S.YFs0.boundary: All four diamonds are metabolites of S.YFs0 only. They describe what the public architecture constructs and what its own maturity boundary permits. No empirical effectiveness, EEG uniqueness, coercion-detection accuracy, production readiness, or cross-paper universality is claimed here.

edges.title: Human authorization × capability release
edges.text: w distinguishes possession/identity from intentional human authorization; x realizes that distinction as a local ceremony that withholds the cryptographic authorization output until multiple local conditions are satisfied. Together they derive the architecture’s core object: authentication is no longer merely proof that a credential exists, but a gate on whether high-impact capability is released now.

edges.title: Revocability/local-first philosophy × sovereignty boundaries
edges.text: w declares revocable cognitive factors and local-first privacy; y locates raw signals, model comparison, and policy enforcement inside a trusted local boundary while giving users re-enrollment/consent rights. Together they derive a privacy architecture in which human-state evidence is intended to remain a private input to authorization rather than become a reusable platform identity asset.

edges.title: Security ambition × explicit maturity boundary
edges.text: w makes broad design claims about human-aware, quantum-safe authorization; z places research prototype, security architecture, hardware evaluation, pilot deployment, and external review in future phases and disclaims warranties. Together they derive a strict epistemic boundary: the white paper specifies intended properties and a path to test them; it does not report that those properties have already survived that path.

edges.title: Private multimodal evidence × remote cryptographic proof
edges.text: x defines local cognitive/EEG/distress evaluation followed by post-quantum authorization release; y insists relying parties receive proofs/attestations rather than raw brain/body data. Together they derive a separation of evidence from outcome: sensitive local evidence can contribute to a decision without becoming the data transmitted to the verifier.

edges.title: Standards-backed crypto × unvalidated composite assurance
edges.text: x includes concrete standardized primitives such as ML-KEM and future ML-DSA/SLH-DSA directions alongside proprietary cognitive/EEG mechanisms; z shows the latter still require prototyping, hardware evaluation, and external review. Together they derive that standardized cryptography can strengthen one layer without validating the security, liveness, coercion sensitivity, or usability of the complete stack.

edges.title: High-assurance use cases × governance/deployment restriction
edges.text: y proposes digital-asset, enterprise, AI-agent, secure-communication, and defense/high-assurance applications while also defining threat and ethical controls; z’s roadmap and license restrict current use to evaluation and prohibit high-risk production use absent separate authorization. Together they derive that the public carrier presents intended application domains, not evidence of readiness for those domains.

faces.title: Authorization can be treated as a local policy transformation rather than a remote biometric lookup
faces.text: Together, w + x + y derive the architecture’s deepest constructive move: private human-presence/state evidence is gathered and evaluated locally, combined with possession/knowledge and cryptographic state, and transformed into a remote authorization outcome. w supplies the distinction between credential and authorization; x supplies the ceremony; y supplies the trust/privacy boundary. Remove any one and the system collapses toward conventional MFA, raw-biometric verification, or an undefined privacy claim.

faces.title: A new authentication factor is only as mature as its validation ladder
faces.text: w motivates cognitive/coercion-aware factors, x specifies how they would participate in authorization, and z reveals that prototype, security architecture, hardware evaluation, pilots, and external review remain future phases. Together they derive a staged validation requirement: a plausible factor design is not an earned authentication assurance level until liveness, false accept/reject behavior, spoofing, coercion discrimination, recovery, and hardware integration are actually tested.

faces.title: User sovereignty is architectural only when it survives deployment and governance
faces.text: w declares local-first privacy/revocability; y encodes no raw-cloud extraction, consent, re-enrollment, transparent safety modes, and no raw relying-party access; z constrains current evaluation and calls for external privacy/biometric-ethics review. Together they derive that “user sovereignty” is not a slogan attached to a sensor—it is a set of enforceable information-flow, revocation, consent, and review properties that must survive implementation.

faces.title: Human checkpoints can bound delegated machine action without giving agents the human credential
faces.text: x ends a local ceremony in a cryptographic authorization release; y names AI-agent delegation as a use case in which an agent may prepare a high-impact action but a human must release final authorization; z keeps this as a proposed/pilot-stage architecture rather than a proven safety guarantee. Together they derive a clean delegation pattern: automation can possess planning/execution capability while final authority remains behind a separate human-local gate.

volume.title: Separate credential possession, private human evidence, and authority release
volume.text: The complete white paper constructs a security architecture in which high-impact authority is not equated with possession of a password, token, biometric resemblance, or agent capability. Instead, a trusted local device is proposed to combine revocable cognitive participation, live local EEG/liveness evidence, optional coercion-risk signals, possession/knowledge factors, and post-quantum cryptography, then release only a cryptographic authorization outcome to the external system. This creates a conceptual separation between who/what holds a credential, the private evidence used to judge a local authorization event, and the capability that is finally released. The architecture also explicitly aims to make cognitive factors revocable and raw evidence non-exportable. However, the same full carrier makes clear that the composite system is a design-stage object: proprietary implementation details are withheld and the roadmap still requires prototypes, formal threat architecture, hardware evaluation, pilots, and external review. The paper therefore earns an authorization/trust-boundary architecture, not an empirical claim that EEG/cognitive/coercion verification or end-to-end security has been demonstrated.

metabolites.title: Identity evidence is not the same object as authorization
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.YFs0:wxy.
CREATE: Separate the questions “is this the recognized credential/user?” from “should this high-impact action be authorized under the present local conditions?” and give the latter its own gate.
COPY: Across protected operations, preserve the rule that valid possession/identity evidence is necessary but can remain insufficient when policy requires current participation, intent, state, or contextual checks.
CONTROL: Define exactly which local conditions may block or reroute authorization, how false rejection/recovery works, and which conditions are merely risk signals rather than identity facts.
CULTIVATE: Apply the separation selectively to actions whose consequence justifies an explicit authorization ceremony, instead of inflating every low-risk login into a high-friction ritual.
Compression: Knowing who holds the credential does not by itself answer whether authority should be released now.
metabolites.compression: Knowing who holds the credential does not by itself answer whether authority should be released now.

metabolites.title: Private evidence can remain local while authorization travels
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.YFs0:xy.
CREATE: Evaluate sensitive biometric/cognitive/state evidence inside a trusted local boundary and convert the local policy result into a cryptographic proof, attestation, commitment, or signature.
COPY: Remote relying parties repeatedly consume the authorization outcome without needing the underlying raw EEG, physiological telemetry, or cognitive profile.
CONTROL: Minimize proof contents, bind them to action/session/context, protect local compute and enrollment, prevent relying-party access to raw signals, and audit that privacy does not silently erode through logs or recovery paths.
CULTIVATE: Extend privacy-preserving authorization by making attestations progressively more selective and unlinkable where possible, while preserving enough verifiability for the actual relying-party risk.
Compression: The verifier may need proof of a local decision, not possession of the evidence that produced it.
metabolites.compression: The verifier may need proof of a local decision, not possession of the evidence that produced it.

metabolites.title: Revocability changes the security meaning of a human-derived factor
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.YFs0:wy.
CREATE: Encode a human-derived authentication factor as a retrainable/rotatable challenge-response profile rather than treating an immutable body trait itself as the permanent credential.
COPY: Future ceremonies compare against the current local profile; compromise can be answered by invalidating/re-enrolling the profile rather than assuming the underlying biological trait can be changed.
CONTROL: Demonstrate that re-enrollment actually produces independent/revocable security material and that attackers cannot reconstruct or replay an old factor from leaked outputs; avoid calling a factor revocable merely because its software wrapper can be reset.
CULTIVATE: Prefer human-derived factors whose exposed representation can be rotated or re-keyed, while empirically testing stability, accessibility, liveness, and false-match behavior over time.
Compression: A human-derived factor is safer to compromise when the credential representation can change even though the human cannot.
metabolites.compression: A human-derived factor is safer to compromise when the credential representation can change even though the human cannot.

metabolites.title: Standardized components do not validate a composite security system
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.YFs0:wxz.
CREATE: Combine mature/standardized primitives with novel sensing, modeling, enrollment, policy, hardware, and recovery mechanisms into one security architecture.
COPY: The standardized subcomponents can remain well specified while uncertainty persists at interfaces and novel factors; reproducing the architecture diagram does not remove that uncertainty.
CONTROL: Validate every novel factor and interface independently, then test end-to-end failure modes, red-team behavior, usability, recovery, false accept/reject rates, coercion/spoof robustness, side channels, and hardware trust before assigning deployment-grade assurance.
CULTIVATE: Use standards as stable anchors in the validation program while progressively replacing architectural promises with measured properties and externally reviewed guarantees.
Compression: A system does not inherit end-to-end assurance merely because some of its parts are standardized.

vertices.title: Authentication is reframed as human authorization
vertices.text:
Source span: public-release notice through Sections 1–5: Abstract, Executive Summary, the authentication-without-human-assurance problem, five design principles, and the relationship to Plurigrid/passport.gay, ending before System Overview.
Nutrient: the conceptual redesign: possession, knowledge, and static biometrics are treated as insufficient for high-impact authorization because the correct credential can be stolen, coerced, or exercised without meaningful human participation. The proposed object is a local human-authorization safe governed by privacy, revocability, post-quantum migration, and coercion awareness.

vertices.title: Local ceremony converts multimodal participation into cryptographic release
vertices.text:
Source span: Sections 6–10: System Overview, Cognitive-Color Challenge-Response, Proof-of-Brain as Final Authentication Factor, Post-Quantum Cryptographic Architecture, and Coercion-Aware Authentication.
Nutrient: the operational design sequence: device possession + local secret + revocable cognitive challenge + live local EEG evaluation + optional distress-risk modulation + post-quantum secure channel culminate in release of an authorization proof/attestation/signature. Raw cognitive or physiological evidence is not the remote credential.

vertices.title: Trust boundaries, threat surface, applications, and user sovereignty
vertices.text:
Source span: Sections 11–17: Privacy Architecture, Device Architecture, Security Model, comparison to existing authentication models, use cases, Nash ecosystem context, and Ethics and Governance.
Nutrient: where authority and sensitive data are supposed to live: raw EEG/cognitive profiles stay local, relying parties receive cryptographic outcomes, profiles are revocable, host devices should not control the ceremony, threat categories are explicit, AI-agent delegation is gated by a human checkpoint, and governance commitments constrain data extraction and deployment.

vertices.title: Development status, legal boundary, and source provenance
vertices.text:
Source span: Sections 18–19 plus Appendix A and References: Roadmap, Conclusion, restrictive evaluation license/terms, and cited sources.
Nutrient: the maturity/control boundary: prototype, formal security architecture, hardware evaluation, bounded pilots, and external review are future work; the technology is offered for restricted evaluation with no warranties and high-risk-use limits; references ground PQ standards and motivating external work but do not convert the proposed composite system into an empirically validated product.

edges.title: Population/lattice mechanics make disjoint refinement and coarsening regions addressable, enabling the lower-diamond additive comparison.
Newest-vertex-bisection conformity means the cost of selecting one edge includes its forced closure; marking must score that coupled repair rather than the isolated edge.
Ancestry, descendants, genetic diversity, and free-person structure connect local mesh growth to competitor cardinality.
Lower-diamond energy localization plus estimator equivalence converts local indicator sums into comparable total-energy decrements.
The lower-diamond law transfers into populations, making comparisons against optimal populations stable across independent coarsenings.
edges.text:
zy — Modified maximum marking guarantees sufficient per-step energy decrease, while free-node and mesh-complexity bounds convert that local decrease into finite energy and instance optimality.


FOUR FACE RELATIONS
wxz — refinement geometry + lower-diamond energy + closure-aware estimators form a local-to-global accounting system.
wxy — population order + lower-diamond localization + free-node conservation stabilize competitor comparisons under further refinement.
wzy — conformity-aware marking + population combinatorics make the selection policy part of the theorem’s guarantee class, not an implementation detail.
xzy — total-energy decrement + modified maximum marking + comparator geometry establish mesh-by-mesh near-bestness up to explicit constants and cardinality slack.


ONE VOLUME
In the source’s two-dimensional Poisson / P1 / conforming-NVB setting, a no-coarsening AFEM can be non-asymptotically instance-optimal for total error because four witnesses close together: admissible refinements form a structured population lattice; energy differences localize through a lower-diamond law; edge indicators track total-energy change including oscillation; and modified maximum marking prices conformity-induced closure, while genetic-diversity/free-node bounds control competitor cardinality. The theorem is finite instance optimality up to constants and a cardinality factor C scaling like 1/mu^2; it is not plain-energy instance optimality and not a universal AFEM theorem.


SURVIVING METABOLITES — 4
1. Finite near-bestness is stronger than asymptotic rate matching. Class optimality does not certify each realized state against a comparable-size best competitor.
2. Selection cost includes closure debt. When one local action forces coupled repairs for validity or conformity, its priority score must include the whole forced closure.
3. Representation debt belongs inside the certified objective. Here total error includes oscillation; the theorem does not license dropping that debt merely because it can be asymptotically higher order.
4. Instance certificates require structural conservation. Local progress becomes global near-bestness only with explicit combinatorial bounds linking chosen edits, removable structure, and total growth.


BOUNDARY / REFUSALS
- The theorem is bounded to the stated Poisson, polygonal-domain, P1, conforming newest-vertex-bisection setting and the paper’s modified maximum strategy.
- Instance optimality is for total error; the paper explicitly does not establish the analogous result for plain energy error alone.
- The comparison carries multiplicative constants and cardinality slack; it is not literal exact minimum work at every step.
- The 2016 version of record is distinct provenance from the metabolized arXiv v2 carrier.
- No substrate-general law of selective computation is imported by analogy.

edges.title: Environment-conditioned legality becomes a compositional contract
edges.text: w supplies the asymmetric assumption/guarantee interpretation and the optimistic compatibility pressure; x supplies the formal product, illegal-state, environment, compatible-state, and composition machinery. Together they earn a precise open-system claim: incompatibility is not merely the presence of a potential mismatch in a raw product but the absence of a legal environment that can keep the interaction away from it. Without w, the formal pruning lacks its contract interpretation; without x, optimism remains a motivation rather than an executable compatibility relation.

edges.title: Role polarity determines the direction of safe refinement
edges.text: w supplies the distinction between environment-controlled inputs and component-controlled outputs; y supplies alternating refinement. Together they earn the contravariant revision law: a replacement may weaken assumptions on the environment by accepting more inputs while strengthening guarantees by restricting component-controlled outputs on the shared contract. Without w, the opposite variance of inputs and outputs is unmotivated; without y, the polarity has no formal replacement relation.

edges.title: Execution assumptions license specialization without universalizing it
edges.text: w supplies the general open-component contract and its division of control; z supplies the stronger single-threaded ownership discipline. Together they earn that a structural simplification may be valid because an execution model rules out interactions that the general contract must otherwise retain. Without w, specialization can be mistaken for the general interface law; without z, no execution-specific reduction is earned.

edges.title: Refinement becomes conditional substitutability
edges.text: x supplies compatibility/composition as an environment-sensitive relation; y supplies alternating refinement and Theorem 4. Together they earn the paper's drop-in replacement result: under the stated input-side condition, replacing a component by a refinement preserves compatibility with the environment and composes with local refinement. Without x, refinement has no compatibility target to preserve; without y, compatibility alone says nothing about replacement across versions.

edges.title: Semantic compatibility and execution ownership jointly justify pruning
edges.text: x supplies general incompatible-state pruning under optimistic environment semantics; z supplies the additional input-step pruning justified by single-threaded ownership. Together they earn a two-stage principle: state/transition removal is semantics-preserving only when the relevant interaction semantics or execution discipline proves the removed behavior unusable. Without x, pruning lacks the general compatibility baseline; without z, the stronger single-threaded reduction is unjustified.

edges.title: Semantic revision and operational specialization are distinct
edges.text:
y supplies a behavioral refinement preorder over interfaces; z supplies an execution-model specialization that reduces representation while retaining compatibility semantics under its assumptions. Together they earn that making an implementation representation smaller is not itself a refinement claim, and refining a contract does not by itself authorize execution-specific pruning. Without y, version/substitution semantics disappear; without z, the distinction between contract evolution and operational reduction is not exposed.


4 FACES — RANK-3 NECESSITY


S.aeHL:wxy — Drop-in continuity requires typed obligations, contextual compatibility, and directional refinement
w identifies environment assumptions versus component guarantees; x defines legal-context compatibility and composition; y defines contravariant refinement and its compatibility-preservation theorem. Together they earn the source's central replacement discipline: a revised interface is safely substitutable not because names or observed traces match, but because the interaction roles have the correct variance and the refined component remains compatible with the old environment under explicit side conditions. Remove w and the roles lose polarity; remove x and there is no environmental compatibility obligation; remove y and there is no directional replacement relation.


S.aeHL:wxz — Compatibility-preserving reduction requires both interaction semantics and execution ownership
w supplies the open-system control split, x supplies optimistic composition/pruning, and z supplies the single-threaded ownership constraint. Together they earn why some transitions/states can be deleted only after the environment/game semantics and execution model jointly make them unreachable in legitimate interaction. Remove w and ownership has no contract role; remove x and there is no formal compatibility-preserving baseline; remove z and the extra reduction is not justified.


S.aeHL:wyz — Contract evolution and implementation specialization must not be conflated
w supplies the asymmetric public contract, y supplies semantic refinement across versions, and z supplies representation reduction under a stronger execution model. Together they earn that a system may change along two independent axes: its public obligations can refine while its internal/interface representation can also specialize, but neither change licenses the other. Remove w and there is no public obligation surface; remove y and no version relation; remove z and no distinct operational-specialization axis.


S.aeHL:xyz — Compositional verification can stage three guarded reductions
x supplies compatibility pruning and associative composition, y supplies local refinement and compositional substitutability, and z supplies single-threaded state-space reduction. Together they earn a staged verification architecture in which incompatible behavior is removed, replacement is checked locally, and execution-specific structure may be compressed—each under a different semantic guard. Remove x and incompatibility cannot be pruned compositionally; remove y and version replacement cannot be certified; remove z and the execution-specific reduction disappears.


1 VOLUME — RANK-4 CLOSURE


S.aeHL:wxyz — Bounded volume invariant
Interface Automata provides a directional calculus for open component contracts. A component interface separates assumptions controlled by its environment from guarantees/outputs controlled by the component. Compatibility is existential and contextual: two components are compatible when some legal environment can keep their composition away from illegal interactions, and the incompatible region can be computed and pruned. Safe refinement is contravariant across the assumption/guarantee boundary: a replacement may accept more environmental inputs while producing a behavior set no broader than the specification permits, and under the paper's stated input-side condition this refinement preserves compatibility compositionally. Stronger execution assumptions such as a single-threaded control discipline can justify additional state/transition pruning without redefining the public compatibility relation.


Therefore operation-name equality, raw trace inclusion, or “more features” is insufficient evidence of safe replacement. Substitutability is an interaction property with directional obligations and explicit context conditions. Conversely, a change that violates those conditions is not silently continuous merely because it can be made to work after adapting the environment.


Evidence boundary of the volume: this is a formal result for the paper's interface-automata model. The formalism cannot express required inputs without extensions such as fairness/synchrony/real-time constraints; Theorem 4 has an explicit side condition for compatibility-preserving substitution; single-threaded reduction is conditional on that execution model; and the source does not formalize epistemic evidence/claim boundaries.


COLLAPSED METABOLITES


INV-S.aeHL-01 — ASSUMPTION/GUARANTEE POLARITY
Bounded invariant: In an open component contract, environment-controlled inputs and component-controlled outputs have opposite refinement variance. A safe refinement can accept at least the old legal inputs while restricting—not expanding—the component-controlled outputs on the preserved contract.
Minimal earning body: wy.
CREATE: type each interaction by who controls it before defining replacement.
COPY: preserve the input/output polarity across versions and compositions.
CONTROL: reject “refinement” claims that silently demand more from old environments or expose new uncontrolled outputs on the preserved contract.
CULTIVATE: when an obligation must genuinely reverse or retire this polarity, represent the change as migration rather than silent refinement.
Compression: safe replacement weakens assumptions and strengthens guarantees.


INV-S.aeHL-02 — CONTEXTUAL COMPATIBILITY
Bounded invariant: For interface automata, open-component compatibility is the existence of a legal environment that can avoid illegal interactions, not the absence of every potentially illegal state in the raw product.
Minimal earning body: wx.
CREATE: build the product and identify mismatched shared actions as illegal interaction states.
COPY: carry environmental control explicitly when composing more components.
CONTROL: prune states from which output/internal behavior can force illegality despite the best environment.
CULTIVATE: add stronger liveness/fairness/time obligations only as explicit extensions when “may input” is insufficient.
Compression: compatibility is what some legal context can sustain, not what every imaginable context survives.


INV-S.aeHL-03 — CONDITIONAL SUBSTITUTABILITY
Bounded invariant: Alternating refinement can preserve compatibility and compose locally, but only under the source's stated conditions—especially the restriction preventing an old environment from exercising newly introduced inputs in ways the old specification never covered.
Minimal earning body: xy.
CREATE: compute an alternating-simulation witness between specification and replacement.
COPY: carry the refinement relation through compatible compositions when the side conditions hold.
CONTROL: audit shared/new input connectivity before claiming drop-in substitution.
CULTIVATE: when the side condition fails, test or adapt the specific environment and record migration debt rather than declaring universal replacement.
Compression: refinement is a substitutability theorem with a context boundary, not a synonym for “newer implementation.”


INV-S.aeHL-04 — SEMANTICALLY GUARDED PRUNING
Bounded invariant: Representation can be reduced by removing interactions that are provably unusable under the governing semantic/execution contract; stronger reductions require stronger assumptions. General composition prunes incompatibility-forcing states, while single-threaded composition additionally prunes inputs excluded by thread ownership.
Minimal earning body: xz.
CREATE: establish the semantic or execution condition that makes behavior unreachable.
COPY: preserve the public compatibility meaning while reducing the representation.
CONTROL: forbid pruning whose impossibility witness depends on an unstated execution assumption.
CULTIVATE: specialize further only when a stronger execution discipline is explicitly earned.
Compression: delete behavior only after the contract proves it cannot participate.


COLLAPSE WITNESS
Four metabolites survive removal tests. INV-01 carries the fundamental directional role polarity; INV-02 carries contextual compatibility independent of versioning; INV-03 carries the conditional replacement theorem; INV-04 carries semantics-preserving reduction under progressively stronger assumptions. The single-threaded specialization is not retained as its own broad universal rule beyond INV-04, and the acquisition receipt's proposed epistemic evidence-boundary analogy is not promoted because the source does not formalize it.


PLACEMENT WARRANT
Root z — Governance / CONTROL is the smallest realized living locus that truthfully accounts for this source. The paper's durable contribution governs admissible interaction, compatibility, replacement, and pruning through explicit directional constraints. It is not primarily a generative mechanism (w), a carrier/correspondence law (x), or a developmental/adaptive process (y). INDEX.yaml shows z as a realized unsplit locus, so no new semantic depth is created merely to store this organism.

vertices.title: Open components as asymmetric contracts
vertices.text:
Source span: PDF pages 1–3 · printed pp. 109–111.
Nutrient: The paper motivates interface automata as lightweight temporal interfaces for components that are not input-enabled. Inputs denote assumptions about what an environment may ask of a component; outputs denote guarantees/behaviors controlled by the component. The motivating User/Comp/Channel example contrasts pessimistic composition, which rejects any reachable potential mismatch, with an optimistic view: components are compatible when there exists an environment that can steer their joint use away from illegal interactions.
Boundary carried by this body: this is a formal modeling proposal and motivating semantics, not an empirical law of all interfaces.

vertices.title: Compatibility, composition, legal environments, and pruning
vertices.text:
Source span: PDF pages 4–8 · printed pp. 112–116.
Nutrient: The paper formally defines interface automata, composability, product, illegal states, environments, compatible states, and composition. Compatibility is environment-sensitive: incompatible product states are those from which the environment cannot prevent an output/internal trajectory into an illegal mismatch. Algorithm 1 computes compatible states by backward reachability through output/internal steps; composition prunes incompatible states and then unreachable residue. Composition is associative, enabling staged compatibility checking. The paper also states a limitation: the formalism can express which inputs may occur but not which inputs must occur; fairness, synchrony, or real-time constraints would be needed for stronger liveness-style obligations and are outside scope.
Boundary carried by this body: optimistic compatibility can be witnessed by an environment that produces no inputs; the source therefore does not encode required-input liveness.

vertices.title: Contravariant refinement and conditional substitutability
vertices.text:
Source span: PDF pages 9–10 · printed pp. 117–118.
Nutrient: Ordinary trace containment is rejected as the right refinement relation for non-input-enabled interfaces because a useful implementation may accept additional inputs/services while preserving the original contract. The paper defines alternating simulation and interface refinement with contravariant action typing: a refinement may admit at least the specification's inputs while exposing no more outputs than the specification permits on the shared contract. Refinement is a preorder. Theorem 4 connects refinement to compatibility and composition: under its stated input-side condition, a refined component can replace its specification in a compatible environment, and refinement composes locally. Algorithm 2 computes the maximal alternating simulation; refinement checking is PTIME-complete.
Boundary carried by this body: substitutability is conditional; new inputs used by the environment can introduce new incompatibilities, so refinement is not a blanket guarantee for arbitrary migrated contexts.

vertices.title: Single-threaded specialization and semantic-preserving reduction
vertices.text:
Source span: PDF pages 11–12 · printed pp. 119–120.
Nutrient: The paper specializes interface automata to single-threaded systems by separating running and waiting states and exploiting ownership of the sole active thread. It defines single-threaded composition, which removes input steps that cannot occur under this execution discipline and prunes newly unreachable states. The specialized composition is associative and can substantially reduce state space; ordinary and single-threaded formulations retain the same compatibility criterion for composable single-threaded interfaces under the stated construction.
Boundary carried by this body: this reduction depends on the single-threaded execution model and cannot be generalized to arbitrary concurrent systems without re-earning the assumptions.

S.atV2.title: Equivalence of Dynamical Systems by Bisimulation

edges.title: Process equivalence becomes computable and compressive
edges.text: w supplies the symmetric continuation-preserving relation and the fact that traces alone may be too coarse; x supplies maximal-relation computation and quotient reduction. Together they earn that process sameness is not merely definitional: in the paper's linear setting it can be tested through an explicit maximal relation and then used to remove exactly those internal distinctions that do not affect the preserved continuation obligations. Without w there is no process-equivalence criterion to preserve; without x there is no earned reduction/computation consequence.

edges.title: Branching semantics determine whether trace equality is sufficient
edges.text: w supplies the nondeterministic gap between external behavior and bisimulation; y supplies the deterministic theorem where equality of external behavior collapses back to bisimilarity. Together they earn a sharp regime distinction: the need for a finer process relation is driven by admissible branching/disturbance structure rather than by external-output vocabulary alone. Without w there is no failure case; without y there is no bounded condition under which the distinction disappears.

edges.title: The process-equivalence membrane survives a change of carrier class
edges.text: w supplies the linear trajectory-matching definition/characterization; z supplies its nonlinear reformulation with submanifolds and controlled-invariant geometry. Together they earn that the constitutive idea is not tied uniquely to linear coordinates, while simultaneously showing that formal realization and computability depend on carrier-specific regularity. Without w the nonlinear extension lacks the source's base relation; without z there is no evidence that the relation survives beyond the linear substrate.

edges.title: Classical minimal realization is a special case of bisimulation reduction
edges.text: x supplies maximal self-bisimulation and quotient reduction; y supplies the deterministic collapse and recovery of classical state-space equivalence. Together they earn that familiar deterministic realization equivalence sits inside the broader bisimulation/reduction framework rather than constituting an unrelated notion of sameness. Without x there is no quotient/minimality route; without y there is no bridge to the classical deterministic case.

edges.title: Reduction generalizes from invariant subspaces to invariant foliations
edges.text: x supplies linear controlled-invariant quotient machinery; z supplies nonlinear controlled-invariant distributions/submanifolds and quotient foliations. Together they earn a bounded structural recurrence: process-preserving reduction is implemented as quotienting along relation-preserving geometry, although the nonlinear version requires additional regularity. Without x the reduction mechanism has no formal linear base; without z its cross-carrier extension is not earned.

edges.title: Nondeterministic continuation, not linearity, is the load-bearing distinction
edges.text:
y supplies the deterministic theorem equating external behavior with bisimilarity; z supplies a nonlinear counterexample where external behavior still fails to determine bisimulation because deadlock/continuation differs. Together they earn that linear versus nonlinear is not the decisive boundary for trace sufficiency: determinacy/branching semantics remain load-bearing. Without y there is no deterministic collapse; without z one could incorrectly attribute the gap only to the linear disturbance construction.


4 FACES — RANK-3 NECESSITY


S.atV2:wxy — Process sameness licenses reduction only when continuation obligations are preserved
w distinguishes external traces from symmetric continuation-preserving equivalence; x shows how that equivalence supports maximal computation and quotient reduction; y identifies the deterministic regime where trace equality itself becomes sufficient. Together they earn an obligation-sensitive reduction law: internal state can be collapsed only to the extent that the chosen process-equivalence obligation survives, with deterministic external behavior as a bounded special case. Remove w and reduction loses its stronger continuation criterion; remove x and no compression consequence follows; remove y and the special trace-sufficient regime is missing.


S.atV2:wxz — Bisimulation is structurally portable but operationally substrate-bounded
w supplies the core relational obligation, x supplies constructive linear computation/reduction, and z supplies nonlinear generalization with regularity conditions. Together they earn that the same process-equivalence membrane can survive representation-class change without implying that one algorithm or quotient construction works unchanged everywhere. Remove w and there is no invariant relation; remove x and constructive linear closure is absent; remove z and portability beyond linear systems is unearned.


S.atV2:wyz — Equality of external behavior is sufficient only under the right evolution semantics
w supplies the nondeterministic counterexample and symmetric relation; y supplies deterministic equivalence; z supplies a nonlinear deadlock counterexample and extension. Together they earn that the adequacy of trace/interface equality depends on the evolution semantics, not simply on coordinate form or linearity. Remove w and the process relation is not defined sharply; remove y and the sufficiency regime disappears; remove z and the conclusion could remain an artifact of the linear model class.


S.atV2:xyz — Equivalence and abstraction require different directional obligations
x supplies quotient/reduction consequences, y distinguishes one-way simulation from symmetric bisimulation and recovers deterministic equivalence, and z shows the generalization/regularity boundary. Together they earn that reduction, abstraction, and process identity should not be conflated: one-way simulation may suffice for some specification/abstraction obligations, whereas symmetric bisimulation licenses equivalence, and both remain model-class bounded. Remove x and no reduction consequence is present; remove y and directionality is absent; remove z and the scope/regularity boundary is missing.


1 VOLUME — RANK-4 CLOSURE


S.atV2:wxyz — Bounded volume invariant
A system-level notion of "same process" that is weaker than mechanism identity yet stronger than equal externally observed traces is earned by symmetric continuation-preserving bisimulation: related states must match admissible external input-output behavior while remaining related under all allowed internal/disturbance evolutions in both directions. In the paper's linear setting this equivalence admits an algebraic characterization, a maximal-relation algorithm, and state-space quotient reduction. In deterministic systems the distinction collapses—equality of external behavior implies bisimilarity and recovers classical state-space equivalence—whereas nondeterministic systems can share all external traces while differing in branching/deadlock futures and therefore fail to be bisimilar. The relation extends toward nonlinear systems through controlled-invariant submanifold/foliation machinery under stated regularity assumptions.


Evidence boundary of the volume: this is a formal theorem-and-construction result inside the paper's system classes, not a claim that bisimulation establishes physical/mechanistic identity, not a universal process ontology, and not a proof that all hybrid, stochastic, computational, or biological systems admit the same characterization or quotient.

vertices.title: Bisimulation definition, characterization, and the external-behavior gap
vertices.text:
Source span: printed pp. 2160–2163.
Nutrient: The paper defines bisimulation for input-state-output systems as a symmetric relation over states: under the same external input, every admissible disturbance-driven trajectory from either side must have a matching trajectory on the other side, preserve the state relation through time, and produce equal outputs. Bisimilarity is treated as an equivalence relation under the stated surjectivity conditions. For linear systems the relation receives an algebraic/geometric-control characterization. Crucially, bisimilarity implies equality of external behavior, but in nondeterministic systems the converse can fail: equal external traces can conceal different branching, derivative, or deadlock structure.
Boundary carried by this body: the formalism is not mechanism identity; it is process equivalence relative to the specified state/input/output/disturbance semantics.

vertices.title: Maximal relation, algorithm, and quotient reduction
vertices.text:
Source span: printed pp. 2163–2166.
Nutrient: If any bisimulation relation exists, a maximal one exists. The paper supplies a descending-subspace algorithm for computing it in the linear setting and a fixed-point criterion for bisimilarity. A bisimulation relation of a system with itself defines state equivalence; quotienting by the associated controlled-invariant subspace produces a lower-dimensional system that remains bisimilar. The maximal self-relation yields the strongest reduction available under this criterion, and general bisimulation relations factor through reduced systems connected by a one-to-one relation.
Boundary carried by this body: reduction is licensed only by the preserved bisimulation obligations; dimensional compression is not independently evidence of equivalence.

vertices.title: Simulation, abstraction, and the deterministic collapse
vertices.text:
Source span: printed pp. 2166–2168.
Nutrient: Simulation is introduced as the one-sided variant of bisimulation and is tied to abstraction/specification obligations. In the linear continuous-time setting considered, mutual simulation can be combined into bisimulation. The paper then specializes to deterministic systems and proves the key boundary result: equality of external behavior implies bisimilarity. Transfer/Markov-parameter equality characterizes the existence of a bisimulation relation, and for controllable/observable deterministic systems this recovers classical state-space equivalence through an invertible state transformation.
Boundary carried by this body: the collapse from trace equality to process equivalence depends on determinism and the paper's stated system assumptions; it is not a universal theorem for arbitrary computational or stochastic processes.

vertices.title: Nonlinear extension, regularity limits, and outlook
vertices.text:
Source span: printed pp. 2169–2172.
Nutrient: The paper extends the bisimulation/simulation vocabulary to nonlinear systems using submanifolds, controlled-invariant distributions, and quotient foliations under smoothness/regularity assumptions. A nonlinear example again shows equal external behavior without bisimilarity because deadlock/continuation structure differs. The conclusion situates bisimulation as a unifying relation for state-space equivalence, reduction, and abstraction, while leaving broader uncertainty/robustness, controller-interconnection modularity, hybrid systems, and behavioral formulations as future directions.
Boundary carried by this body: nonlinear quotient existence and maximal-relation computation require regularity conditions; hybrid and broader stochastic claims are not earned here.

edges.text: The locally valid expectation certificate is exactly what e-LOND can aggregate without modeling the joint dependence structure. The family guarantee is inherited from the local evidence contract, not from independence.

edges.title: doubly-sequential evidence → operating regime
edges.text: Within an individual experiment, an e-process can support lawful stopping; across experiments, the stopped e-values can enter the online stream. These are two sequential axes joined by the e-value handoff.

edges.title: evidence currency → proof boundary
edges.text: If a statistic is not actually a null-valid e-value (or was produced by an invalid stopped process), the cross-test FDR theorem has no certificate to consume. Local validity is load-bearing.

edges.title: family-control architecture → power regime
edges.text: Avoiding arbitrary-dependence reshaping can improve power, and randomized variants can improve rejection efficiency. Yet procedures exploiting correctly known local dependence may sometimes be stronger. Performance is regime-specific.

edges.title: dependence transport → sharpness and scope
edges.text: The arbitrary-dependence result is not merely a loose safety statement: the appendix gives a construction approaching the nominal FDR level. Its tightness is tied to the e-value currency and theorem contract.

edges.title: empirical/application behavior → proof-indexed interpretation
edges.text: Simulation and application evidence illustrate utility, but they cannot silently certify reference models, nuisance fits, filtration conditions, or adversarially changing targets beyond the theorem’s assumptions.

faces.title: DOUBLE-SEQUENTIAL COMPOSITION REQUIRES TWO SEPARATE VALIDITY CUSTODIES
faces.text: Optional stopping inside a test and online multiplicity across tests are different problems. They compose only when the within-test process hands the family controller a bona fide e-value. A valid e-process can pay stopping debt; e-LOND can then pay cross-test dependence debt.

faces.title: DEPENDENCE ROBUSTNESS IS CURRENCY-DEPENDENT, NOT DATA-DEPENDENCE IMMUNITY
faces.text: Theorem 1 tolerates arbitrary dependence among valid e-values. It does not make the construction of those e-values assumption-free. The local expectation/process certificate remains mandatory even when no cross-test dependence model is supplied.

faces.title: APPLICATION FLEXIBILITY ENDS WHERE LOCAL EVIDENCE OR STREAM CONTRACT CHANGES
faces.text: Overlapping, sequential, or otherwise dependent data can be compatible with the framework only when the local validator justifies the resulting e-values. Misspecified reference laws, same-sample nuisance leakage, target switching, or adversarial hypothesis generation are not repaired merely by passing the outputs to e-LOND.

faces.title: POWER GAINS DO NOT WIDEN THE GUARANTEE CLASS
faces.text: Dropping p-value reshaping, adding randomization, or constructing online e-confidence intervals changes power or utility. It does not expand the assumptions under which the underlying e-values are valid or transform application evidence into a stronger theorem.
