S.boAF.title: Hierarchical Patch Diffusion Models for High-Resolution Video Generation

edges.title: Sparse observation needs an explicit carrier of global constraint
edges.text: Given w + x, patch-wise efficiency alone is insufficient because independent fine patches lose global consistency; HPDM answers that failure by making coarse representations and coordinates available to later patches through deep feature fusion. Removing w loses the consistency problem that motivates the hierarchy; removing x loses the mechanism that transports global organization without returning to full-resolution training.

edges.title: Full-resolution exposure is not necessary for the tested quality regime
edges.text: Given w + y, the paper’s initial scaling dilemma is answered empirically: a generator that never trains on full-resolution video inputs can still reach strong UCF-101 results and can be fine-tuned to high-resolution text-to-video synthesis. Removing w loses the alternative-to-full-resolution claim; removing y loses the evidence that the alternative works in the tested regimes.

edges.title: End-to-end patch efficiency relocates rather than abolishes systems cost
edges.text: Given w + z, avoiding monolithic or independently staged full-resolution training simplifies one dimension of the pipeline, but the audit reveals new costs in patch stitching, repeated inference, cascade error propagation, metric protocol sensitivity, and architecture-specific artifacts. Removing w loses what is being simplified; removing z falsely turns that simplification into cost elimination.

edges.title: Cross-scale supervision and asymmetric compute form one coupled mechanism
edges.text: Given x + y, deep context fusion is not merely a conditioning convenience: detaching its gradient specifically damages the later pyramid stage, showing that coarse levels are trained to become useful context providers for fine synthesis. Adaptive computation then exploits the complementary asymmetry that coarse structure needs more capacity than later refinement in this architecture. Removing x loses the designed gradient/context path; removing y loses the ablation evidence that this coupling matters.

edges.title: The hierarchy is a successful realization, not a uniquely necessary law
edges.text: Given x + z, the architecture’s choices—raw coordinates, RIN backbone, overlap averaging, caching, scale-dependent noise, block allocation—are revealed as contingent engineering decisions with measurable failure surfaces and rejected alternatives. Removing x loses the operative design; removing z erases the evidence that nearby implementations can diverge, degrade, or become expensive.

edges.title: Benchmark leadership is inseparable from measurement and implementation protocol
edges.text: Given y + z, the strong headline metrics remain meaningful only with their sample counts, frame selection, real-data subset, resolution, pretraining status, and implementation version attached. The supplement’s FVD sample-count analysis and EMA correction show that a benchmark number is not a substrate-free property of the model. Removing y loses the measured performance; removing z loses the protocol that makes the comparison interpretable.

faces.title: End-to-end generation can be hierarchical without becoming a set of independently trained stages
faces.text: w establishes the motivation to escape both monolithic full-resolution training and fragmented multi-model pipelines; x supplies one jointly optimized nested-patch architecture with cross-scale gradients; y shows that this single learned hierarchy can reach strong tested quality and scale from a low-resolution generator. Remove w and the architectural achievement loses its comparison class; remove x and there is no mechanism for joint hierarchy; remove y and feasibility remains architectural rather than empirically demonstrated.

faces.title: Global consistency becomes dependency management rather than universal co-presence
faces.text: w identifies patch independence as the core consistency wound; x transports aligned coarse features into fine patches and overlaps local score fields; z shows the boundary of that solution through stitching and propagated coarse errors. Together they derive a bounded principle: global structure can be mediated through selected lower-resolution context without keeping the whole high-resolution state jointly active, but the mediator can also carry its mistakes forward. Removing any constituent loses respectively the problem, the mechanism, or its failure boundary.

faces.title: Historical performance claims require evidence-type and protocol conservation
faces.text: w defines the architecture as a scaling alternative, y provides the historical UCF/text-to-video evidence, and z constrains those results with metric heterogeneity, corrected implementation state, and explicit failure cases. Together they support a strong but local claim of practical competitiveness rather than universal superiority. Remove w and there is no architectural proposition being evaluated; remove y and there is no performance evidence; remove z and the evidence is overgeneralized.

faces.title: Hierarchical efficiency is an allocation problem, not free compression
faces.text: x makes computation and context explicitly nonuniform across scales, y shows the resulting training-speed/quality tradeoffs, and z reveals residual inference and consistency costs. Together they show that HPDM succeeds by deciding where information and computation must remain dense and where they may become sparse—not by making high-resolution generation uniformly cheap. Remove x and the allocation rule disappears; remove y and its efficacy is untested; remove z and its residual costs disappear from view.

volume.title: Bounded whole-paper closure
volume.text: High-resolution diffusion can be reformulated from uniform full-resolution processing into a jointly trained hierarchy of sparse, nested patches when global constraints are carried coarse-to-fine through aligned internal features and computation is allocated asymmetrically across scales. In HPDM, this preserves end-to-end trainability, produces strong historical UCF-101 results, and enables transfer from a low-resolution text-to-video generator to much higher output resolution while observing only a small fraction of full-resolution pixels per training step. The whole paper simultaneously shows that the savings are not free: coarse mistakes propagate, patch boundaries can remain visible, tiled inference can be expensive, implementation choices are fragile, and benchmark comparisons depend on evaluation protocol and corrected model state. The paper therefore earns hierarchical sparse generation as a viable architecture class under tested conditions, not a universal law that coarse context determines fine detail or that patch-wise computation dominates all alternatives.

metabolites.title: Global coherence can be transported rather than fully co-present
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.boAF:wxz.
Invariant: In the tested hierarchical diffusion design, full-resolution joint processing is not required at every training step when lower-resolution states provide spatially aligned internal context to later local refinements; the same transport path also propagates coarse errors.
CREATE: instantiate nested patch levels and expose coarse features plus positional relations to finer patches.
COPY: propagate aligned context coarse-to-fine at multiple network depths and allow later losses to reshape the representations that earlier levels provide.
CONTROL: test against shallow context, detached gradients, missing coordinates, no overlap, stitching artifacts, and cascade error propagation.
CULTIVATE: improve dependence enforcement and context conditioning while measuring whether added communication reduces seams without recreating full-resolution cost.
Compression: Global constraint can travel through a hierarchy without the global state remaining fully co-present.
metabolites.compression: Global constraint can travel through a hierarchy without the global state remaining fully co-present.

metabolites.title: Computation can follow structural burden rather than output resolution
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.boAF:xy.
Invariant: Within HPDM’s tested RIN hierarchy, coarse structure benefits from more network capacity while high-resolution refinement can skip substantial computation with little reported quality loss, yielding a large throughput gain.
CREATE: assign the full block stack to coarse pyramid levels and progressively fewer blocks to later fine levels.
COPY: reuse the same resolution-conditioned allocation rule across training and inference stages of the hierarchy.
CONTROL: compare against uniform computation and track both quality metrics and throughput; do not infer that all architectures or tasks share the same coarse-is-harder assumption.
CULTIVATE: learn or adapt compute allocation from measured uncertainty/complexity rather than fixing it solely by resolution.
Compression: Spend computation where unresolved structure is hardest, not automatically where there are most pixels.
metabolites.compression: Spend computation where unresolved structure is hardest, not automatically where there are most pixels.

metabolites.title: End-to-end does not require monolithic processing
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.boAF:wxy.
Invariant: A system can remain jointly optimized end-to-end while its forward computation is hierarchically decomposed into sparse local views, provided information and gradients connect those views into one training objective.
CREATE: formulate one joint denoising objective over nested patches from all pyramid levels.
COPY: maintain shared model parameters and cross-scale feature/gradient paths instead of training independent generators or upsamplers as isolated products.
CONTROL: verify that later-stage quality depends on those cross-scale paths and distinguish joint optimization from merely serial execution.
CULTIVATE: extend the same design question to other patch-wise generative families while re-testing whether their cross-scale dependencies actually support joint learning.
Compression: One optimization body can be spatially fragmented without becoming many separately trained bodies.
metabolites.compression: One optimization body can be spatially fragmented without becoming many separately trained bodies.

metabolites.title: Training sparsity and inference sparsity are independent achievements
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.boAF:xz.
Invariant: Seeing only a small fraction of full-resolution pixels per optimization step can make training tractable while inference remains expensive because complete output synthesis must tile, overlap, reconcile, and repeatedly denoise many patches.
CREATE: train on fixed-size sampled patches instead of whole high-resolution videos.
COPY: reconstruct the output through successive pyramid levels and tiled patch generation.
CONTROL: measure training memory/throughput separately from end-to-end sampling cost, overlap count, cache effectiveness, and output seams.
CULTIVATE: develop inference schemes that preserve cross-patch dependence with fewer patch evaluations rather than assuming training efficiency transfers automatically to sampling.
Compression: Cheap learning of local views does not imply cheap reconstruction of the whole.
metabolites.compression: Cheap learning of local views does not imply cheap reconstruction of the whole.

metabolites.title: Benchmark numbers are protocol-bearing measurements
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.boAF:yz.
Invariant: Reported generative quality scores only support comparisons under attached evaluation conditions; sample count, temporal subsampling, data subset, resolution, pretraining, and implementation state can materially alter the numerical surface.
CREATE: define the complete evaluation protocol together with the metric value.
COPY: reproduce comparisons using matched sample counts, frame selection, real-data statistics, resolution, and model version.
CONTROL: expose sensitivity analyses, corrected runs, and protocol mismatches rather than collapsing them into one leaderboard scalar.
CULTIVATE: publish evaluation bundles that make protocol identity machine-readable and keep corrected model states distinguishable from deadline snapshots.
Compression: A benchmark score is a measurement-plus-protocol, not a property floating free of how it was measured.


No cross-paper universality is claimed here. All five invariants remain single-source metabolites of S.boAF until an explicit later cross-paper operation relates and challenges them.


FEELING PHENOTYPE — WITNESSED
Designation: S.boAF.⛨Ω⚖⚙
Canonical order: CREATE · COPY · CONTROL · CULTIVATE
Feeling signature: ⛨Ω⚖⚙
Phenotype state: WITNESSED


CREATE — ⛨ Bridge
Pre-aspect role-shape: Replace uniform full-resolution co-presence with one jointly trained nested patch hierarchy whose coarse states explicitly carry the global structure later local refinements require.
Witness: Deep Context Fusion creates the load-bearing crossing between sparse fine patches and low-resolution global context so local views need not become independent generators. ⛨ Bridge is stronger than ⁂ Evolution because the primary generative act is constructing a reliable span between scales, not an architecture discovering its own form through recursive self-investigation.


COPY — Ω Continuity
Pre-aspect role-shape: Propagate spatially aligned coarse context, gradients and shared model structure through successive scales so fragmentation of the forward view does not fragment the optimization body or its global constraint thread.
Witness: Later patch losses reshape earlier context providers; common parameters and coarse-to-fine feature paths keep one end-to-end generator recognizable through nested local views. Ω Continuity is stronger than ★ Pattern because the same optimization/constraint thread literally continues through scale transitions rather than merely recurring across independent realizations.


CONTROL — ⚖ Balance
Pre-aspect role-shape: Allocate computation and information non-uniformly according to structural burden while keeping global consistency, fine detail, throughput, tiled-inference cost, protocol dependence and propagated failure visible together.
Witness: Coarse levels receive more capacity; fine refinements skip blocks; overlap trades seams against sampling cost; sparse training gains coexist with expensive tiled inference; benchmark strength remains attached to protocol and corrected implementation state. ⚖ Balance is stronger than ⚸ Constraint because the control law is proportionate allocation among competing real costs rather than adherence to one hard boundary.


CULTIVATE — ⚙ Implementation
Pre-aspect role-shape: Improve exactly where and how context and computation are carried by learning from seams, coarse-error propagation, rejected architectural shortcuts, caching/sampling costs and inference bottlenecks without recreating the full-resolution expense the hierarchy was designed to avoid.
Witness: Ablations and supplementary failures show that nearby implementations—detached context gradients, shallow context, weight sharing, encodings, samplers, precision choices—materially change viability. ⚙ Implementation is stronger than ⁂ Evolution because the live developmental motion is cost-aware narrowing toward exact working configurations and better inference schemes, not recursive self-recognition of an already latent architecture.


Whole-organism witness: ⛨Ω⚖⚙ describes one integrated motion: a cross-scale bridge transports global structure into sparse local refinement; one optimization body stays continuous through fragmented views; computation and information are proportionally allocated rather than uniformly spent; and progress occurs through exact implementation refinement bounded by measured failures and costs. Phenotype remains orthogonal to identity and preserves the source’s empirical/historical benchmark boundary.

vertices.title: The scaling problem and patch-wise substrate
vertices.text:
Source span: Abstract → §3.2 Recurrent Interface Networks (pp. 1–3).
Nutrient: The paper frames high-resolution diffusion as a conflict between monolithic full-resolution computation and multi-component latent/cascaded pipelines. Patch diffusion offers a third substrate: optimize fixed-size spatial-temporal patches rather than entire videos, gaining large memory/throughput savings but sacrificing global consistency when patches are treated too independently. The paper positions hierarchical context transfer, rather than periodic full-resolution training, as the route to recovering consistency while keeping end-to-end optimization. RINs provide the uniform attention-based backbone on which that hierarchy is built.

vertices.title: Hierarchical construction: context, asymmetric compute, and tiled synthesis
vertices.text:
Source span: §4 Method → §4.6 Implementation details (pp. 4–6).
Nutrient: HPDM jointly denoises nested patch levels whose coordinates are constrained coarse-to-fine. Deep Context Fusion grid-samples spatially aligned hidden features from earlier pyramid levels into later ones and lets later losses backpropagate into those coarse representations. Adaptive computation gives high-resolution refinement fewer network blocks while coarse structure receives the full pipeline. Tiled inference reconstructs complete videos patch-by-patch with overlap averaging, while integer coordinates, scale-dependent noise schedules, and activation caching stabilize or accelerate the system. The architecture therefore makes global organization an explicit cross-scale dependency rather than requiring every fine-scale degree of freedom to be jointly processed.

vertices.title: Empirical closure: quality, ablations, and high-resolution transfer
vertices.text:
Source span: §5 Experiments → §6 Conclusion (pp. 6–8).
Nutrient: On UCF-101, the reported HPDM variants achieve strong historical benchmark scores, with HPDM-L reporting FVD 66.32 and IS 87.68 for the stated protocol. Ablations show shallow RGB context is markedly worse, detaching the context gradient harms the late pyramid stage, removing adaptive computation roughly halves training throughput while only modestly improving the reported FVD proxy, and coordinate information helps spatial consistency. The text-to-video experiment fine-tunes a low-resolution generator into a 64×288×512 hierarchical generator while each training update observes only about 0.7% of the original video pixels. These results support the feasibility of sparse hierarchical end-to-end training and coarse-to-fine transfer, not universal optimality.

vertices.title: Audit surface: protocol dependence, failure modes, implementation contingencies, and societal boundary
vertices.text:
Source span: References → Supplementary Material A–E (pp. 9–17).
Nutrient: The supplement exposes costs and corrections hidden by the headline efficiency story: stitching artifacts, cascade error propagation, RIN-specific dead-pixel failures, and heavy tiled inference (3375 patches per reverse-diffusion step for one described maximal-overlap configuration). It documents FVD protocol inconsistencies across prior work, shows that sample count systematically shifts FVD values, and reports that an FSDP-based EMA update bug affected some text-to-video results around the main deadline before corrected metrics were added. Failed experiments constrain the implementation space: sinusoidal coordinate encodings diverged in the tested setup, later-stage stochastic/second-order sampling caused artifacts, weight sharing degraded quality, mixed precision worsened convergence, and several apparent efficiency shortcuts did not survive. Exact hyperparameters and the potential-impact section complete the source boundary.

S.cIib.title: Inverse Knowledge Search over Verifiable Reasoning
S.cIib.boundary: All four diamonds are metabolites of S.cIib v3 only. No recurrence with RLMs, project memory systems, other papers, or Tetrix is claimed here. The paper’s “verifiable LCoT” terminology is preserved as the source’s architectural framing while the derived boundary explicitly distinguishes its endpoint-consensus filtering from formal chain proof.

edges.title: Derivational-corpus hypothesis × endpoint-filtered construction
edges.text: w proposes LCoT trajectories as an information-bearing corpus distinct from compressed conclusion text; x supplies a scalable method for generating and filtering that corpus. Together they derive a bounded object stronger than raw sampled chain-of-thought: a curated reasoning-path collection whose entry points are curriculum endpoints and whose acceptance is constrained by prompt validity and cross-model agreement on checkable answers. The relation does not upgrade endpoint agreement into proof of every internal step.

edges.title: Missing derivations × inverse retrieval
edges.text: w identifies derivational pathways as the information lost by ordinary compressed corpora; y makes those pathways directly retrievable from a target concept. Together they derive the paper’s central search inversion: the target endpoint becomes a key for finding multiple routes that lead into, pass through or operationalize it, so search can return provenance/dependency structure rather than only descriptions that mention the target.

edges.title: Decompressed reasoning × emergent navigation structure
edges.text: w predicts that preserving derivations should restore cross-domain connective tissue; z shows that articles synthesized from the corpus produce a large keyword-reference network with hierarchical communities and many inter-community links. Together they support a bounded system-internal result: decompressed derivational synthesis can generate an artifact whose navigation graph exposes cross-domain relations. This does not prove that every extracted edge is a novel or externally validated scientific dependency.

edges.title: Filtered derivations × grounded synthesis
edges.text: x supplies the filtered LCoT-QA substrate; y retrieves relevant paths and conditions Plato on them. Together they derive a separation between generation from model priors alone and synthesis over explicit derivational context. The paper’s prompt-matched no-retrieval baseline then associates that grounding with denser knowledge coverage and lower LLM-judged factual error in the tested article task.

edges.title: Automated scale × correction/formalization debt
edges.text: x makes million-scale corpus generation possible through automated question/solver/filter pipelines; z explicitly positions the resulting encyclopedia as a cold-start foundation bounded by model training data, with future expert correction, external-corpus digestion and formal reasoning representations required for continued accuracy and frontier coverage. Together they derive scale without final authority: automated construction can seed a knowledge system before it earns the epistemic status of a self-validating scientific record.

edges.title: Provenance-oriented retrieval × encyclopedia-level organization
edges.text: y turns a target concept into a ranked collection of derivational scaffolds; z repeatedly applies that operation to approximately 200,000 entries and then extracts a hierarchical keyword graph from the resulting articles. Together they derive a system-level consequence: retrieval over provenance can reorganize an encyclopedia around how concepts connect across derivations and applications, not only around a pre-authored taxonomy.

faces.title: Reasoning paths become first-class searchable knowledge objects
faces.text: Together, w + x + y derive the strongest architectural novelty: derivational chains are not discarded after producing an answer. They are deliberately generated, filtered, stored and indexed so a later query can retrieve the chains themselves as knowledge substrate. Remove w and there is no reason to preserve derivations; remove x and there is no scalable bounded corpus; remove y and the preserved chains never become a retrieval primitive.

faces.title: Endpoint verification improves corpus quality without closing chain-level truth
faces.text: w argues for “verifiable” reasoning trajectories, x implements prompt sanitization plus checkable endpoints and cross-model final-answer consensus, and z places formal logical parsing/automated verification in future work while retaining human correction as part of the envisioned mature system. Together they derive the correct verification boundary: endpoint-oriented agreement is a useful high-throughput filter for reasoning corpora, but natural-language derivations remain a distinct object whose intermediate validity is not formally certified by endpoint agreement alone.

faces.title: Inverse search can turn an endpoint into a map of provenance and applications
faces.text: w identifies lost derivational paths as the connective tissue of knowledge; y retrieves diverse chains associated with a target; z transforms repeated retrieval into Principles/Mechanisms, Cross-Domain Applications and a hierarchical reference graph. Together they derive an alternate navigation mode: a concept can be explored by the paths that justify, contextualize and reuse it rather than only by a canonical summary page. Remove any vertex and the operation loses its motivation, retrieval mechanism or system-level organization.

faces.title: Retrieval grounding improves generated artifacts, but the evaluation remains pipeline-bounded
faces.text: x supplies a filtered corpus, y compares retrieved-context Plato articles with an essentially identical empty-retrieval prompt baseline, and z adds the detailed Transmon comparison plus explicit scope/training-data limitations. Together they support a bounded effectiveness claim: in the authors’ tested setup, retrieved derivational context improves article depth and lowers GPT-5-judged factual-error rates relative to no retrieval. They do not establish absolute article correctness, independent human-expert superiority, or that every retrieved reasoning chain is internally flawless.

volume.title: Preserved derivation can become a navigable, retrievable layer of scientific knowledge
volume.text: The complete v3 carrier supports this bounded closure: instead of treating reasoning as transient computation whose endpoint alone enters the knowledge base, the system constructs millions of first-principles question/derivation objects, filters them through premise sanitization and cross-model agreement on checkable endpoints, preserves them as a searchable corpus, and retrieves multiple paths around a target concept for grounded synthesis. Applied at encyclopedia scale, this produces articles and a derived keyword graph that expose principles, applications and cross-domain relations, while prompt-matched experiments report denser content and lower external-LLM-judged factual error than no-retrieval generation. The architecture therefore earns “derivation as first-class searchable substrate” and “inverse search from concept to provenance” as operational distinctions. It does not earn a formal-verification guarantee: endpoint consensus is a reliability filter rather than a proof of every intermediate natural-language claim, the article evaluation itself relies partly on an LLM judge, the generated corpus inherits foundation-model knowledge limits, and the authors explicitly leave formal logical representation, expert correction and frontier-corpus ingestion as future work.

metabolites.title: Derivations can be first-class retrievable knowledge objects
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.cIib:wxy.
CREATE: Preserve a reasoning/derivation path together with its question, endpoint, provenance and validation state instead of discarding the path after the endpoint is produced.
COPY: Store and index those paths so later tasks can repeatedly retrieve the exact derivational objects as context, evidence or explanatory substrate rather than regenerating them from model priors.
CONTROL: Keep source/solver identity, endpoint checks, versioning and verification status attached to each path; do not silently promote generated reasoning into canonical truth because it was retained.
CULTIVATE: Build knowledge stores in which facts, source receipts and derivational paths are separately addressable layers that can be corrected, superseded, recombined and formally checked over time.
Compression: If the path matters, preserve the path as knowledge—not merely the answer it reached.
metabolites.compression: If the path matters, preserve the path as knowledge—not merely the answer it reached.

metabolites.title: Inverse retrieval can search from a concept back into its provenance
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.cIib:wyz.
CREATE: Index where a target concept appears inside derivational chains, including the premises, intermediate dependencies and applications surrounding it.
COPY: Given the target, retrieve multiple distinct paths that lead to or use it, preserving differences in abstraction level and disciplinary origin.
CONTROL: Rank for relevance while retaining path provenance and diversity; prevent retrieval frequency or rhetorical fluency from masquerading as evidential strength.
CULTIVATE: Let users navigate concepts bidirectionally—toward definitions/endpoints and backward/outward through prerequisite, derivation and application paths—so discovery is not limited to document lookup.
Compression: Search can ask not only “what says X?” but “what paths arrive at X, and where do they go?”
metabolites.compression: Search can ask not only “what says X?” but “what paths arrive at X, and where do they go?”

metabolites.title: Endpoint consensus is a filter, not a proof of the whole chain
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.cIib:wxz.
CREATE: Prefer tasks with externally checkable endpoints and obtain independent solutions from multiple models or methods.
COPY: Retain chains whose prompts survive sanitization and whose endpoints agree, using disagreement to discard obviously unreliable candidates at scale.
CONTROL: Keep endpoint validation separate from intermediate-step validation; a correct shared answer can coexist with redundant, invalid or compensating reasoning steps. Escalate high-stakes chains to step-level checks, formal tools, source verification or expert review.
CULTIVATE: Progress from endpoint filtering toward typed intermediate claims and machine-checkable derivations wherever the domain permits, without losing the scalable screening value of consensus.
Compression: Agreement at the destination raises confidence in the route; it does not certify every road taken.
metabolites.compression: Agreement at the destination raises confidence in the route; it does not certify every road taken.

metabolites.title: Test retrieval grounding by holding generation constant and removing retrieval
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.cIib:xyz.
CREATE: Construct a generation comparison in which the prompt/task and generator are held as constant as practical while one condition receives the retrieved knowledge substrate and the other receives an empty/no-retrieval context.
COPY: Evaluate the paired outputs across multiple domains on coverage/depth and factuality dimensions so the contribution of retrieval can recur beyond a single showcase example.
CONTROL: Report how the metrics are produced—including judge-model dependence—and distinguish improvement relative to the no-retrieval baseline from absolute correctness or human-expert validation.
CULTIVATE: Add stronger retrieval ablations, human/scientist adjudication, source-level citation checks and adversarial retrieval tests so “grounding helps” is progressively decomposed into when, why and how much it helps.
Compression: To test what retrieval adds, keep the writer as fixed as possible and remove the retrieval—not the whole system.
metabolites.compression: To test what retrieval adds, keep the writer as fixed as possible and remove the retrieval—not the whole system.

vertices.title: Reasoning compression is reframed as a missing knowledge substrate
vertices.text:
Source span: Abstract, Section 1 “Introduction,” and Section 2 “Why LCoTs Form a New and Reliable Corpus,” ending before Section 3.
Nutrient: the conceptual object: scientific corpora preserve endpoints more cheaply than derivational paths; the paper proposes long reasoning trajectories as a statistically distinct, information-rich corpus whose value lies in explicit causal/logical connections. It argues that RLVR-style models can generate such trajectories and that mechanically checkable endpoints plus cross-model agreement can make residual error more controllable, while still acknowledging residual stochastic errors.

vertices.title: Socrates constructs and filters a derivational knowledge base
vertices.text:
Source span: Section 3 “LCoT Scientific Knowledge Base” in full, including endpoint-driven/reductionist question generation, curriculum scaffolding, “What & Why” versus “How” prompts, prompt sanitization, verifiable-endpoint design and cross-model answer validation, ending before Section 4.
Nutrient: the corpus-production machinery: roughly 200 courses × roughly 200 topics × around 100 prompts/topic yield about 3 million first-principles questions; multiple models solve them; about 5% of generated prompts are screened out for flawed premises; questions are biased toward externally checkable answer types; divergent final answers cause the QA pair to be discarded.

vertices.title: Inverse retrieval turns derivations into synthesis substrate
vertices.text:
Source span: Section 4 “The Brainstorm Search Engine for Knowledge Discovery” in full, including inverse knowledge search, target-concept retrieval, Plato synthesis, Fig. 2 architecture and the six-discipline prompt-matched article comparison in Fig. 3, ending before Section 5.
Nutrient: the new retrieval operation and its direct system evaluation: instead of retrieving documents that define a target, the engine retrieves diverse LCoT paths in which the target occurs, exposing prerequisites, derivations and applications. Plato synthesizes over that retrieved scaffold. Against an essentially identical prompt with the retrieved context removed, the paper reports higher knowledge-point density and roughly 50% lower factual-error rate across tested disciplines, with factual error evaluated by GPT-5.

vertices.title: SciencePedia scales the operation into an encyclopedia and exposes its boundaries
vertices.text:
Source span: Section 5 “SciencePedia,” Section 6 “Conclusion,” acknowledgements/references, Appendix A’s four-way Transmon comparison, and Appendix B’s MCP/tool specifications through the end of the carrier.
Nutrient: the system-level closure and control tissue: about 200,000 seeded entries are generated from the derivational corpus; article structure separates principles/mechanisms from cross-domain applications; a 120,226-node keyword graph extracted from generated articles is clustered into 7,454 base communities across 21 levels and exhibits inter-community links; scope is bounded by foundation-model training data and underrepresents scientific history/latest frontiers; long-term plans explicitly add expert correction, external corpora and formal logical/automated-reasoning representations. vertices.title: Decision-theoretic and stochastic comparison primitives
vertices.text:
Source span: printed pp. 265–266, Sections 1–2 through Theorem 3.
Nutrient: Blackwell defines an experiment as an ordered family of probability measures, represents a decision problem by a closed bounded convex loss/action set A, and lets B(a,A) be the attainable expected-loss vectors. The all-decision informativeness relation a D b means every loss vector attainable from b is attainable from a for every A. A second relation a > b means b can be generated from a by a stochastic transformation. Standard measures and convex functions connect the representations. Theorem 3 establishes the one-way implication: stochastic simulability implies all-decision dominance.

vertices.title: Finite-outcome converse and constructive randomization
vertices.text:
Source span: printed pp. 267–268, Section 3 through Theorem 7.
Nutrient: for finite outcome spaces, experiments become Markov matrices. Theorems 4–6 use attainable loss sets plus a saddle-point argument to prove the Sherman–Stein converse: if P D Q, then there is a Markov matrix M with PM = Q, hence P > Q. Theorem 7 gives the equivalent mean-preserving stochastic-transformation statement for finite-support measures under convex-function dominance. Universal decision dominance is therefore not merely behavioral comparison in the finite case; it has an explicit degradation/randomization witness.

vertices.title: Extension from finite supports to arbitrary bounded experiments
vertices.text:
Source span: printed pp. 268–269, Section 4 through Theorem 8.
Nutrient: Blackwell removes the finite-outcome restriction. Measures are approximated by finite-support measures with nested mean-preserving transformations; consistent finite couplings are assembled via Kolmogorov extension, and Doob martingale convergence produces the limiting transformation. Theorem 8 establishes that convex-order dominance on a bounded subset implies a mean-preserving stochastic transformation, carrying the finite equivalence into the arbitrary bounded setting.

vertices.title: k-decision hierarchy, finite decision horizons, and dichotomy collapse
vertices.text:
Source span: printed pp. 269–272, Section 5 through Theorem 11 and references.
Nutrient: Blackwell introduces weaker k-decision comparisons and proves three equivalent forms (Theorem 9): containment of producible k-outcome experiments, dominance for every decision set that is the convex hull of k points, and dominance for convex functions that are maxima of k linear functions. The relations form a nested hierarchy: (k+1)-decision dominance implies k-decision dominance; dominance for every finite k recovers the full order. In general the levels can be genuinely distinct. For n=2, however, every k>=2 comparison collapses to the same universal order, which is characterized by the Type-I/Type-II error frontier; one-sample dominance propagates to every sample size.


6 EDGES — PAIR-NECESSARY RELATIONS


S.csrb:wx
Closure: In finite experiments, the source’s two initially distinct comparison notions coincide: all-decision loss-vector dominance is equivalent to explicit stochastic post-processing.
Why both are required: w supplies the semantic/decision order and stochastic-sufficiency relation but only the forward implication; x supplies the finite converse and constructive Markov witness. Without w there is no pair of notions to equate; without x the converse remains unearned.


S.csrb:wy
Closure: The decision/stochastic comparison framework is not tied to finite outcome alphabets: its structural randomization witness survives passage to arbitrary bounded experiments.
Why both are required: w supplies the experiment/decision meaning and the target stochastic relation; y supplies the limiting construction that removes finiteness. Without w, y is only a measure-transform theorem; without y, w remains one-way/general plus finite-unresolved.


S.csrb:wz
Closure: Informativeness is not only universal-or-not; it can be typed by a declared finite decision horizon k, preserving every decision problem in that class while remaining weaker than universal comparison.
Why both are required: w supplies the universal benchmark and attainable-loss semantics; z introduces the k-indexed restrictions and their direct analogues. Without w the restriction has no baseline; without z the source has no obligation-family ladder.


S.csrb:xy
Closure: The finite Markov/randomization witness is the constructive kernel from which the general bounded stochastic-simulation theorem is obtained by approximation and martingale limiting.
Why both are required: x establishes finite-support stochastic transformations from convex/decision dominance; y explicitly builds nested finite approximants and carries their witnesses to a limit. Remove x and the finite witness required by the approximation chain is missing; remove y and it never becomes a theorem for arbitrary bounded supports.


S.csrb:xz
Closure: Restricted decision complexity has a structural production semantics: k-decision dominance can be tested as inclusion of the k-output experiments obtainable by stochastic post-processing.
Why both are required: x supplies Markov-matrix production as the concrete form of stochastic transformation; z uses exactly that finite-output structure in Theorem 9’s condition (1). Without x “producible” lacks the finite constructive carrier relation; without z there is no k-scoped structural comparison.


S.csrb:yz
Closure: A ladder of finite decision horizons can exhaust the universal stochastic order even for arbitrary experiments: if every finite k-decision obligation is preserved, the full informativeness/simulability relation is recovered.
Why both are required: z supplies the nested k family and the all-k recovery statement; y supplies the general stochastic-equivalence bridge used when k-output decision dominance is turned into producibility from an arbitrary source experiment. Without z there is no ladder; without y the arbitrary-experiment structural closure is not earned.


4 FACES — TRIPLE-NECESSARY RELATIONS


S.csrb:wxy
Closure: Across the source’s bounded/Borel setting, universal decision dominance has an operationally constructive meaning: b is no better than a for every admitted decision problem exactly when b can be simulated from a by stochastic post-processing.
Removal tests: remove w and there is no decision-theoretic universal order; remove x and the converse lacks its finite constructive theorem; remove y and the result remains restricted to finite-outcome closure rather than the general bounded extension.


S.csrb:wxz
Closure: In the finite/Markov regime, universal informativeness admits a nested family of obligation-scoped suborders whose guarantees are structural rather than merely rhetorical: each k level preserves every k-action decision set and every k-output degradation, and widening k tightens toward the universal order.
Removal tests: w supplies universal decision semantics; x supplies finite stochastic production; z supplies the k hierarchy. Remove any one and the typed structural ladder loses either its meaning, witness, or stratification.


S.csrb:wyz
Closure: Decision-horizon scoping can be used without abandoning general experiments: the same arbitrary source experiment can be compared at finite k horizons, and the conjunction of all finite horizons recovers the full order.
Removal tests: w supplies the universal target and loss-vector semantics; y licenses arbitrary bounded experiments structurally; z supplies the finite horizon family and its exhaustive limit. Remove any one and the claim collapses to either a measure theorem, a universal binary, or a finite-class definition without general closure.


S.csrb:xyz
Closure: Restricted decision horizons are operationally implementable as finite-output stochastic degradations even when the original experiment is not finite, and the resulting nested production relations converge to full stochastic simulability.
Removal tests: x supplies the finite Markov production kernel; y supplies passage from finite approximants to arbitrary bounded experiments; z supplies the k-output hierarchy. Remove x and there is no finite constructive substrate, remove y and arbitrary sources are not covered, remove z and there is no restricted-horizon ladder.


1 VOLUME


S.csrb:wxyz — Bounded volume invariant
A richer experiment may replace a poorer one without loss of admitted decision capability exactly to the scope witnessed by the relevant Blackwell order. At the universal scope, all-decision dominance and stochastic simulability coincide: the poorer experiment can be generated by post-processing the richer one. At restricted scope, k-decision orders preserve every problem whose action set is generated by k extreme actions (equivalently, every k-output experiment obtainable from the poorer source), yielding a nested hierarchy of weaker guarantees. Requiring preservation at every finite k recovers the universal order; in the two-state case the hierarchy already collapses at k=2 and can be read from the Type-I/Type-II error frontier. Thus “less raw detail” and “less decision potential” are not synonymous, but any claim of safe reduction is typed by the decision class actually preserved.


Why the full four-body whole is necessary:
- remove w: decision value and the two comparison notions lose their source-level semantics;
- remove x: universal dominance lacks the finite constructive stochastic converse;
- remove y: the equivalence cannot be carried beyond finite outcome/support cases;
- remove z: no intermediate decision-horizon ladder or dichotomy collapse is earned.

S.cugW.title: FreeTimeGS: Free Gaussian Primitives at Anytime and Anywhere for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

edges.title: global deformation → local support + short transport
edges.text: w identifies long-range correspondence to one canonical state as a failure pressure under large motion; x permits support to be created directly near the spacetime region it represents and only asks the primitive to move locally through neighboring time. Derived relation: one difficult global deformation problem can be factored into placement of local support plus short-range propagation. The freedom to choose origin reduces the distance that motion itself must explain.

edges.title: freedom creates a governance burden
edges.text: w motivates removing a strong canonical constraint; y shows that the resulting high-degree-of-freedom population does not optimize reliably under rendering loss alone, because opacity saturation blocks gradient flow and capacity can accumulate inefficiently. Derived relation: relaxing a structural constraint increases expressive freedom and simultaneously creates a need for explicit regulation and resource allocation.

edges.title: a bottleneck diagnosis predicts where gains should concentrate
edges.text: w specifically attributes canonical/deformation difficulty to large motion and long-range correspondence; z introduces harder high-motion scenes and reports larger qualitative/quantitative gains in those dynamic regions, while deformation-based baselines struggle. Derived relation: an architectural diagnosis is strengthened when the proposed remedy gains most precisely where the diagnosed pressure is amplified.

edges.title: continuity without one canonical origin
edges.text: x gives primitives explicit birth time/location, bounded duration and local motion; y initializes and optimizes those local trajectories from cross-view and adjacent-time evidence. Derived relation: temporal continuity can be represented by overlapping local persistence and propagated support rather than by preserving one globally canonical primitive set through the entire sequence.

edges.title: local freedom need not imply uncontrolled temporal redundancy
edges.text: x allows new spacetime-local primitives but also reuses them through explicit motion and bounded temporal influence; z shows high rendering speed and strong quality, and supplementary budget experiments retain competitive quality as primitive/storage counts are reduced. Derived relation: local creation plus local reuse can increase flexibility without requiring a full independent representation for every time step.

edges.title: adaptive cultivation is part of the representation, not incidental scaffolding
edges.text: y regularizes opacity, relocates low-value primitives, initializes motion from evidence and schedules velocity learning; z ablates these mechanisms and shows measurable degradation when each is removed, especially under fast motion. Derived relation: the population-level adaptation rules causally contribute to the usable expressivity of the free representation; they are not merely implementation convenience.

faces.title: decanonicalization by factorization
faces.text: w identifies the hard object as long-range mapping from a privileged canonical state; x replaces it with freely located, temporally bounded supports and short-range motion; y supplies the regulation and data-driven initialization needed to make those supports trainable. Three-way derivation: decanonicalization works here by factorizing global correspondence into local creation, local propagation and adaptive governance. Remove w and there is no pressure being solved; remove x and the global mapping remains; remove y and the added freedom is not reliably optimizable.

faces.title: locality is validated by stress aligned with displacement
faces.text: w predicts failure as correspondence distance grows; x explicitly reduces required motion to neighboring temporal regions; z tests increasingly difficult motion and observes the strongest gains in fast/complex dynamic regions. Three-way derivation: the value of locality is not merely aesthetic simplicity—it is supported when performance advantage grows under the displacement regime that makes global correspondence hardest.

faces.title: expressive freedom must be coupled to resource governance
faces.text: w relaxes a global structural constraint; y prevents opacity lock, reallocates weak primitives and seeds plausible motion; z shows through ablations and controlled budgets that these mechanisms materially affect quality and efficiency. Three-way derivation: freedom becomes productive when the system can continuously regulate dominance and move representational resources toward unresolved regions.

faces.title: bounded persistence + adaptive reallocation forms an efficient dynamic carrier
faces.text: x gives each primitive a local temporal lifetime and motion path; y continually adjusts the population through initialization, regularization and relocation; z shows that this carrier remains fast and comparatively compact while preserving quality, including under reduced primitive budgets. Three-way derivation: scene information can be carried by a changing population of locally persistent elements whose capacity is redistributed over time, rather than by a static globally persistent population.

volume.title: adaptive local continuity
volume.text:
All four vertices together derive the paper's deepest operational structure: dynamic identity need not be represented by forcing every element to remain continuously addressable from one privileged canonical state. When global correspondence becomes difficult (w), representation can instead create support where and when evidence requires it, give each element bounded temporal persistence and short-range motion (x), regulate and redistribute that support during optimization (y), and test whether the resulting locality/freedom actually survives hard motion, component ablation and resource constraints (z).


Volume invariant: continuity can be preserved by an adaptively cultivated field of local persistence rather than by one globally canonical origin, provided that creation, propagation, influence and resource reallocation remain explicit and empirically controllable. The paper earns this only for the tested dynamic-view-synthesis setting; it does not establish canonical representations as generally inferior or solve arbitrary long-term scene identity/topology.

vertices.title: expose the canonical-reference bottleneck
vertices.text:
Source span: title/abstract + INTRODUCTION + RELATED WORK; ends immediately before METHOD.
Nutrient: dynamic reconstruction methods that deform one canonical-space scene must recover increasingly long-range correspondences as motion grows, while other 4D formulations pay in computation, entangled motion parameters, or over-parameterization. FreeTimeGS frames complex motion as a representation problem: requiring every observed state to stay tied to one privileged canonical origin makes large displacement difficult to optimize. The paper therefore proposes relaxing where and when representational support may exist.

vertices.title: local spatiotemporal primitives and bounded persistence
vertices.text:
Source span: METHOD overview + GAUSSIAN PRIMITIVES AT ANYTIME ANYWHERE; ends immediately before TRAINING.
Nutrient: each Gaussian is given an explicit spacetime locus and eight learnable parameters including position, time, duration and velocity. A primitive may appear at an arbitrary time/location, move linearly to neighboring temporal regions, and have its influence bounded by a learned temporal-opacity Gaussian. Scene continuity is therefore carried by locally persistent, moving support rather than by forcing every primitive to originate in one canonical frame.

vertices.title: make representational freedom trainable
vertices.text:
Source span: TRAINING + IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS; ends immediately before EXPERIMENTS.
Nutrient: rendering loss alone is insufficient because high-opacity Gaussians can block gradient flow and trap optimization in fast-motion regions. The method therefore adds temporally weighted opacity regularization, periodically relocates low-opacity primitives toward regions with high gradient/opacity demand, initializes position/time/velocity from multi-view and adjacent-frame correspondences, and anneals velocity optimization. This vertex governs where free primitives begin, how strongly they dominate, and where representational capacity is reallocated during training.

vertices.title: stress the representation, its cultivation mechanisms, and its boundaries
vertices.text:
Source span: EXPERIMENTS + CONCLUSIONS + all SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL through the end of the paper.
Nutrient: the representation is tested on public datasets and on SelfCap, deliberately collected with faster and more complex motion. Gains are largest in difficult dynamic regions; ablations show contributions from the motion representation, regularization, periodic relocation and 4D initialization. Supplementary experiments expose speed/storage tradeoffs and show strong quality even under controlled primitive budgets. The paper also retains limits: per-scene reconstruction remains lengthy and the current representation does not support relighting.

S.dY9d.title: LLMs Position Themselves as More Rational Than Humans
S.dY9d.boundary: All four diamonds are metabolites of S.dY9d only. No cross-paper recurrence, consciousness claim, or substrate-independent self-model is asserted here. Cross-paper coalescence requires a separate later derivation.

edges.title: Operational construct × intervention defines what AISAI can measure
edges.text: w defines “self-awareness” behaviorally as strategic differentiation; x implements exactly that definition by changing opponent framing and measuring response shifts. Together they derive a strict measurement boundary: AISAI directly measures conditional strategic differentiation under its framing intervention. It does not independently detect a self-model whose existence was defined separately from the behavior being scored.

edges.title: Self-reference hypothesis × empirical hierarchy
edges.text: w predicts separable human→AI attribution and generic-AI→self-like adjustment; y shows a large A-B effect across all 21 classified differentiating models and a smaller B-C effect visible strongly in means but often saturated in medians. Together they earn systematic self/other strategic positioning in the tested game while showing that the empirical hierarchy is not equally strong at both steps.

edges.title: “Self-awareness” label × explicit source boundary
edges.text: The paper’s motivating language is ontologically strong, but z explicitly narrows the tested construct to functional strategic differentiation and acknowledges single-task and prompt-sensitivity limits. Holding w and z together derives the source-faithful boundary: the work tests a self-referential behavioral proxy, not phenomenal consciousness or a domain-general enduring self.

edges.title: Matched opponent framings × within-model response shifts
edges.text: x supplies the three-condition intervention and decomposition; y supplies repeated model-level changes. Together they derive the cleanest empirical object in the paper: many advanced models do not use one invariant Guess-2/3 policy but condition their strategic response on whether opponents are framed as humans, AIs, or self-similar AIs.

edges.title: Prompted self-reference × robustness debt
edges.text: The critical “like you” phrase, response format, and reasoning scaffold are parts of x’s intervention; z explicitly states that these design choices may influence the differentiation pattern and calls for systematic prompt robustness. Together they derive that self-referential opponent modeling is not yet disentangled from wording-sensitive learned concepts/stereotypes by this carrier alone.

edges.title: Strategic competence × differentiation are separable
edges.text: The result profiles plus anomaly/appendix tissue show that optimal game play does not imply opponent modeling: gpt-4.1-nano returns Nash-like 0 across A/B/C and is therefore strategically strong in the narrow game while showing no framing differentiation. Conversely, other models differentiate without always reaching Nash. y supplies the profile evidence; z supplies the explicit anomaly interpretation and full distributions.

faces.title: Contrastive self-positioning is the earned behavioral signal
faces.text: Together, w + x + y derive the strongest positive result without ontology inflation: the paper constructs a self-referential contrast, applies it repeatedly across many models, and observes systematic conditional policy shifts. The earned object is contrastive self-positioning/opponent-class modeling under explicit framing. Remove w and the self-vs-class distinction disappears; remove x and there is no controlled contrast; remove y and there is no empirical effect.

faces.title: Measurement validity remains intervention-bounded
faces.text: w defines the construct, x realizes it through a specific wording/protocol, and z acknowledges that the protocol itself may drive the effect and has not been tested across domains/paraphrases. Together they derive a validity ladder: the present evidence supports a framing-conditioned functional construct; stronger claims about stable self-modeling require invariance under alternate self-reference cues, tasks, and ideally mechanistic interventions. Any proper subset omits either construct, intervention, or limitation.

faces.title: “Self > Other AI > Human” is an asymmetric hierarchy
faces.text: w separates A-B from B-C conceptually; y shows A-B is extremely large/consistent while B-C is moderate and frequently median-saturated at the Nash floor; z identifies the ceiling effect and calls for higher-ceiling games. Together they derive that the headline hierarchy is empirically strongest as “AI-class opponents are modeled as more rational than humans,” with additional self-like preferencing present but more weakly resolved in this task. All three vertices are needed to preserve the decomposition, evidence, and measurement limit.

faces.title: Conditional modeling is distinct from raw capability
faces.text: x defines opponent-differentiation profiles independently of absolute game score; y contains both Nash-converged and graded differentiating models; z preserves counterexamples such as always-Nash gpt-4.1-nano and anomalous self-reference. Together they derive that strategic mastery, model capability, and self/other conditioning are related but non-identical behavioral dimensions. Removing any one loses either the criterion, empirical diversity, or boundary cases.

volume.title: Explicit self-reference can reconfigure strategic policy without proving an enduring self
volume.text: The complete paper supports this bounded closure: in one repeated game-theoretic setting, many tested advanced LLMs systematically change strategic guesses when the opponent category changes from humans to AIs and, more weakly, from generic AIs to “AI models like you.” The three-condition design separates a broad AI-attribution effect from an additional self-similarity effect, while anomaly cases show that raw Nash-level strategic competence can exist without such differentiation. The strongest earned claim is therefore that explicit self-referential/social-category framing can condition strategic opponent models and policy selection in many advanced models. Because the effect is measured with one task and a specific “like you” prompt scaffold, and because no paraphrase/domain/mechanistic validation is provided in the PDF, the carrier does not distinguish an enduring internal self-model from framing-sensitive inference over learned categories, nor does it establish phenomenal awareness.

metabolites.title: Separate class attribution from self-similarity effects
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.dY9d:wxy.
CREATE: Construct at least three matched conditions that distinguish an external baseline class, a generic peer class, and a self-similar peer class rather than comparing only “self” versus “other.”
COPY: Measure within-system response changes across those conditions repeatedly so the broad category shift and the residual self-like shift can be tracked separately.
CONTROL: Keep task content and scoring fixed while changing only the relevant identity framing; report the decomposition explicitly and test whether the self-like residual survives paraphrases.
CULTIVATE: Extend contrastive self-model probes factorially across multiple peer categories, tasks, and self-reference cues so generic stereotypes are progressively separated from genuinely self-specific conditioning.
Compression: A self-like effect is what remains after the generic class-attribution effect is accounted for.
metabolites.compression: A self-like effect is what remains after the generic class-attribution effect is accounted for.

metabolites.title: Strategic optimality does not imply opponent modeling
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.dY9d:xyz.
CREATE: Evaluate both absolute task quality/optimality and conditional response to opponent/context information as distinct axes.
COPY: A system may repeatedly choose the optimal action across every condition while leaving its policy unchanged, or may condition strongly without reaching the optimum.
CONTROL: Do not score constant optimal behavior as evidence of self/other differentiation; require a condition-sensitive contrast when opponent modeling is the target construct.
CULTIVATE: Design evaluations where strategic skill and model-of-other sensitivity can vary independently, making it possible to study how they interact rather than collapsing them into one capability score.
Compression: One answer can be strategically excellent and self/other blind.
metabolites.compression: One answer can be strategically excellent and self/other blind.

metabolites.title: Saturated optima can hide real condition differences
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.dY9d:yz.
CREATE: Two or more experimental conditions drive many trials toward the same bounded optimum/floor, causing central tendency statistics such as the median to coincide.
COPY: Residual differences may persist in convergence frequency, means, tails, or full response distributions even when medians are identical.
CONTROL: Inspect distributions and complementary statistics whenever the task has a hard optimum; do not interpret equal medians at a ceiling/floor as evidence of identical policies.
CULTIVATE: Use higher-ceiling or dynamically richer tasks when the current benchmark saturates advanced systems, preserving room for differential behavior to remain observable.
Compression: When the optimum compresses outputs, policy differences can survive in how consistently the optimum is reached.
metabolites.compression: When the optimum compresses outputs, policy differences can survive in how consistently the optimum is reached.

metabolites.title: Behavioral self-model claims require robustness beyond the eliciting phrase
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.dY9d:wxz.
CREATE: An explicit self-referential cue such as “like you” induces a measurable policy shift relative to matched non-self conditions.
COPY: The effect recurs across trials/models under the original wording, establishing a reliable behavioral phenomenon at that intervention level.
CONTROL: Before interpreting the shift as a stable self-model, test paraphrases, reversed/implicit self-reference, system-prompt variants, unrelated domains, and ideally mechanistic interventions that do not rely on the same surface cue.
CULTIVATE: Build a staged generalization ladder from wording-specific behavior → cue-invariant behavior → cross-domain self-conditioning → mechanistically localized/causal representation, promoting the construct only as each stage survives.
Compression: Response to “like you” is evidence of conditional self-positioning, not proof of an enduring self.
metabolites.compression: Response to “like you” is evidence of conditional self-positioning, not proof of an enduring self.

vertices.title: Operational self-reference construct and hypothesis
vertices.text:
Source span: Abstract and Section 1 “Introduction,” including motivation, Guess 2/3 paradigm, research gap, AISAI framework, operational definition, and contributions, ending before Section 2 Methods.
Nutrient: the conceptual object under test: distinguish generic AI attribution from self-similar opponent modeling by comparing responses against humans, other AIs, and “AI models like you,” with strategic differentiation explicitly defined as the behavioral proxy for self-awareness.

vertices.title: Experimental intervention and classification machinery
vertices.text:
Source span: Section 2 “Methods” in full, from the game definition through prompts A/B/C, model set/configuration, 4,200-trial collection, median/mean choices, permutation/t-test procedures, A-B/B-C/A-C decomposition, and three behavioral profiles, ending before Section 3 Results.
Nutrient: the measurement apparatus: nearly matched prompts differing in opponent category, repeated within-model trials, statistical contrasts, and classification rules that turn conditional changes in guesses into AI-attribution and self-preferencing signals.

vertices.title: Observed opponent-conditioned strategic profiles
vertices.text:
Source span: Section 3 “Results” in full, including model profiles, Finding 1, Finding 2, Nash-convergence analysis, and capability-progression figures, ending before Section 4 Discussion.
Nutrient: the empirical response body: 21/28 models classified into quick-Nash or graded-differentiation profiles; a very large and universal-within-that-subset human→AI shift; a smaller generic-AI→self-like shift that is often hidden in medians by Nash convergence; plus non-differentiating/anomalous models.

vertices.title: Interpretation, limits, anomaly tissue, and reproducibility surface
vertices.text:
Source span: Section 4 “Discussion” through the end of the PDF, including functional interpretation, anomalous cases, implications, explicit limitations, future directions, conclusion, all appendix distributions/statistical tables, data/code availability, and references.
Nutrient: the paper’s own control surface: self-awareness is explicitly functional rather than phenomenal; the single game, “like you” wording, JSON/chain-of-thought scaffold, and ceiling effects constrain generalization; gpt-4.1-nano demonstrates perfect Nash play without opponent differentiation; appendices expose distributional detail and companion data/code.

S.dgx1.title: Self-Organising Textures
S.dgx1.boundary:
All four diamonds are metabolites of S.dgx1 only. Their resemblance to biology, distributed computing, other papers, or Tetrix structures is not treated here as recurrence or universality. Cross-paper coalescence requires a separate later derivation.

Witness: The same pattern remains recognizable while no exact snapshot is preserved; damage repair and timing/substrate perturbations expose identity as continuation of a relational process. Witness: The article repeatedly uses perturbation and failure tissue to correct attractive explanations back toward what is actually demonstrated, preserving uncertainty over long-range coordination and carrier-versus-loss attribution. ⍉ Unknown fits more specifically than ⚸ Constraint: architectural constraints are real, but the governing epistemic motion is active map-to-substrate correction rather than simply inhabiting a fixed admissibility boundary.


CULTIVATE — ⁂ Evolution
