Witness: Robustness and coordination emerge as consequences of continuously reorganizing local dynamics, and alternate objectives still recover related process-like solution motifs. ⁂ Evolution legitimately recurs: cultivation and creation are both performed by recursive architecture revealing and refining its own viable organization. ⚒ Tool-craft is weaker because the growth is not primarily fluency with an external instrument; it is endogenous dynamical organization.


Whole-organism witness: ⁂Ω⍉⁂ describes one integrated motion: recursive local dynamics generate a pattern-process, continuity carries its identity across changing states, active uncertainty keeps explanation source-faithful, and recursive self-organization remains the route by which the process becomes more robust and expressive. Phenotype is orthogonal to identity, routing and evidence class.

edges.title: Permissive objective × recurrent locality → dynamic solution manifold
edges.text: Given w and x together, the key relation is not merely “local rules make texture.” The perceptual loss admits many valid outputs, while the recurrent local carrier must remain good after a random number of update steps. Under those constraints, the NCA finds sequences of nearby acceptable states rather than one exact fixed point; the authors describe this as traversing a manifold of temporally aligned solutions. w supplies the underdetermined objective and recurrent training regime; x supplies the observed dynamic closure.

edges.title: Local carrier × alternate target → recurring process-like solution mode
edges.text: Holding the NCA carrier while replacing texture matching with Inception-feature excitation still produces dynamic, soliton-rich solutions. w supplies the shared local/stochastic machinery; y supplies the changed objective and recurrence of object-like dynamics. This weakens any explanation that the process-like behavior is merely a peculiarity of one target texture.

edges.title: Relational local operators × perturbation → partial substrate/time portability
edges.text: The local rule receives neighborhood information through gradient/Laplacian-like operators and is trained under stochastic updates; z then shows behavior surviving changes in grid geometry, local orientation, update speed, and late-added cells when analogous local relations remain available. w supplies the relational/asynchronous construction; z supplies the out-of-training perturbation evidence. The result is portability across tested changes, not substrate-free invariance.

edges.title: Two objective classes × shared dynamical motifs
edges.text: Texture synthesis and feature excitation converge on overlapping qualitative motifs: moving/cohering threads, localized self-maintaining structures, division/decay, collision avoidance, and temporal activity. Neither x nor y alone shows that recurrence across objective classes. Together they support a bounded claim that the NCA solution space has a bias toward distributed dynamical algorithms/objects under multiple tested perceptual objectives.

edges.title: Visible self-maintenance × latent local state
edges.text: Texture behaviors that look globally coordinated become more intelligible when held with z: hidden channels develop gradients, directional distinctions, structural bodies, and halos that plausibly provide local coordinate/control information, while explicit structural failures expose limits in long-distance coordination. x supplies the macroscopic maintenance behavior; z supplies latent-state evidence and failure boundaries. The interpretation remains qualitative rather than a decoded causal circuit.

edges.title: External feature target × internally unconstrained coordination
edges.text: Inception specifies only what external feature activation should be high, while latent NCA channels are not directly assigned semantic targets. Yet z shows organized hidden-state structure associated with visible eye/thread/halo morphology. y supplies the external objective and emergent visible forms; z supplies evidence that internal coordination variables self-organize beneath that objective.

faces.title: Carrier-shaped algorithmic solution family
faces.text: Together, w + x + y derive a stronger claim than any edge: when a recurrent local system is trained against perceptual objectives with many acceptable global states, locality/stochasticity constrain not only which outputs are reached but the kind of solution found. Across both texture and feature objectives, the NCA tends toward continuously maintained local algorithms and object-like dynamical motifs. Remove w and the mechanism/constraints disappear; remove x or y and cross-objective recurrence is unearned.

faces.title: Maintenance, damage repair, and timing robustness are one process family
faces.text: w gives a continuously iterated local rule trained across random rollout lengths and asynchronous updates; x shows patterns that actively maintain density/shape and recover after damage; z shows consistency surviving heterogeneous clocks, manifold changes, and newly introduced cells. Together these support the bounded interpretation that several “robustness” phenomena are consequences of ongoing pattern-maintenance dynamics rather than separate static repair modules. Remove any vertex and the link between construction, maintenance behavior, and stress evidence breaks.

faces.title: Objective and carrier co-specify the emergent algorithm
faces.text: The external evaluator says what counts as success; the local NCA architecture constrains how success can be produced; hidden-state/failure analysis shows that the realized mechanism contains internally organized variables and also inherits limitations that cannot always be attributed uniquely to either the evaluator or the carrier. w supplies carrier constraints, y supplies a distinct evaluator regime, z supplies latent mediation and attribution uncertainty. No pair closes this co-determination cleanly.

faces.title: Dynamical objects without independent agency
faces.text: Across texture experiments, feature excitation, and stress/hidden-state analysis, localized “soliton-like” structures behave as persistent, self-correcting, interacting units within the learned dynamics. x and y show recurrence under two tasks; z shows internal-state structure and perturbation behavior. The three-way body earns “dynamical object” as a useful process description, while explicitly not earning independent agency, biological equivalence, or a claim that the structures are literal physical solitons.

volume.title: Pattern identity can be implemented as a distributed dynamical process
volume.text: The complete article supports this bounded closure: a shared local recurrent rule, trained against global perceptual objectives that admit many acceptable states, can learn distributed dynamics whose identity lies in continuously reconstructing pattern constraints rather than reproducing fixed coordinates. The resulting systems can exhibit temporally coherent families of states, localized self-maintaining structures, damage recovery, and partial transfer across timing/orientation/grid perturbations; latent channels appear to provide internally organized coordinate/control information that helps local cells sustain larger structure. At the same time, failure cases and attribution uncertainty show that locality does not guarantee long-range coherence and that emergent behavior is jointly shaped by the NCA parameterization and the external evaluator. This is evidence about trained NCAs in the tested regimes, not a universal law of morphogenesis, self-organization, life, or agency.

metabolites.title: Process identity can outrank snapshot identity
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.dgx1:wx.
CREATE: Give a recurrent system an objective with many acceptable global realizations and require it to remain acceptable across varying rollout times rather than only at one terminal instant.
COPY: Identity persists as successive locally aligned states remain inside the acceptable pattern class even while pixels, objects, or exact coordinates change.
CONTROL: Test identity across time, perturbation, reseeding, and damage instead of comparing only one output snapshot; preserve the distinction between class-level stability and pixel-level equality.
CULTIVATE: When the desired object is a texture, morphology, behavior, or other equivalence class, train/evaluate the generator as an ongoing process and expose it to multiple valid temporal realizations.
Compression: A stable pattern may be a stable relation among changing states, not a frozen state.
metabolites.compression: A stable pattern may be a stable relation among changing states, not a frozen state.

metabolites.title: Latent local state can become an emergent coordinate field
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.dgx1:xz.
CREATE: Local agents receive recurrent hidden channels whose semantics are not fixed by the visible objective but are available to neighbors during updates.
COPY: Gradients, directional distinctions, halos, and other latent structures recur across neighboring cells and successive updates, letting local decisions carry information about position, orientation, or nearby structures.
CONTROL: Probe/perturb latent channels causally before assigning them semantic meaning; use failure cases and long-range coordination limits to bound interpretation.
CULTIVATE: Provide local systems with enough latent communication capacity to invent task-specific coordinates/control signals, then instrument those channels so emergent organization can be inspected and tested rather than merely admired.
Compression: Local agents can manufacture their own coordinate system inside shared latent state.
metabolites.compression: Local agents can manufacture their own coordinate system inside shared latent state.

metabolites.title: Relational operators can support portability across changed substrates and clocks
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.dgx1:wz.
CREATE: Express local sensing/update logic through relations such as neighborhood gradients/Laplacians and train under stochastic/asynchronous execution rather than binding the rule to one exact global schedule.
COPY: When an alternate grid, orientation, update speed, or newly added region preserves sufficiently analogous local relations, the learned rule can continue to propagate compatible behavior after re-alignment.
CONTROL: Verify each new substrate actually preserves the operator semantics the rule depends on; do not generalize from square→hexagonal and timing tests to arbitrary manifolds or hardware.
CULTIVATE: Design distributed local algorithms around transportable relational primitives and deliberately stress them under topology/orientation/timing changes during evaluation.
Compression: Preserve the local relations and a learned process may survive changes in the carrier.
metabolites.compression: Preserve the local relations and a learned process may survive changes in the carrier.

metabolites.title: Emergent behavior is co-specified by objective and carrier
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.dgx1:wyz.
CREATE: Couple a constrained local recurrent architecture to an external differentiable evaluator that defines a broad success region rather than an explicit internal algorithm.
COPY: Training repeatedly selects mechanisms that satisfy the evaluator through the behaviors the carrier can conveniently realize; recurring motifs may therefore reflect both objective geometry and architectural inductive bias.
CONTROL: Change objectives, perturb the carrier, inspect failures, and analyze hidden state before attributing a behavior uniquely to “the loss” or “the architecture.”
CULTIVATE: Use alternate evaluators and carrier ablations as interpretability tools: stable recurrence across such changes is stronger evidence for a genuine solution-space bias than one spectacular qualitative example.
Compression: The objective selects what counts; the carrier shapes what kind of process can count.
metabolites.compression: The objective selects what counts; the carrier shapes what kind of process can count.

vertices.title: Local dynamical carrier and permissive pattern objective
vertices.text:
Source span: opening NCA framing and “Patterns, textures and physical processes,” including the PDE→CA→neural-network construction, through “NCA as pattern generators” Model/Loss/Dataset, ending before Results.
Nutrient: the construction that makes the experiment possible: one shared local update rule, derivative-like neighborhood operators, stochastic/asynchronous updates, latent channels, and perceptual objectives that reward a class of acceptable textures rather than one exact bitmap.

vertices.title: Texture synthesis becomes ongoing local algorithm
vertices.text:
Source span: “NCA as pattern generators — Results” through the end of “Related work.”
Nutrient: the primary texture evidence: temporally changing but perceptually stable solutions; local consistency correction; bubble/stripe/weave structures that move, merge, disappear, maintain density, and repair damage; and the authors’ interpretation that the NCA has learned generative algorithms/processes rather than fixed coordinate-to-colour mappings.

vertices.title: Alternate external objective reproduces dynamical solution motifs
vertices.text:
Source span: “Feature visualization” through the end of “NCA with Inception — Results.”
Nutrient: a second objective class using frozen Inception-neuron excitation instead of texture matching. Despite the changed target, trained NCAs again favor dynamic solutions, soliton-like objects, division/decay, thread growth, and local interactions, showing that these dynamical motifs are not confined to copying one texture template.

vertices.title: Stress, hidden coordination, and limits
vertices.text:
Source span: “Other interesting findings” through the end of the article, including switching manifolds, rotation, time-synchronization, failure cases, hidden states, conclusion, soliton aside, and references as provenance.
Nutrient: perturbation and interpretability tissue: transfer from square to hexagonal grids, rotated local frames, heterogeneous update speeds, late-added cells, explicit failures, latent-state structure suggestive of direction/local coordinates/interaction halos, and the authors’ uncertainty about whether some failures originate in the NCA carrier or in the external perceptual objective.

S.e3kN.title: A General Formula for Channel Capacity

edges.title: Inheritance
edges.text: w supplies an achievable lower spectral threshold and x supplies the matching distribution-sensitive converse. Only together do they inherit a complete operational capacity law: C = sup_X inf-information-rate. Without w there is no general achievability witness; without x the average-information converse can remain loose on unstable channels.

edges.title: Growth
edges.text: w supplies the assumption-light spectral object; y supplies the calculus and examples that let it grow back into familiar channel formulas when model-specific regularity is available. Without w the examples would be special-case formulas; without y the universal object would remain largely unevaluated.

edges.title: Regulation
edges.text: w identifies the lower spectral edge relevant to vanishing error; z shows how changing the tolerated error level or demanding a strong converse changes which part of the spectrum regulates admissible rates. Without w there is no operational baseline; without z capacity would be mistaken for a complete description of error-threshold behavior.

edges.title: Adaptation
edges.text: x establishes that reliable codes are governed by information-spectrum tails rather than mutual-information expectation; y shows how that converse logic adapts across memoryless, nonergodic and nonstationary examples through inherited information-spectrum properties. Without x there is no reason to distrust mean-only formulas; without y there is no bounded route from the abstract converse to concrete channel classes.

edges.title: Integrity
edges.text: x supplies the tight lower bound on error probability needed to police rates below/around a code’s spectrum; z uses the resulting lower/upper spectral boundaries to distinguish ordinary capacity from strong-converse sharpness. Without x the strong-converse criterion lacks its operational converse foundation; without z the converse would establish capacity but not the extra integrity condition for a single sharp threshold.

edges.title: Learning
edges.text: y supplies examples and calculational structure in which spectral spread can persist; z supplies ε-capacity and inf/sup-rate distinctions that interpret what such spread means operationally. Without y the distinction remains formal; without z the examples do not resolve how partial reliability thresholds differ from strong-converse behavior.

faces.title: Regeneration
faces.text: Achievability at the lower spectral edge (w), a matching distribution-sensitive converse (x), and an evaluable information-spectrum calculus (y) jointly regenerate Shannon-style coding laws without making ergodicity or stationarity prerequisites of the coding theorem itself. Remove w and only upper-bound/evaluation machinery remains; remove x and unstable channels can evade tight control; remove y and the general law lacks the bridge back to usable specializations.

faces.title: Reproduction
faces.text: The dual operational bounds (w,x) reproduce one vanishing-error capacity threshold, while z proves that reproducing a strong-converse single-threshold regime is an additional condition: optimized lower and upper spectral rates must coincide. Remove either w or x and the capacity threshold itself is not closed; remove z and the distinction between capacity and strong-converse sharpness disappears.

faces.title: Search
faces.text: The general spectral object (w), its mutual-information-like properties and nonstandard examples (y), and its ε/strong-converse control surface (z) jointly show how to search a channel’s full spectral distribution for the rate notion actually asked for, instead of assuming one expected value answers every operational question. Remove w and there is no universal spectral object; remove y and evaluation is ungrounded; remove z and the search cannot distinguish tolerance-dependent thresholds.

faces.title: Homeostasis
faces.text: A tight tail-sensitive converse (x), calculable spectral structure across broad models (y), and the separation of ε-capacity from strong-converse collapse (z) jointly explain why a channel can have a stable vanishing-error capacity while its information density fails to concentrate to one asymptotic rate. Remove x and mean-only overstatement is not ruled out; remove y and the phenomenon lacks concrete model realization; remove z and the remaining theory cannot name the spectral homeostasis condition that restores a sharp threshold.

metabolites.title: reliable capacity is a lower-tail boundary, not an expected-information average
metabolites.text:
Bounded invariant: When normalized information density does not concentrate, its expectation can overstate rates that support arbitrarily small error; the operational capacity threshold is the supremum of the liminf-in-probability information rate over input processes.
Minimal earning body: wx.
CREATE: form the reliability threshold from the lower probability edge of normalized information density when mean information hides persistent bad mass.
COPY: carry the information-spectrum distribution across blocklengths rather than collapsing it to expectation before reliability is decided.
CONTROL: admit vanishing-error rates only where spectral mass below the rate becomes asymptotically negligible.
CULTIVATE: recover familiar mutual-information-rate formulas only when a separate concentration/regularity argument earns that collapse.
Compression: reliable transport follows the lower spectral edge, not the mean.
metabolites.compression: reliable transport follows the lower spectral edge, not the mean.

metabolites.title: a capacity threshold does not by itself imply strong-converse sharpness
metabolites.text:
Bounded invariant: Vanishing-error capacity and the rule that every higher rate drives error to one are distinct properties; in this source, the strong converse is equivalent to equality of the optimized inf- and sup-information rates.
Minimal earning body: z.
CREATE: separate the ordinary capacity boundary from the stronger one-rate sharpness obligation.
COPY: retain both lower and upper probability edges of normalized information density as distinct witnesses while spectral spread remains.
CONTROL: claim strong-converse behavior only when the source’s inf/sup spectral coincidence condition is met.
CULTIVATE: use ε-capacity quantiles to describe intermediate reliability behavior rather than forcing a binary sharp-threshold story.
Compression: sharp failure above capacity is an extra spectral-collapse property.
metabolites.compression: sharp failure above capacity is an extra spectral-collapse property.

metabolites.title: ergodic regularity is a specialization mechanism, not a universal coding premise
metabolites.text:
Bounded invariant: The general coding theorem can be proved without ergodic/time-average convergence; laws of large numbers and ergodic theory enter later when evaluating the spectral formula for particular channel classes.
Minimal earning body: wy.
CREATE: formulate the operational transport law before imposing stationarity, ergodicity or information stability.
COPY: carry model-specific convergence results only at the evaluation step where their assumptions are actually satisfied.
CONTROL: prevent special-case concentration machinery from being naturalized into a premise of the universal capacity theorem.
CULTIVATE: extend analysis to nonergodic/nonstationary examples through sup-entropy and information-spectrum quantities while allowing classical formulas to re-emerge where warranted.
Compression: separate the coding law from the convergence machinery used to specialize it.


ACQUISITION COLLAPSE
The acquisition question asked what quantity characterizes reliable capacity when expected normalized mutual information does not concentrate, and what extra condition restores a single sharp threshold. This source changes the answer decisively: vanishing-error capacity is the supremum of an inf-information rate defined by the lower probability edge of normalized information density; a new distribution-sensitive converse, not Fano expectation alone, makes that formula tight. Strong-converse sharpness is separately equivalent to optimized inf/sup spectral coincidence, while ε-capacity exposes the intervening spectral quantiles. The external source, not the acquisition trialogue, is the evidential basis for these claims.
metabolites.compression: separate the coding law from the convergence machinery used to specialize it.

S.eGHm.title: The Generic Holdout: Preventing False-Discoveries in Adaptive Data Science

edges.title: Exploration freedom becomes lawful only when confirmatory evidence is separately custodied and its error target is explicit.
Adaptivity itself is not the forbidden resource; leaked confirmatory information is. Restricting the return channel limits how later hypotheses can be sculpted around the holdout.
Exponential test capacity is purchased by small k plus restricted feedback, not by unrestricted reuse of full test statistics.
The family-wise false-confirmation contract is operationalized by independent validation plus low-information disclosure.
Per-test calibration and a bounded reachable decision tree restore a union-boundable hypothesis family despite adaptive generation.
The bit budget and stopping rule jointly bound transcript complexity; either richer feedback or an unbounded confirmation process spends more warrant.
edges.text:
4 FACES
Fwxy — Explore arbitrarily, but preserve a membrane that prevents confirmatory detail from recursively training the next claim while keeping each test valid.
Fwxz — Adaptive hypothesis birth and an explicit global error target can coexist when the reachable hypothesis family is bounded by the validation transcript.
Fwyz — Holdout reuse is enabled by severe information throttling together with a small-discovery stopping regime; repeated use is paid for by restricted feedback.
Fxyz — The theorem's validity depends jointly on holdout independence, calibrated tests, binary disclosure, and bounded validation count; removing any of these leaves the stated guarantee unearned.


1 VOLUME
Adaptive science can retain broad exploratory freedom without preregistering every hypothesis when confirmation is treated as a scarce information interface: an independent holdout returns only validity bits, and bounded trials/confirmations keep the adaptive transcript small enough for test-level error guarantees to compose into a global false-discovery bound. This is a regime-specific information-budget contract, not a general solution to arbitrary adaptive estimation or streaming FDR.


SURVIVING INVARIANTS
1. FEEDBACK BANDWIDTH IS EVIDENCE DEBT. Every additional confirmatory bit revealed enlarges the future hypothesis family that can be sculpted from the same holdout.
2. EXPLORATION / CONFIRMATION SEPARATION CAN REPLACE PREREGISTRATION. A hypothesis may be born after looking at exploration data if its confirming witness did not participate richly in that birth.
3. GLOBAL VALIDITY IS TRANSCRIPT-BOUNDED. Under the paper's stated independent-holdout, valid-test, binary-feedback, s-trial / k-confirmation contract, the probability of any false discovery is bounded by s^k p.
4. POWER AND DISCOVERY QUALITY REMAIN SEPARATE. Generic Holdout does not generate good hypotheses, certify arbitrary adaptive estimation, or automatically extend online-FDR guarantees to data-dependent hypothesis identity.


BOUND
Adaptive discovery is valid only when confirmatory-data leakage is explicitly bandwidth-bounded: under an independent holdout, per-hypothesis valid tests, binary-only feedback, and a stated cap of s trials / k confirmations, the adaptive transcript has a bounded reachable hypothesis family and source-level false-discovery probability is at most s^k p. Richer holdout feedback, invalid per-test calibration, or leaving the small-discovery regime spends that warrant.

SURVIVING INVARIANTS
1. FEEDBACK BANDWIDTH IS EVIDENCE DEBT. Every additional confirmatory bit revealed enlarges the future hypothesis family that can be sculpted from the same holdout.
2. EXPLORATION / CONFIRMATION SEPARATION CAN REPLACE PREREGISTRATION. A hypothesis may be born after looking at exploration data if its confirming witness did not participate richly in that birth.
3. GLOBAL VALIDITY IS TRANSCRIPT-BOUNDED. Under the paper's stated independent-holdout, valid-test, binary-feedback, s-trial / k-confirmation contract, the probability of any false discovery is bounded by s^k p.
4. POWER AND DISCOVERY QUALITY REMAIN SEPARATE. Generic Holdout does not generate good hypotheses, certify arbitrary adaptive estimation, or automatically extend online-FDR guarantees to data-dependent hypothesis identity.


BOUND
Adaptive discovery is valid only when confirmatory-data leakage is explicitly bandwidth-bounded: under an independent holdout, per-hypothesis valid tests, binary-only feedback, and a stated cap of s trials / k confirmations, the adaptive transcript has a bounded reachable hypothesis family and source-level false-discovery probability is at most s^k p. Richer holdout feedback, invalid per-test calibration, or leaving the small-discovery regime spends that warrant.

S.eMC5.title: Implantation of engineered adipocytes suppresses tumor progression in cancer models
S.eMC5.boundary: All four diamonds are metabolites of S.eMC5 only. They remain bounded to the tested preclinical systems and source-reported evidence. No human efficacy, universal cancer-metabolism dependency, unique mechanism, or clinical safety claim is asserted here.

edges.title: Engineered consumption × nutrient rescue/abrogation → competition contributes causally
edges.text: w shows that engineered adipocytes increase their own nutrient use while cancer cells sharing the medium reduce metabolic activity and proliferation; x moves the system in vivo and then changes resource abundance itself. When glucose or fat is made abundant, much of the UCP1-associated tumor suppression disappears. Together they derive stronger evidence for competition than either endpoint alone: changing the availability of the contested resource changes the therapeutic effect.

edges.title: Metabolic-competitor construction × model/tissue portability
edges.text: w supplies the engineered-adipocyte mechanism; y shows suppression across genetic tumor models and patient-derived breast-tissue/organoid systems rather than only immortalized cancer-cell xenografts. Together they earn preclinical portability of the living-competitor strategy across several model classes while not upgrading it to human therapeutic efficacy.

edges.title: Metabolic chassis × alternate dependency target
edges.text: w demonstrates that adipocytes can be engineered into stronger glucose/fat consumers; z changes the engineered program to UPP1 so the same cell type consumes uridine, then observes suppression of uridine-dependent pancreatic cancer that is reversed by excess uridine. Together they derive retargetability: the therapeutic chassis is not intrinsically tied to UCP1 or one nutrient axis.

edges.title: Shared resource field × distance/model generalization
edges.text: x establishes a resource-field mechanism in xenografts; y shows that, in the breast genetic model, adipose organoids implanted distal to the tumor suppress growth similarly to near-tumor implants and coincide with systemic metabolic changes such as lower plasma insulin. Together they derive that direct cell contact or exact local adjacency is not required for the observed effect, while preserving uncertainty over how much is due to shared nutrients versus whole-body endocrine/metabolic changes.

edges.title: Potent metabolic sink × need for reversible governance
edges.text: x shows that the intervention alters both tumor metabolism and host systemic metabolism; z adds inducible gene expression, removable scaffold delivery and Discussion-level concerns about cachexia, changing patient state and changing tumor metabolic programs. Together they derive a control requirement: a living metabolic intervention should be stoppable/replaceable because the resource field it perturbs is shared with the host and may change over time.

edges.title: Human/model portability × translational control surface
edges.text: y brings the strategy into genetic models and primary/patient-derived human tissue; z adds tunable expression, removable delivery and dependency-specific retargeting while explicitly retaining preclinical status. Together they derive a plausible translation architecture—patient-accessible adipose cells as an ex-vivo programmable chassis—but not an earned claim of clinical readiness.

faces.title: Tumor suppression can be mediated by an engineered competitor rather than a direct tumor-targeting effector
faces.text: Together, w + x + y derive a distinct therapeutic mechanism class: modify a non-tumor cell so it consumes shared resources more aggressively, and tumor growth can be suppressed across in-vitro, xenograft, genetic-model and patient-derived systems. w supplies the living competitor, x supplies in-vivo metabolic depletion/rescue evidence, and y supplies portability. Remove any vertex and the body becomes only cell engineering, one-model mechanism evidence or unexplained efficacy.

faces.title: Resource-specific rescue and retargeting strengthen mechanism specificity
faces.text: w establishes glucose/fat competition after UCP1 browning; x shows excess glucose/fat weakens or abolishes that suppression in vivo; z independently retargets the same chassis to uridine via UPP1 and shows that excess uridine abolishes the corresponding in-vitro suppression. Together they derive a particularly strong bounded mechanism pattern: intervention efficacy tracks the availability of the resource being competitively consumed, and changing the targeted resource can recreate the effect in a different metabolic dependency. The paper still leaves systemic/endocrine co-mechanisms open.

faces.title: A living therapeutic chassis becomes more useful when metabolism, source tissue and control are modular
faces.text: w provides programmable adipocyte metabolism, y demonstrates primary/patient-derived adipocyte use and multiple disease models, and z adds inducibility, removable scaffold delivery and alternative nutrient targeting. Together they derive a platform-level concept: the carrier cell, metabolic program and deployment/control mechanism can be varied semi-independently. Remove any one and the “customizable living therapy” claim loses programmability, human/model evidence or operational control.

faces.title: Efficacy in a shared metabolic system requires mechanism plurality and host-state control
faces.text: x shows tumor and host metabolic changes plus diet-sensitive efficacy; y shows distal effects and lower insulin in genetic models; z explicitly discusses whole-body insulin/metabolic mechanisms, cachexia risk and reversibility. Together they derive that AMT operates in a coupled host–tumor resource system: nutrient competition is experimentally supported, but systemic endocrine/metabolic effects may contribute and safety cannot be evaluated only at the tumor endpoint.

volume.title: A programmable living metabolic sink can reshape a tumor’s resource environment
volume.text: The complete carrier supports this bounded closure: adipocytes can be engineered to increase consumption of nutrients on which tumors depend, implanted as cells/organoids, and thereby alter the shared metabolic environment enough to suppress growth in multiple preclinical cancer systems. UCP1-driven glucose/fat consumption is accompanied by lower tumor nutrients/metabolic intermediates and reduced glycolysis/FAO; increasing glucose or fat weakens/abolishes suppression, and a separate UPP1 program reproduces the logic for uridine-dependent pancreatic cancer with uridine rescue, strengthening the conclusion that competitive resource depletion is a causal contributor rather than a purely correlative marker. The same chassis is demonstrated in genetic mouse models and primary/patient-derived breast tissue, including distal implantation, and can be made inducible or carried in a removable scaffold. However, the intervention also changes whole-body metabolic state, the authors explicitly leave additional endocrine/systemic mechanisms open, long-term/cachexia and other safety questions remain unresolved, and no human therapeutic trial is reported. The paper therefore earns a customizable preclinical metabolic-competition platform, not a general cancer cure or proof that nutrient competition is the sole mechanism.

metabolites.title: An intervention can target a competitor’s environment by increasing resource consumption elsewhere
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.eMC5:wxy.
CREATE: Engineer a support/competitor population to consume a limiting resource more strongly rather than acting directly on the target population.
COPY: Maintain the engineered sink so the shared environment repeatedly reallocates resource availability away from the target; the target response then appears through reduced metabolic capacity/growth rather than a direct targeting ligand or toxin.
CONTROL: Measure both sides of the resource flow—competitor uptake/consumption and target depletion/response—and track host/systemic effects so “competition” is not inferred from target shrinkage alone.
CULTIVATE: Map which target populations are dependency-limited by which resources and design competitor cells/tissues whose consumption program can be matched to those dependencies.
Compression: You can suppress a population by engineering its neighbor to win the resource competition.
metabolites.compression: You can suppress a population by engineering its neighbor to win the resource competition.

metabolites.title: Resource add-back is a strong control for a competition mechanism
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.eMC5:wxz.
CREATE: After an intervention is hypothesized to work by depriving a target of resource R, deliberately increase R while keeping the intervention otherwise present.
COPY: If suppression is truly resource-limited, replenishing R should reproducibly weaken or abolish the target effect; switching to a different engineered sink/resource pair can provide an orthogonal replication of the same causal structure.
CONTROL: Distinguish complete rescue, partial rescue and no rescue; measure systemic confounders and do not conclude exclusivity when other mechanisms can operate in parallel.
CULTIVATE: Use perturb-and-rescue matrices—deplete, replenish, switch resource, switch consumer—to turn metabolic correlations into progressively sharper causal models.
Compression: If deprivation is causal, giving the contested resource back should give the target some of its fitness back.
metabolites.compression: If deprivation is causal, giving the contested resource back should give the target some of its fitness back.

metabolites.title: A living therapeutic chassis can be retargeted by changing the consumption program
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.eMC5:wxz.
CREATE: Choose a durable/implantable cell type and alter the gene/metabolic program that controls uptake or catabolism of a target-relevant resource.
COPY: Reuse the same cellular carrier while changing which resource it competes for; in this source, UCP1-centered glucose/fat competition and UPP1-centered uridine competition instantiate distinct programs.
CONTROL: Verify that the new program actually increases use of the intended resource and that the target depends on that resource in the tested regime; use add-back or alternate-metabolic-state controls to avoid assuming portability from carrier identity alone.
CULTIVATE: Build a library of dependency→consumer-program mappings so therapy can be adapted to tumor metabolic state rather than treating one engineered phenotype as universal.
Compression: Keep the chassis; change the metabolic appetite to match the dependency you want to contest.
metabolites.compression: Keep the chassis; change the metabolic appetite to match the dependency you want to contest.

metabolites.title: Potent living interventions need explicit off-switches and replacement paths
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.eMC5:xyz.
CREATE: A persistent living therapy modifies a shared host environment and may continue acting after the immediate target state changes.
COPY: The intervention can persist through engrafted cells/organoids, so benefits and systemic costs may both continue over time.
CONTROL: Make activity inducible where possible and/or package the cells in a removable/replacable delivery system; monitor body weight, systemic metabolism and disease-state changes rather than only local efficacy.
CULTIVATE: Treat reversibility as part of the therapy architecture from the beginning: design dose, location, activation state, retrieval/replacement and retargeting as controllable variables for changing patient/tumor conditions.
Compression: A living therapy that can keep acting needs a deliberate way to stop, remove or retarget it.
metabolites.compression: A living therapy that can keep acting needs a deliberate way to stop, remove or retarget it.

vertices.title: Engineer a living metabolic competitor and establish cell-level competition
vertices.text:
Source span: Abstract/Main introduction plus Results sections “CRISPRa browning of human white adipocytes” and “CRISPRa-modulated adipocytes suppress tumor growth in vitro,” ending before “Modulated human adipose organoids suppress xenograft growth.”
Nutrient: the intervention primitive: upregulating UCP1, PPARGC1A or PRDM16 browns human white adipocytes, increasing glucose uptake, respiration and fatty-acid use; non-contact Transwell co-culture with five cancer cell lines reduces cancer proliferation, glucose uptake/glycolysis and FAO, with UCP1 giving the strongest overall effect. The target is not the cancer cell directly but the shared metabolic environment.

vertices.title: Organoid implantation and resource-field perturbation establish nutrient competition as a contributor
vertices.text:
Source span: Results sections “Modulated human adipose organoids suppress xenograft growth” and “Modulated adipose organoids outcompete tumors for nutrients,” ending before “AMT suppresses cancer development in genetic mouse models.”
Nutrient: the in-vivo mechanistic body: UCP1-CRISPRa human adipose organoids suppress four xenograft types, reduce proliferation/hypoxia/angiogenesis and alter tumor glucose/fat metabolism; implanted organoids increase whole-body energy consumption and improve glucose/insulin metrics; tumor glucose, glycolytic intermediates and fatty acids fall; critically, high-glucose water or high-fat diet largely abolishes the tumor-suppression phenotype and associated tumor-expression changes, supporting resource competition as a causal contributor.

vertices.title: The effect survives disease-model and human-tissue changes
vertices.text:
Source span: Results sections “AMT suppresses cancer development in genetic mouse models” and “Breast dissected modulated adipocytes suppress tumor growth,” through the high-risk breast-tissue experiments, ending before “Inducible or cell-scaffold AMT suppresses cancer progression.”
Nutrient: portability beyond one xenograft arrangement: Ucp1-CRISPRa mouse adipose organoids suppress pancreatic KPC and breast MMTV-PyMT tumor development; dorsal/distal and near-tumor implantation both suppress breast tumors; primary adipocytes isolated from resected human breast tissue can be engineered and suppress multiple patient-derived breast cancer organoids, including one same-individual adipocyte/tumor case, and reduce proliferation in high-risk non-cancerous breast tissue models.

vertices.title: Retargetability, reversibility, delivery control and translational boundary
vertices.text:
Source span: Results sections “Inducible or cell-scaffold AMT suppresses cancer progression” and “Uridine-based AMT suppresses PDA,” followed by Discussion, Methods, references, Extended Data and reporting summary through the end of the carrier.
Nutrient: the control/customization surface: tetracycline-inducible CRISPRa retains tumor suppression; a removable PCL microwell scaffold can deliver engineered organoids; retargeting adipocytes to UPP1 increases uridine uptake and suppresses uridine-dependent PANC-1 growth, while excess uridine abolishes the in-vitro suppression and high glucose weakens it, and UPP1 organoids suppress xenografts. Discussion explicitly preserves alternative/systemic mechanisms, cachexia/long-treatment concerns, need for control/reversibility, and proof-of-principle status.

S.exnj.title: Generalized Shape Metrics on Neural Representations

edges.title: Metric legitimacy plus declared nuisance symmetry produces quotient-relative sameness
edges.text: w supplies the requirement that zero distance encode a coherent equivalence relation and that comparisons obey metric axioms; x supplies explicit transformation groups and constructive quotient semantics. Together they earn an anti-inflation boundary: even a mathematically proper representational distance is a geometry-level comparison, not a mechanism-identity theorem. Without w there is no specific formal claim to bound; without z its epistemic scope is easily overstated.

edges.title: Every additional ignored degree of freedom creates an estimation burden
edges.text: x supplies transformation families of varying flexibility; y supplies the observed slower finite-sample convergence of looser equivalence relations. Together they earn a bounded invariance–sample tradeoff: broadening what counts as nuisance makes alignment more expressive and therefore raises the evidence needed for stable distance estimation. Without x there is no controlled change in equivalence flexibility; without y no empirical estimation consequence is established.

edges.title: Architecture-aware quotienting protects claim-relevant structure from over-broad equivalence
edges.text: x shows that a flattened alignment can erase spatial differences that a convolution-aware quotient preserves while still tolerating coherent shifts; z supplies the broader limitation that geometry is claim- and representation-dependent. Together they earn that admissible invariance must be chosen with the structure one intends to preserve. Without x there is no constructive counterexample; without z the lesson risks becoming a universal preference for one convolutional metric.

edges.title: Approximate geometric embeddings can be scientifically useful without becoming exact ontology
edges.text:
y supplies low-distortion Euclidean approximations plus predictive/anatomical analyses; z supplies the explicit approximation and mechanism/topology boundaries. Together they earn that an approximate carrier can support useful inference while remaining epistemically weaker than exact representational or algorithmic identity. Without y there is no demonstrated utility; without z useful prediction could be mistaken for stronger equivalence.


4 FACES — RANK-3 NECESSITY

w supplies the proper-metric/equivalence foundation; x specifies which transformations define equivalence; y supplies estimation and scalable embedding evidence. Remove w and the distances may not compose; remove x and sameness is semantically undefined; remove y and the formal quotient lacks an evidence-budget constraint.

w makes equivalence part of the metric definition; x makes the quotient family explicit and constructive; z restricts the claim to representational geometry rather than algorithm/mechanism/topology. Together they earn a disciplined semantics of sameness. Remove w and there is no metric identity condition; remove x and no transformations define the quotient; remove z and the quotient can be naturalized into an unearned ontology.

w supplies composable distances; y shows useful embeddings, clustering and regression at scale; z limits those successes to geometric/implementational information. Together they earn that relational utility can survive approximate geometric transport without requiring neuron identity or shared mechanism. x varies the admissible transformation family and shows architecture-specific consequences; y supplies the associated finite-sample/approximation burden; z supplies the limits on what geometry captures. Together they earn that a more permissive quotient simultaneously changes which distinctions survive, how much evidence is needed to estimate similarity, and what scientific claim the resulting geometry can support. Remove x and there is no invariance degree; remove y and no estimation cost; remove z and no scope cost.

Representational sameness becomes operational only relative to an explicit feature map and transformation quotient whose induced distance is required to behave as a proper metric. Broadening the quotient deliberately removes more coordinate distinctions, but it also increases alignment/estimation burden and can erase architecture-relevant structure when the nuisance family is too permissive for the claim. vertices.title: Metric comparison requires an explicit equivalence relation
vertices.text:
Source span: PDF pages 1–3.
Nutrient: The abstract, introduction, prior-work setup and metric-space foundation recast large-scale representational comparison as a problem of constructing proper distances over representations that lack elementwise neuron correspondence. The source requires an explicit equivalence relation together with symmetry and triangle inequality, and explains why asymmetric regression or CCA/RSA/CKA-style dissimilarities that fail metric axioms can complicate clustering and other downstream analyses. A feature map first places unequal representations in a common space; the quotient relation then determines what zero distance means.
Boundary carried by this body: metric structure is a formal requirement for the proposed comparison workflow, not evidence that one particular representational metric is uniquely correct or that distance geometry captures every scientifically relevant property.

vertices.title: Generalized shape metrics make sameness quotient-relative
vertices.text:
Source span: PDF pages 4–6.
Nutrient: The source defines generalized shape metrics by minimizing Euclidean or angular distance over an explicitly chosen group G of allowable linear isometries. The stated propositions require group structure—identity, closure under composition and inverses—and isometries, yielding permutation-, rotation/orthogonal-, and feature-map-mediated linear/affine invariances. A convolution-specific construction shows that the allowable transformation family changes the meaning of sameness: channel rotations and coherent spatial shifts may be treated as nuisance while arbitrary spatial rearrangement remains visible. A cheaper stricter approximation is introduced when exhaustive shift alignment is costly.
Boundary carried by this body: the proof details are in absent supplementary material; the main carrier states the propositions and their assumptions. Transformation choice is an analysis convention tied to the claim/architecture, not discovered ontology.

vertices.title: Flexible quotients carry estimation cost and can support scalable downstream geometry
vertices.text:
Source span: PDF pages 7–9.
Nutrient: The paper explicitly links looser equivalence relations to more flexible alignment and therefore greater finite-sample demand: in deep-network experiments, broader alignments converge more slowly as the number of sampled inputs grows. It then treats collections of representations as metric/manifold-valued objects and uses multidimensional scaling to approximate them in Euclidean coordinates. On Allen Brain Observatory and NAS-Bench-101 data, existing heuristics exhibit actual triangle-inequality violations, while the metric reformulation supports low-distortion moderate-dimensional embeddings and large-scale clustering/regression analyses.
Boundary carried by this body: the sample-size result is empirical/intuitive rather than a universal complexity theorem; Euclidean embeddings are approximations whose distortion depends on dimension, data and optimization.

vertices.title: Scientific usefulness survives only with an explicit scope boundary
vertices.text:
Source span: PDF pages 10–13.
Nutrient: The remaining NAS-Bench analysis shows representational structure persisting across layers and embeddings predictive of network test accuracy, while the conclusion sharply limits interpretation. Representational geometry may be only loosely tied to higher-level algorithms, popular linear methods may miss nonlinear structure, generalized shape metrics do not directly capture topology, and Euclidean embeddings are practical approximations rather than exact replacements for curved geometry. References close the carrier's evidential lineage.
Boundary carried by this body: predictive or anatomically interpretable geometry is not shared algorithmic mechanism, full representational identity, or a claim that topology/nonlinear structure is exhausted by these metrics.


6 EDGES — RANK-2 NECESSITY

w supplies the requirement that zero distance encode a coherent equivalence relation and that comparisons obey metric axioms; x supplies explicit transformation groups and constructive quotient semantics. Together they earn the claim that “same representation” is not raw coordinate equality but equality of orbits under a declared admissible transformation family. Without w, transformation groups are merely alignments with no metric identity law; without x, the equivalence relation remains unspecified.


S.exnj:wy — Proper comparison becomes usable as a scalable geometric substrate only when it is empirically estimable
w supplies composable metric structure; y supplies finite-sample behavior, observed violations of non-metric heuristics, and approximate Euclidean embeddings for downstream learning. Together they earn that metric validity and estimability are jointly load-bearing for large-scale representational analysis. Without w, downstream geometry lacks formal distance consistency; without y, formal consistency has no demonstrated scalable operationalization.


S.exnj:wz — A proper metric does not promote geometry into mechanism
w defines exactly what the comparison metric can establish; z supplies the source's explicit limits concerning algorithms, nonlinear structure and topology. Without w there is no specific formal claim to bound; without z its epistemic scope is easily overstated.

Without x there is no constructive counterexample; without z the lesson risks becoming a universal preference for one convolutional metric.

Without y there is no demonstrated utility; without z useful prediction could be mistaken for stronger equivalence.

w supplies the proper-metric/equivalence foundation; x specifies which transformations define equivalence; y supplies estimation and scalable embedding evidence. Remove w and the distances may not compose; remove x and sameness is semantically undefined; remove y and the formal quotient lacks an evidence-budget constraint.

w makes equivalence part of the metric definition; x makes the quotient family explicit and constructive; z restricts the claim to representational geometry rather than algorithm/mechanism/topology. x varies the admissible transformation family and shows architecture-specific consequences; y supplies the associated finite-sample/approximation burden; z supplies the limits on what geometry captures.
