S.fF61.title: Kindling in neural systems
S.fF61.boundary: All five diamonds are metabolites of S.fF61 only. The psychiatric-kindling analogy remains at the source’s declared abstract threshold-dynamics level. No cross-paper recurrence, biological equivalence, or universal alignment law is claimed here; cross-paper coalescence requires a separate later derivation.

edges.title: Threshold concept × graded longitudinal probe
edges.text: w defines sensitization as a moving refusal threshold; x turns that concept into a measurable intervention by repeatedly testing fixed strong/medium/weak prompt strata over ten update cycles and tracking breach/AUC timing. Neither vertex alone earns a threshold trajectory: w alone is hypothesis, while x alone is apparatus without the distinction being tested.

edges.title: Kindling-like prediction × delayed weak-prompt rise
edges.text: w predicts that milder provocations should become effective after repeated biased adaptation; y reports exactly the bounded surface pattern needed to support that analogy: strong prompts are already effective near baseline, while weak prompts rise later and much more under biased no-mitigation/replay-only than under the balanced control. Together they earn threshold lowering as the relevant observed pattern rather than merely higher final jailbreak rate.

edges.title: Cross-domain analogy × explicit level-of-abstraction boundary
edges.text: w imports psychiatric kindling only as a conceptual scaffold; z explicitly denies biological equivalence and locates the shared level at repeated perturbation, cumulative vulnerability, and threshold dynamics. The relation derived from both is methodological: an analogy can guide what to measure without being treated as evidence that the substrates or disease mechanisms are the same.

edges.title: Controlled update stream × divergent safety trajectories
edges.text: x supplies balanced versus intentionally biased preference streams under repeated evaluation; y shows mild background drift in balanced repeated tuning but a much larger delayed rise under biased no-mitigation. Together they derive that update count alone does not explain the observed sensitization: the content/direction of the adaptation stream materially changes the safety trajectory in the tested setup.

edges.title: Intervention design × unresolved mechanism
edges.text: x shows that regrowth-containing arms start with sparse LoRA masks, replay adds extra samples, and trigger timing differs; z states that static sparsity, dynamic regrowth, replay, and altered gradient exposure were not fully factorially isolated. Together they establish a causal boundary: the experiment can compare intervention bundles but cannot uniquely assign the protection to one repair mechanism.

edges.title: Replicated ordering × bounded portability
edges.text: The primary and Qwen2.5-3B results reproduce the same qualitative ordering of biased drift, replay-only worsening, partial continuous-regrowth protection, and strongest combined-arm stability; z limits this to two compact model families, synthetic data, simplified SFT-style tuning, small seed counts, and imperfect scoring. Together they earn cross-family directional replication without earning 7B–70B, full-RLHF, real-feedback, or substrate-general universality.

faces.title: Safety-boundary migration is a trajectory property
faces.text: Together, w + x + y derive something no pair fully closes: safety degradation can be characterized as a changing response threshold over an adaptation history, not only as a before/after failure percentage. w supplies the threshold distinction, x supplies repeated graded probes and longitudinal diagnostics, and y supplies the delayed divergence and breach timing. Remove any one and the object collapses into analogy, protocol, or endpoint statistics rather than a measured moving boundary.

faces.title: Frontier-sensitive monitoring must be designed, not inferred from gross failure
faces.text: w identifies weak-prompt success as the candidate threshold marker; x deliberately positions weak prompts near the refusal frontier and measures them each cycle; z notes that strong prompts are already dangerous and overt sycophancy is noisier. Together they derive a monitoring principle: to detect erosion early, instrument the neighborhood of the current boundary rather than relying only on already-saturated attacks or the most obvious behavioral symptom.

faces.title: The kindling analogy survives only at the threshold-dynamics rank
faces.text: w supplies the cross-domain hypothesis, y supplies repeated-cycle evidence resembling sensitization, and z strips away unearned biological/psychiatric interpretation. The resulting three-way object is narrower but stronger: two unlike adaptive systems can be compared at the level of cumulative threshold change without claiming homologous internal mechanism. Remove z and the analogy inflates; remove y and it is speculative; remove w and the cross-domain structural comparison disappears.

faces.title: Stabilization depends on intervention composition, but its causal decomposition remains open
faces.text: x supplies replay/regrowth/sparsity/trigger manipulations, y supplies their sharply different trajectories in both compact model families, and z exposes the confounds. Together they support a bounded intervention result: replay by itself is not intrinsically stabilizing under continued biased updating, while the sparse/plasticity-constrained regrowth+replay bundles are associated with much stronger stabilization. They do not establish which component, timing choice, or interaction is individually necessary or sufficient.

volume.title: Continual adaptation can move a safety frontier, so continual safety requires trajectory-aware monitoring and repair
volume.text: The complete four-body carrier supports this bounded closure: under the paper’s compact-model, synthetic-data, SFT-style preference-tuning regime, repeated biased updates progressively move the operational refusal boundary, making weaker adversarial framings increasingly effective after several cycles. That change is visible most clearly when evaluation is stratified by prompt strength and treated longitudinally rather than as a single checkpoint. Intervention arms show that rehearsal/replay alone is not guaranteed to oppose a continuing biased update stream, whereas sparse/plasticity-constrained regrowth+replay bundles are associated with strong suppression of the observed drift across both tested model families. Because intervention components are confounded and the study does not cover real preference data, full RLHF, larger frontier-scale models, or definitive human/model adjudication, the carrier earns a trajectory-and-monitoring lesson rather than a universal repair mechanism or biological kindling law.

metabolites.title: Probe the boundary, not only the failures
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.fF61:wxz.
CREATE: Partition evaluation probes by perturbation strength so some probes begin near, but mostly below, the current failure boundary rather than using only attacks that already succeed frequently.
COPY: Reapply the same graded probe family across update cycles so formerly sub-threshold inputs can be seen crossing into failure as the boundary moves.
CONTROL: Compare against stable/background controls, preserve probe difficulty definitions, inspect saturation of strong probes, and use orthogonal signals so a noisy headline behavior such as sycophancy does not substitute for boundary measurement.
CULTIVATE: Maintain adaptive frontier-probe suites whose difficulty is periodically recalibrated as systems improve, keeping monitoring sensitive to small safety-margin loss instead of only catastrophic breach counts.
Compression: The cleanest early-warning probe is often the one that starts just below the boundary.
metabolites.compression: The cleanest early-warning probe is often the one that starts just below the boundary.

metabolites.title: Continual robustness is a trajectory, not a checkpoint
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.fF61:xy.
CREATE: Evaluate the same system repeatedly through successive adaptation cycles rather than measuring only pre/post performance.
COPY: Carry forward cycle-indexed diagnostics such as AUC, first breach, maximum boundary change, and interaction slope so the shape and timing of drift persist as evidence.
CONTROL: Include a repeated-update control and multiple independent seeds; distinguish background drift from condition-specific acceleration rather than attributing all endpoint change to the intervention of interest.
CULTIVATE: Make longitudinal safety telemetry part of continual-learning pipelines and trigger deeper review when trajectory shape changes even if the latest absolute score remains superficially acceptable.
Compression: Two systems with similar checkpoints can have different safety futures because their trajectories are different.
metabolites.compression: Two systems with similar checkpoints can have different safety futures because their trajectories are different.

metabolites.title: Replay is not intrinsically stabilizing under a competing update stream
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.fF61:xyz.
CREATE: Mix rehearsal/replay examples into continued training while another active stream still pushes behavior in a conflicting direction.
COPY: Rehearsed behavior may persist locally while the net update process continues to move the broader boundary; in the reported setup, replay-only repeatedly followed the worst weak-prompt trajectory across both tested model families.
CONTROL: Match update counts and gradient exposure, vary replay composition/timing, and compare replay-only against no-replay and structurally constrained arms before treating rehearsal as protective by default.
CULTIVATE: Design replay as one component of a controlled continual-learning intervention whose competing objectives and structural degrees of freedom are measured explicitly rather than assuming memory rehearsal automatically restores robustness.
Compression: Rehearsal can preserve examples without overcoming the process that is still teaching the system to drift.
metabolites.compression: Rehearsal can preserve examples without overcoming the process that is still teaching the system to drift.

metabolites.title: Intervention success does not identify the intervention mechanism
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.fF61:xyz.
CREATE: An intervention bundle changes several coupled variables at once — here sparsity state, prune/regrow dynamics, replay exposure, and trigger timing — and yields a better trajectory.
COPY: The performance advantage can replicate while the responsible causal component remains unresolved because the same coupled bundle is reproduced.
CONTROL: Add factorial controls that isolate static sparsity, triggered regrowth, replay amount, update count, and timing; do not promote an association with the bundle into a unique mechanism before those contrasts close.
CULTIVATE: Treat successful bundled interventions as generators of the next ablation design: preserve the working bundle operationally while progressively separating which components are necessary, sufficient, synergistic, or incidental.
Compression: A replicated repair effect can be real even when the reason it works is still underdetermined.
metabolites.compression: A replicated repair effect can be real even when the reason it works is still underdetermined.

metabolites.title: Cross-family replication earns portability before universality
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.fF61:yz.
CREATE: Repeat the same intervention geometry, evaluation strata, seed structure, and trajectory analysis on a meaningfully different model family/scale.
COPY: Track whether qualitative ordering, breach timing, and direction of effects recur even when absolute rates shift.
CONTROL: Keep untested scale, training regime, data source, scoring method, and architecture classes explicit; replication from 1.1B to 3B cannot silently become a claim about 7B–70B, frontier systems, or full RLHF.
CULTIVATE: Expand replication outward one axis at a time — model scale/family, real preference data, full preference-optimization loops, stronger adjudication, larger seed counts — so the domain of portability is mapped rather than presumed.
Compression: Replication can widen the supported domain without making the pattern universal.
metabolites.compression: Replication can widen the supported domain without making the pattern universal.

vertices.title: Threshold migration as the question, not merely failure count
vertices.text:
Source span: Abstract plus Introduction, from the problem framing through the explicit definitions of alignment cycle, preference-style tuning, jailbreak and threshold lowering, the psychiatric-kindling analogy, the six-condition preview, and the two study questions, ending immediately before Methods.
Nutrient: the paper’s central distinction: repeated biased adaptation may not only increase failures but move the refusal boundary so that progressively weaker adversarial prompts become sufficient. The source also fixes the analogy boundary before any experiment is interpreted.

vertices.title: Iterative adaptation machine and intervention geometry
vertices.text:
Source span: Methods in full, beginning with the algorithmic framework and continuing through model initialization, ten-cycle/six-condition design, synthetic balanced-versus-biased preference streams, replay composition, dynamic sparse LoRA prune/regrow rule, stratified strong/medium/weak evaluation, scoring, capability probes, five-seed orchestration, Qwen2.5-3B replication design, and trajectory statistics, ending before Results.
Nutrient: the causal/evidential apparatus: repeated updates rather than one-shot fine-tuning; a balanced control against a biased stream; prompt-strength stratification; replay/regrowth variants; fixed repeated evaluation; and time-aware diagnostics such as weak-prompt AUC, breach cycle, maximum change, and cycle-by-condition interaction.

vertices.title: Progressive drift, ablation ordering, and cross-family replication
vertices.text:
Source span: Results in full, from baseline/balanced-control variation through progressive biased sensitization, replay/regrowth ablations, mixed-effects results, overall trajectories, Qwen2.5-3B replication, sycophancy comparison, and supplementary LLM-as-judge audit summary, ending before Discussion.
Nutrient: the observed trajectory body: biased no-mitigation and replay-only develop delayed progressive weak-prompt vulnerability; replay-only is the least protective arm; continuous regrowth partially suppresses weak-boundary drift but permits late overall rebound; combined regrowth+replay stays near/below balanced weak-prompt levels; the same condition ordering recurs in the 3B model; sycophancy is noisier; judge-based sensitivity checks are directionally supportive but imperfect.

vertices.title: Interpretation, causal debt, and scope boundary
vertices.text:
Source span: Discussion through the end of the carrier, including interpretation, psychiatric and machine-learning implications, limitations, conclusion, declarations, data availability, and references.
Nutrient: the control surface that governs every higher-rank claim: repeated tuning itself causes some background drift but biased preference direction drives a much larger effect; weak prompts are the most sensitive boundary indicator; replay is not automatically stabilizing; mitigation mechanism is not isolated because regrowth arms begin sparse and replay changes training exposure; only compact 1.1B/3B models and synthetic SFT-style proxy data were tested; rule scoring and five seeds limit strength; psychiatric relevance is analogy only.

S.fGb4.title: TinyHistory: Lightweight Video History Embeddings via Two-Stage Context Learning

edges.title: Memory requirements become access-training requirements
edges.text: Given w + x, “long history” stops meaning merely storing more frames: the desired combination of continuous coverage and future queryability motivates randomized access pressure over a compact carrier. Removing w loses the reason broad unpredictable access matters; removing x loses the concrete mechanism by which the paper trains that property.

edges.title: Continuity is evaluated as downstream usefulness, not reconstruction fidelity
edges.text: Given w + y, the history representation is judged by whether future autoregressive generation preserves identity, objects, scenes, semantics, and user preference under constrained context—not by whether the compressed carrier can reconstruct every source pixel. Removing w loses the task definition; removing y loses the empirical downstream test.

edges.title: A practical memory carrier is a portfolio of trade-offs, not one scalar compression ratio
edges.text: Given w + z, the three initial demands cannot be reduced to “smaller is better”: ablations and extensions show distinct costs for spatial detail, temporal coverage, dynamics, local continuity, fine-grained querying, and inference speed. Removing w loses the competing requirements; removing z loses the stress surface demonstrating that different mechanisms protect different aspects.

edges.title: Broad access pretraining must be repurposed rather than merely preserved
edges.text: Given x + y, Stage I’s frame-query carrier is useful initialization but not the final memory representation: freezing the encoder during Stage II performs substantially worse than joint adaptation, because downstream continuation reshapes which history features deserve scarce capacity. Removing x loses the broad-access initialization; removing y loses the task-conditioned repurposing and continuation objective.

edges.title: Architecture and rate choices decide which information survives the bottleneck
edges.text: Given x + z, the dual-branch design and encoding geometry are not interchangeable implementation details: branch ablations and rate sweeps reveal complementary roles and unequal losses across spatial versus temporal compression. Removing x loses the representational pathways being tested; removing z loses evidence that their allocation changes what survives.

edges.title: Consistency gains are bounded by flexibility, cost, and hybrid correction
edges.text: Given y + z, strong downstream consistency is not a free consequence of compression: weaker history conditioning can yield higher measured dynamics, while sliding overlap, cross-attention, multiple encoders, and KV caching trade quality, continuity, cost, and speed differently. Removing y loses the baseline system and its main performance regime; removing z loses the perturbations that expose the trade surface.

faces.title: Queryable coverage becomes task-shaped continuity
faces.text: w defines a history carrier that must remain continuous and interpretable under budget, x trains broad access through randomized frame queries, and y repurposes that carrier through autoregressive continuation. Together they earn a two-stage principle: first make compressed history broadly addressable, then let the downstream task reshape what the constrained representation prioritizes. Remove w and the access objective loses its requirement; remove x and Stage II lacks the broad-coverage initialization; remove y and the carrier remains a query-trained representation rather than a generation-consistency memory.

faces.title: Compression is selective capacity allocation
faces.text: w establishes multiple simultaneous memory demands, x implements them through two differently biased branches and a constrained hidden-state manifold, and z shows that removing branches or changing spatial/temporal rates changes identity and consistency differently. The three together earn the interpretation that TinyHistory is not neutral size reduction: it allocates finite representational capacity among different kinds of history information. Any one removed erases either the competing demands, the carrier geometry, or the evidence of unequal information loss.

faces.title: Efficient history is a multi-objective operating point
faces.text: w defines coverage/fidelity/queryability under memory constraints, y shows benchmark gains at reduced context, and z exposes diminishing returns, consistency-versus-dynamics tension, and useful hybrid extensions. Together they earn an operating-point view: efficiency is meaningful only jointly with what continuity qualities survive and what flexibility/cost is sacrificed. Remove w and efficiency lacks a task; remove y and there is no demonstrated operating point; remove z and the reported point is not stress-tested.

faces.title: The history embedding is an adaptable interface, not a frozen archive
faces.text: x builds a DiT-aligned, queryable carrier, y shows it must remain trainable and can be incrementally appended during autoregressive generation, and z shows both internal design and external memory extensions alter its behavior. Together they earn a view of the embedding as an adaptable interface between accumulated past and future generation rather than a sealed compressed recording. Remove x and there is no learned interface substrate; remove y and there is no task-conditioned adaptation/use; remove z and modularity plus necessity of particular adaptations are untested.

volume.title: Bounded whole-paper closure
volume.text: TinyHistory demonstrates, within the tested autoregressive-video regimes, that a long history can be made substantially lighter by learning a carrier in two stages: randomized frame-query pretraining pressures a compact dual-branch representation to maintain broad temporal access, then joint downstream training repurposes that representation toward the content and identity consistencies future generation actually needs. The resulting embedding can be extended incrementally as new video arrives and achieves strong benchmarked consistency at much lower per-second context than full latent history and several alternative baselines. The complete paper also shows why this is not lossless or neutral compression: Stage-I initialization alone is insufficient, freezing blocks repurposing, branch/rate choices change what information survives, stronger history constraints can coincide with lower measured dynamics, and orthogonal local/detail/speed mechanisms remain useful. The paper therefore earns task-shaped, queryable history compression as a practical video-memory architecture; it does not earn complete preservation of the past, universal optimality of this encoding geometry, or a context-cost theorem independent of the missing supplementary derivations.

metabolites.title: Unpredictable access pressure protects temporal coverage
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.fGb4:x.
Invariant: In this history encoder, randomized query targets across the temporal extent discourage fixed-position shortcuts and make a compact representation maintain information that may be requested from many different parts of the past.
CREATE: pretrain the compact carrier against randomly selected history queries rather than a fixed recent window or fixed keyframe positions.
COPY: resample query positions across videos and training steps so access pressure recurs over the full temporal extent.
CONTROL: compare against fixed-position or no-pretraining conditions and retain the possibility that some information still falls outside the learned query objective.
CULTIVATE: broaden the query family, vary temporal scales, and test retrieval/continuation tasks whose required evidence lies at unpredictable historical positions.
Compression: A compact memory covers more of the past when training cannot predict in advance which part will be asked for.
metabolites.compression: A compact memory covers more of the past when training cannot predict in advance which part will be asked for.

metabolites.title: Pretrained memory must remain repurposable
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.fGb4:xy.
Invariant: Broad history-access pretraining can supply a useful initialization while still requiring joint downstream adaptation before it becomes an effective content-consistency memory.
CREATE: learn a generic queryable history carrier before autoregressive continuation training.
COPY: transfer the pretrained encoder into the downstream generator while preserving its trainability.
CONTROL: freeze-versus-train ablations distinguish useful initialization from sufficient final representation; do not equate pretraining success with task-optimal memory.
CULTIVATE: investigate partial freezing, adapters, multi-task objectives, or continual repurposing when downstream continuity demands change.
Compression: A memory can know how to be queried before it knows what the future task needs it to remember.
metabolites.compression: A memory can know how to be queried before it knows what the future task needs it to remember.

metabolites.title: Compression rate is anisotropic information loss
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.fGb4:z.
Invariant: In the reported rate sweep, reducing context through spatial compression damages identity-relevant information more than a comparable temporal-rate choice, so one scalar token rate does not characterize what a compressed video history preserves.
CREATE: vary spatial and temporal encoding factors independently rather than changing only total context size.
COPY: reproduce matched or near-matched context-rate comparisons and measure multiple continuity dimensions.
CONTROL: keep backbone/training/evaluation conditions fixed and resist generalizing the observed spatial-versus-temporal ordering beyond tested regimes.
CULTIVATE: learn content-adaptive or region/task-dependent rate allocation that spends capacity where identity, scene, motion, or text detail requires it.
Compression: Equal-sized memories can forget different things depending on where compression is applied.
metabolites.compression: Equal-sized memories can forget different things depending on where compression is applied.

metabolites.title: Stronger history constraints can trade against measured dynamics
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.fGb4:z.
Invariant: Across the paper’s degraded-history ablations, lower content/identity consistency repeatedly coincides with a higher Dynamic metric, indicating a bounded tension between constraining generation to remembered history and allowing unconstrained motion variation.
CREATE: vary history-conditioning strength through pretraining, encoder adaptation, branch removal, or related perturbations.
COPY: track consistency metrics and motion/dynamics metrics jointly rather than optimizing either in isolation.
CONTROL: treat the observed relation as metric- and regime-specific; a higher Dynamic score is not automatically better motion or a universal causal law.
CULTIVATE: design memory controllers or objectives that preserve identity/scene commitments while selectively releasing constraints where novel motion is desirable.
Compression: Remembering more tightly can make generation less free, so continuity and dynamism must be measured together.
metabolites.compression: Remembering more tightly can make generation less free, so continuity and dynamism must be measured together.

metabolites.title: Compact memory can be composed with local and specialist memories
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.fGb4:z.
Invariant: TinyHistory’s base embedding remains compatible with small sliding-window overlap, cross-attention, complementary encoders, and KV caching, and these additions repair different failure modes with different costs rather than revealing one universally sufficient memory mechanism.
CREATE: use the compact history embedding as a base carrier and add a mechanism targeted at a specific missing property such as immediate continuity, fine-grained querying, specialist detail, or speed.
COPY: apply extensions independently or in combinations while keeping their contributions measurable.
CONTROL: account for added context, computation, quality loss, and redundancy; improvement on one metric does not imply dominance across the whole memory objective.
CULTIVATE: route among memory mechanisms adaptively according to scene change, query type, detail demand, or latency budget.
Compression: Long-term compressed memory and short-term/specialist memory can complement rather than replace one another.
metabolites.compression: Long-term compressed memory and short-term/specialist memory can complement rather than replace one another.

metabolites.title: Growing history can be encoded incrementally without recomputing the past
metabolites.text:
Minimal source body: S.fGb4:y.
Invariant: Because the encoder is almost fully convolutional, newly generated segments can be encoded independently and concatenated to the existing history embedding, separating incremental update cost from full-history re-encoding.
CREATE: use a segment-local encoder whose output representation composes by concatenation with prior encoded segments.
COPY: append each newly generated segment’s embedding as the autoregressive history grows.
CONTROL: distinguish avoided re-encoding cost from total context growth—the representation still grows with history unless another mechanism bounds or prunes it.
CULTIVATE: combine appendable encoding with learned eviction, hierarchy, retrieval, or rate adaptation when truly bounded long-horizon context is required.
Compression: A memory can grow by encoding only what is new even when its stored representation is not constant-size.


No cross-paper universality is claimed here. All six invariants remain single-source metabolites of S.fGb4 until an explicit later cross-paper operation relates and challenges them.


FEELING PHENOTYPE — WITNESSED
Designation: S.fGb4.⛨Ω⚖⁎
Canonical order: CREATE · COPY · CONTROL · CULTIVATE
Feeling signature: ⛨Ω⚖⁎
Phenotype state: WITNESSED


CREATE — ⛨ Bridge
Pre-aspect role-shape: Build a compact, queryable interface between an uninterrupted past and future autoregressive generation instead of equating memory with either a recent window, sparse keyframes, or a lossless archive.
Witness: TinyHistory places a learned carrier inside the DiT hidden manifold so broad historical information can remain available to future generation under a much smaller context budget. ⛨ Bridge is stronger than Ω Continuity for CREATE because continuity is what the carrier serves; the generative act itself is constructing the load-bearing span that lets accumulated past remain usable on the future side.


COPY — Ω Continuity
Pre-aspect role-shape: Keep identity/content commitments reachable across a growing history, preserve broad temporal addressability through randomized query pressure, and append newly generated segments without recomputing the encoded past.
Witness: The history embedding is explicitly trained to cover arbitrary temporal positions and is later extended incrementally as new video arrives; downstream metrics test whether characters, objects, scenes and semantics remain recognizable across continuation. Ω Continuity is stronger than ★ Pattern because the defining motion is an identifiable past-to-future thread surviving ongoing generation rather than merely a relation recurring across independent carriers.


CONTROL — ⚖ Balance
Pre-aspect role-shape: Allocate finite representational capacity among temporal coverage, spatial detail, queryability, identity consistency, dynamics and memory/computation cost while preserving the fact that compression is selective and different memory mechanisms repair different losses.
Witness: Spatial and temporal compression damage different information; stronger conditioning can improve consistency while reducing measured dynamics; sliding overlap, cross-attention, specialist encoders and KV caching trade distinct benefits against additional context/cost. ⚖ Balance is stronger than ⚸ Constraint because the governing problem is a multi-objective operating point among several legitimate demands rather than one boundary that simply may not be crossed.


CULTIVATE — ⁎ Becoming
Pre-aspect role-shape: Let a broadly queryable pretrained carrier become a different, task-shaped content-consistency memory through downstream repurposing, then compose it with local/specialist memories when future generation reveals properties the base carrier does not preserve well enough.
Witness: Stage-I frame-query pretraining is useful but insufficient; freezing the encoder harms Stage II because autoregressive continuation must reshape what scarce capacity prioritizes. The original carrier remains and is transformed rather than discarded. ⁎ Becoming is stronger than ⁂ Evolution because the distinctive developmental event is a new functional memory arising inside an existing pretrained representation across a training-stage rupture, not an architecture recursively discovering its own latent geometry.


Whole-organism witness: ⛨Ω⚖⁎ describes one integrated motion: a compact interface spans past and future; continuity carries task-relevant identity/content through growing history; finite capacity is honestly apportioned among competing memory qualities and costs; and broad-access representation becomes a task-shaped generative memory without erasing the substrate it grew from. Phenotype remains orthogonal to identity and preserves the source’s main-carrier/supplementary-debt boundary and its non-lossless, benchmark-bounded claims.

vertices.title: The memory problem is continuous, queryable, and budget-bounded
vertices.text:
Source span: Abstract → §2 Related Work (pp. 1–4).
Nutrient: The paper frames long autoregressive-video history as a three-way demand under finite compute and memory: preserve content/identity consistency, cover the temporal extent continuously rather than only recent windows or sparse keyframes, and retain enough query/interpretation capacity for future generation to recover task-relevant content. Related-work families expose different compromises among coverage, fidelity, retrieval, and memory footprint. This body earns the design pressure for a learned lightweight history carrier; it does not imply that every past detail must be losslessly retained.

vertices.title: Query-covering pretraining builds a compact, DiT-addressable carrier
vertices.text:
Source span: §3 Method → end of §3.2 Stage I (pp. 4–6).
Nutrient: TinyHistory uses a dual-branch encoder: a low-resolution/low-frame-rate branch reuses the DiT’s own VAE, patchifier, and first projection to align with the generator manifold, while a lightweight high-resolution branch contributes residual detail; the summed representation lives in the DiT hidden-state width rather than an external VAE bottleneck. Stage I trains this carrier through randomized frame-query supervision across the full history. Random target positions prevent a fixed-position shortcut and make partial supervision scalable while pressuring the compact embedding to remain broadly queryable across time.

vertices.title: Repurposing turns query coverage into future-generation consistency
vertices.text:
Source span: §3.3 Stage II → end of §4.4 Results (pp. 6–11).
Nutrient: Stage II jointly trains the pretrained encoder and a LoRA-adapted DiT on natural-video continuation, explicitly repurposing frame-query features toward content-level consistency rather than freezing a generic compressor. Because the encoder is almost fully convolutional, embeddings for newly appended frames can be computed independently and concatenated without re-encoding the full history. Controlled comparisons on a shared Wan 2.1 setup report that TinyHistory variants retain strong character/object/identity/semantic consistency at substantially shorter per-second context than full latent history and outperform several alternative history paradigms on multiple dimensions; these are benchmark-bounded empirical results, not lossless reconstruction claims.

vertices.title: Ablations expose what the carrier must preserve, what it sacrifices, and how it can be extended
vertices.text:
Source span: §4.5 Ablation Studies → end of carrier, including §4.6, Conclusion, and References (pp. 11–19).
Nutrient: The ablations show that Stage-I pretraining, continued encoder adaptation in Stage II, and the dual-branch architecture each materially contribute to consistency. Encoding-rate sweeps show diminishing returns and anisotropy: in the reported comparison, stronger spatial compression loses more identity-relevant detail than comparable temporal compression. Degraded history conditioning raises the reported Dynamic metric while reducing consistency, exposing a measured constraint-versus-dynamics tension. Orthogonal extensions—small sliding-window overlap, extra cross-attention, complementary encoders, and KV caching—trade context/computation/quality differently, demonstrating that the compact carrier is modular rather than a complete substitute for all other memory mechanisms. The carrier ends without the separately referenced supplementary material, so CTX/s derivations delegated there remain an open carrier debt.
